clauses.statement: Missing profile bindings, corpus state, strict execution guards or a supported outbox raises `StorageCapabilityMissing` before execution admission; absent compiled adapters follow {{topology.package.capability-absent}}.

clauses.subject: corpus-unavailable
clauses.statement: If a storage preflight's corpus request fails as {{store.endpoint.unavailable}}, preflight raises `StorageCorpusUnavailable`, naming the bucket or object. The failure does not raise {{run.journal.storage-incomplete}}'s refusal.
clauses.why: because an unanswered bucket says nothing of whether a capability is absent, and a transient outage must not read as an unsupported profile

clauses.subject: storage-unsupported
clauses.statement: An unknown storage profile or an encrypted corpus paired with an unsealed execution adapter raises `StorageProfileUnsupported` before execution admission.
clauses.why: because an unrecognized durability claim cannot select a local fallback safely

clauses.subject: execution-schema
clauses.statement: An execution database whose schema differs from the executable's supported schema raises `ExecutionSchemaIncompatible` before execution admission; preflight creates no missing execution table.
clauses.why: because creating an empty replacement for a missing table erases the evidence of a partial restore

clauses.subject: execution-recovery
clauses.statement: Missing execution tables or a mismatched project recovery identity raise `ExecutionRecoveryMismatch`. Normal startup provisions no recovery identity. A corpus-only restore admits no paid or effectful work.

clauses.subject: execution-backup
clauses.statement: An execution backup contains owners, leases, cadence run history, journal rows, blobs, awakeables and export state from one quiesced PostgreSQL snapshot, together with the corpus object frontier, project recovery identity and executable schema.

clauses.subject: current-owner
clauses.statement: An execution checks its durable owner, admitted pins and active attempt immediately before effect dispatch and publication; a superseded attempt enters neither boundary, and a late stop still follows {{run.cancel.land-path-uncut}}.

clauses.subject: durable-dispatch
clauses.statement: PostgreSQL admission holds shared owner and unexpired lease locks through each bounded provider or destination callback, including item ancestors and entity fences; owner replacement, retirement and takeover serialize after admitted callbacks.

clauses.subject: guard-callback
clauses.statement: A guarded callback may update run metadata; mutating its admitted owner or lease refuses. Nested callbacks retain only scopes and leases their caller already admits. Local adapters expose cooperative checks without strict execution-guard capability.
clauses.why: because nested lock expansion and owner mutation can deadlock the admission that invokes them

clauses.subject: plan-pin
clauses.statement: A run resolves the plan reference it started against for its whole life.

clauses.subject: store-input
clauses.statement: A store-driven run reads its statement once, through the read face under the job's grant at its `as_of`, and records the resolved snapshot id per table and the ordered input rows as its first step.

clauses.subject: input-replay
clauses.statement: A resumed run iterates recorded input without re-reading the statement. Rows landed after the pinned `as_of`, or folded since, do not enter the input set.

clauses.subject: open-as-of
clauses.statement: A store-driven job declaring no `as_of` resolves it to the instant its execution opens, recorded in the input step, so every resume reads that instant.

clauses.subject: input-pin
clauses.statement: A store-driven run's plan reference hashes its body name, statement and declared `as_of`, so a resume under a changed one meets {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}} before any step replays.

clauses.subject: host-structure-pin
clauses.statement: A host-supplied structural identity joins the input plan and owner pins through {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}}; without one, the plan reference hashes body, statement and `as_of` alone, as {{run.journal.input-pin}} states.

clauses.subject: input-truncated
clauses.statement: An input statement whose response the face truncates at its row ceiling raises `RunInputTruncated` before any row runs.
clauses.why: because a silently shortened input set closes `success` as though every row ran

clauses.subject: row-step
clauses.statement: Each input row runs the registered body under a row key, its ordinal in the recorded input; every step the body records carries a label scoped to that key, and a paid call carries {{run.journal.idempotency-key}}.
clauses.why: because two rows sharing one label under one execution resolve to one recorded value

clauses.subject: row-concurrency
clauses.statement: A batch store-driven run holds at most `max_in_flight` rows inside the body at once; a failing row admits no further row, and the run closes after the rows in flight return.

clauses.subject: row-output
clauses.statement: A batch's emitted rows land after the last input row completes and before the owner retires, one run per declared output table through {{run.land.stage-order}}.
clauses.why: because a landing that fails then holds the owner, and its resume replays every paid call instead of paying again

clauses.subject: body-projection
clauses.statement: A registered body's closed effect labels, declared roots, types, transforms and normalization bind its owner before input or effect execution; a caller-supplied projection differing from that registration refuses.

clauses.subject: unwired-capability
clauses.statement: Requesting a capability absent from the running profile raises `CapabilityUnwired` at the first request, before any partial work.

clauses.subject: machine-state
clauses.statement: The host's own stores hold journal rows, execution owners and awakeables. The derived catalog holds none. A catalog rebuild changes none and reconstructs none from the file tree.

clauses.subject: opt-in
clauses.statement: A store-driven job defaults to batch execution; `isolated_items` explicitly declares logical and entity key columns, an entity namespace and a positive failed-attempt budget.
clauses.why: because independent completion changes aggregate failure and retry semantics

clauses.subject: identity
clauses.statement: An isolated item's logical identity derives from its declared key and namespace; its execution identity binds that identity, job, input row, policy and pinned plan, independently of input order.

clauses.subject: completion
clauses.statement: Each successful item lands independently and stores a durable completion receipt; a later fire under the same execution identity skips its body and landing.
scenarios: WHEN one input fails permanently among three isolated items, THEN both healthy items land and reordering a later fire repeats neither completed body.

clauses.subject: terminal-input
clauses.statement: An aggregate whose items all hold terminal receipts releases its pinned input owner, so later fires read fresh input while retaining each item's completion or terminal failure.

clauses.subject: outcomes
clauses.statement: Individual outcomes distinguish success, failure, parked, deferred and waiting; the aggregate succeeds only when every required item succeeds.

clauses.subject: retry-budget
clauses.statement: Failed attempts consume the declared item budget across fires; permanent failures terminate immediately, parked entries consume no failed attempt, and terminal failure receipts prevent further body entry.

clauses.subject: replay
clauses.statement: A nonterminal failed or parked item retains its execution owner and recorded paid calls; its next admitted attempt reuses that journal.

clauses.subject: entity-admission
clauses.statement: Admission holds one leased entity namespace and key across triggers, job names and execution versions; unrelated entities occupy at most the job's `max_in_flight` body slots.
scenarios: WHEN three store-driven jobs declare one entity namespace and key column and two fire in one window, THEN at most one item per key enters a body and the later job's item reports deferred.
WHEN two jobs target one entity under different plans, THEN one enters its body and the other reports deferred while unrelated entities proceed.

clauses.subject: overlap
clauses.statement: An active entity lease returns a deferred item outcome through the scheduler's failed fire report; its next scheduled fire rechecks admission.

clauses.subject: fence
clauses.statement: Recorded effects and output publication check their execution owner and entity fence immediately before dispatch; a superseded owner sends no provider request and publishes no output.
clauses.why: because an owner that resumes after transfer cannot authorize another effect
scenarios: WHEN a newer owner takes an entity's lease while an earlier job's item resumes, THEN that resume sends no delegate request and publishes nothing.
WHEN an entity lease transfers before a paid call, THEN the earlier attempt invokes no provider.

clauses.subject: delegated-item
clauses.statement: Under a delegated body, each call ordinal is one request under {{surface.delegate.envelope}}, its `ok`, `defer` or `permanent` answer recorded under the item's entry key, so a resume replays every recorded answer and sends only the unrecorded call.

clauses.subject: outcome-record
clauses.statement: Each terminal item appends one row to the reserved `_items` table once its receipt commits: job, logical key, entity namespace and key, attempt count, terminal outcome, reason, attempt run id, execution id and end instant.
scenarios: WHEN one of three items fails transiently under a one-attempt budget, THEN `_items` holds two `succeeded` rows and one `exhausted` row naming the job and entity key, and a later fire adds none.

clauses.subject: terminal-outcome
clauses.statement: An item row's outcome is `succeeded`, `failed` for a failure no retry changes, or `exhausted` for a retryable failure on the attempt spending {{run.items.retry-budget}}; its reason carries the failure tag and {{run.record.error-cap}} message.

clauses.subject: waiting-item
clauses.statement: Under `isolated_items`, every retry wait closes its item {{run.retry.waiting-state}} and frees its slot; once the pass ends, an item whose instant falls within {{run.retry.retry-after}}'s ceiling re-enters in the same fire.
clauses.why: because one throttled item sleeping in a slot delays every sibling queued behind it

clauses.subject: served-key
clauses.statement: An item row carries its logical and entity keys as the job's input relation served them, so a key its source masks or classes lands under that rule, never in the clear.
scenarios: WHEN the input table hashes the entity key column, THEN every `_items` row carries the 32-char digest and no clear key.

clauses.subject: cursor-kind
clauses.statement: A cursor declares `monotonic` for a timestamp, autoincrement or watermark, `opaque-token` for a vendor continuation token, or `snapshot-id` for a log sequence number or version id. An undeclared kind resolves to `opaque-token`.

clauses.subject: concurrency-by-kind
clauses.statement: A `monotonic` position is concurrent-safe and commits the highest value observed. An `opaque-token` or `snapshot-id` position moves only under a single-writer lease. Last-write-wins governs no cursor.
clauses.why: because two writers resolving one continuation token by recency skip or duplicate records with no count showing it

clauses.subject: engine-owned
clauses.statement: A connector moves its position only by committing through the engine; that commit is a recorded step and replays as a resolved read.

clauses.subject: commit-with-rows
clauses.statement: A table's run commit marker, {{store.lay-out.run-manifest}}, publishes its rows and new position together. The catalog cursor caches the newest committed marker.
clauses.why: because rows and position committed in two stores leave a crash window that re-lands a batch

clauses.subject: cursor-bytes
clauses.statement: A position is opaque bytes the connector owns, and its kind is a manifest fact the engine reads. Each table carries its own position.

clauses.subject: inclusive-boundary
clauses.statement: A polled load admits a row whose clock value is at or after the stored position, re-landing the boundary instant's rows on every poll.
clauses.why: because a clock coarser than the row grain otherwise drops a sibling sharing the boundary value, permanently and invisibly

clauses.subject: declared-key-required
clauses.statement: The boundary re-land is idempotent on a table declaring a key; on a keyless table the repeats accumulate in its union view.

clauses.subject: watermark-shape
clauses.statement: A watermark position serializes as `{"field": "<name>", "at": <value>}`. `field` names the column whose values determine the watermark.

clauses.subject: field-rename
clauses.statement: Opening a position whose stored field differs from the declared `incremental` field raises `CursorFieldMismatch` before any request leaves the host.

clauses.subject: frontier
clauses.statement: The frontier counts every fetched row, landed or not. A committed position advances or stays unchanged. An empty or older window does not rewind the position.

clauses.subject: walk-position
clauses.statement: Under a `monotonic` cursor, a pull reporting more and carrying a position other than the one it asked continues its walk: the next pull asks that position and admits rows from the walk's floor, and the run commits the frontier.
scenarios: WHEN a `monotonic` walk's pull returns no rows, the position it asked and more, THEN the run ends and commits its frontier.

clauses.subject: unorderable-position
clauses.statement: A row with no orderable value in the clock field, or a stream switching between text and numeric positions mid-pass, raises `CursorPositionUnorderable`, terminal for the pull.

clauses.subject: allowed-lateness
clauses.statement: A table declares `allowed_lateness`, default 0 s; a `monotonic` poll re-reads from its stored position minus that window, so a row arriving that late still lands.
clauses.why: because lateness belongs to the source feeding a table, and a position records only where the frontier stands

clauses.subject: turning-incremental-on
clauses.statement: Enabling `incremental` on a pipeline that holds a position starts from none, re-landing the source's current window once.

clauses.subject: skip-unchanged
clauses.statement: A snapshot-shaped source with `skip_unchanged = true` records its input's raw-byte digest as `{ sha256, rows }`; a matching digest returns zero batches, holds the position and closes a zero-row success. Undeclared, it is false.

clauses.subject: snapshot-completion
clauses.statement: A snapshot source reports complete inventory or unchanged skip independently of row count; a replacing run carries only complete inventory into its manifest.

clauses.subject: zero-row-commit
clauses.statement: A complete empty snapshot of a replacing table commits {{store.declare.empty-replacement}}; a skipped unchanged input holds the frontier and position, and a failed pull publishes neither.
scenarios: WHEN a complete snapshot holds zero rows after a non-empty replacing run, THEN the current read is empty and a bounded read before the commit retains the older rows.
WHEN the source skips unchanged input, THEN the current read and cursor retain their prior values.
WHEN a pull fails before completion, THEN no replacement marker becomes readable.

clauses.subject: awakeable
clauses.statement: An awakeable suspends a run durably: the engine mints an opaque single-use token and persists a `pending` row through the awakeable store; an external party resumes by posting the token back.

clauses.subject: resume-is-a-step-output
clauses.statement: The journal records a resume payload as the awaited step's output under key `sha256("awakeable:" + token)`. A run that resumes and then crashes reads the payload back without suspending again.

clauses.subject: deadline
clauses.statement: A deadline is the creation instant plus a time-to-live, both caller-supplied RFC3339 Zulu strings; the core reads no wall clock.

clauses.subject: timeout-is-sticky
clauses.statement: The engine evaluates expiry against an injected instant. A suspension past its deadline becomes `timed_out` and keeps that state under any later instant.

clauses.subject: idempotent-resolution
clauses.statement: Resolving a token again with the identical payload returns the recorded value.

clauses.subject: conflicting-resolution
clauses.statement: A second resolution with a different payload raises `AwakeableAlreadyResolved` and leaves the recorded value untouched.

clauses.subject: expired-token
clauses.statement: Resolving a token past its deadline raises `AwakeableTimedOut`.

clauses.subject: unknown-token
clauses.statement: A token with no row raises `AwakeableUnknown` and allocates no state.

clauses.subject: resume-route
clauses.statement: `POST /awake/:token` on the served face answers `200` with the recorded payload, `404` for {{run.suspend.unknown-token}}, `409` for {{run.suspend.conflicting-resolution}} and `410` for {{run.suspend.expired-token}}. `GET /awake/:token` reports state without resuming.

clauses.subject: resume-authenticates
clauses.statement: The resume route admits the request's credential before reading the registry, answering `401` without one, and passes the credential's verified `on_behalf_of` as the caller subject.

clauses.subject: caller-binding
clauses.statement: An awakeable may bind a verified caller subject at mint; resolving it then takes the token and a credential for that subject, and any other caller answers as {{run.suspend.unknown-token}}. An unbound token is its whole authority.
clauses.why: because a token leaked through a log otherwise resumes a run, and answering unknown discloses nothing to the wrong holder

clauses.subject: payload-offload
clauses.statement: A payload above {{run.journal.inline-cutoff}} lands in the journal's blob store, and the pending row references it.

clauses.subject: postgres-reconciliation
clauses.statement: A PostgreSQL callback row interrupted after its resume value commits recovers its resolved payload from that journal value; a conflicting resolution follows {{run.suspend.conflicting-resolution}}.
clauses.why: because a separately committed callback row cannot overwrite the journal value that already determines replay

clauses.subject: survives-restart
clauses.statement: A durable awakeable store persists every registry row, so a process reopening it over the same location drops no pending callback; an in-process store ends with its process.

clauses.subject: row-parks
clauses.statement: A store-driven row awaiting an unresolved awakeable parks and frees its slot; the other rows run on, and the parked row re-enters its body once the awakeable resolves or its deadline passes.

clauses.subject: recorded-timeout
clauses.statement: A row's wait past its deadline records a timeout value as that wait's step output, so every re-entry of the body reads the identical value.
clauses.why: because a body branching on the clock rather than on a recorded value replays differently after a crash

clauses.subject: failure-taxonomy
clauses.statement: One tagged failure type crosses every port: `Transient`, `Permanent`, `SchemaIncompatible`, `AuthExpired`, `RateLimited`, `Config`, `Storage`, `UnknownConnector`, `SecretNotFound` and `Canceled`. A caller branches on the tag, never on a message.

clauses.subject: schedule
clauses.statement: A schedule attaches to a step and carries a fixed or exponential backoff with base and factor, a total attempt count including the first, a per-delay clamp, a jitter ceiling and `retry_on`.

clauses.subject: default-policy
clauses.statement: The default schedule is exponential from a 100 ms base with factor 2, to 5 attempts in total, each delay clamped at 30 s, plus seeded jitter below 250 ms.
clauses.why: because zero jitter synchronizes every run that hit one shared throttle

clauses.subject: single-attempt
clauses.statement: A schedule of 1 attempts is the no-retry schedule.

clauses.subject: retryable-classes
clauses.statement: `Transient` and `RateLimited` retry; every other tag stands as the step's answer whatever budget remains. `retry_on` narrows that pair.

clauses.subject: unretryable-tag
clauses.statement: A `retry_on` naming any tag outside `Transient` and `RateLimited` raises `RunRetryTagUnretryable` at plan compile.

clauses.subject: step-failed
clauses.statement: A non-retryable failure, or a step exhausting its schedule, raises `StepFailed` carrying the step label and the underlying tag.

clauses.subject: deterministic-verdict
clauses.statement: A refusal whose check is pure over static input is terminal and consumes no attempt budget.

clauses.subject: retry-after
clauses.statement: A server-supplied `Retry-After` supersedes the computed delay; a remaining wait up to 300 s sleeps in process, and a longer one closes the attempt `RateLimited` under {{run.retry.waiting-state}} instead of sleeping.
clauses.why: because an unclamped upstream delay holds a run slot for as long as the vendor asks

clauses.subject: not-before
clauses.statement: Before any wait, a retrying step records its next-attempt instant beside its attempt count in the execution's journal, so a restart, a container replacement included, reads both back.
clauses.why: because a wait held only in memory restarts on every replacement and calls the vendor early

clauses.subject: waiting-state
clauses.statement: An attempt closed on its next-attempt instant reports `waiting` with that instant on its run row, counts as neither refused nor failed, and keeps its owner; only exhausting the schedule's attempts fails the step.
clauses.why: because a vendor's requested pause is not evidence the work is wrong

clauses.subject: resume-at
clauses.statement: An attempt reaching a step whose stored instant has not passed waits again without invoking the effect; the first attempt at or after it re-enters under the same work key, pins and attempt count.
clauses.why: because resuming under another key or a fresh budget repeats paid work or retries without bound

clauses.subject: crash-resumes-wait
clauses.statement: An attempt resuming a step whose process died mid-sleep sleeps out only the remaining wait to the stored instant.
clauses.why: because restarting the wait over-delays and skipping it calls the vendor early

clauses.subject: wake
clauses.statement: A waiting attempt records its instant on its owner; the scheduler fires that owner's unit at the first beat at or after it, ahead of the unit's regular `schedule` fire, and the next attempt's claim clears it.
clauses.why: because a resume gated on the regular cadence adds up to a full interval to every rate-limited wait

clauses.subject: shared-path
clauses.statement: An HTTP `Retry-After`, a throttled lease mint and a limiter denial each reach the step as a `RateLimited` failure carrying its wait, and each takes {{run.retry.not-before}}.
clauses.why: because two retry owners for one throttle disagree on when to call again

clauses.subject: no-double-spend
clauses.statement: A resumed attempt replays every recorded step, so it reserves no meter permit and issues no call an earlier attempt already recorded.
clauses.why: because each resume reserving afresh spends a budget once per wait

clauses.subject: one-layer
clauses.statement: The step's schedule is the only retry layer: an adapter, a credential mint and a meter acquire inside a step return their failure to it.
clauses.why: because nested retry layers multiply attempts and amplify a vendor outage

clauses.subject: decision-is-pure
clauses.statement: The retry decision is a pure function of the completed one-based attempt and classified failure. Jitter derives from an injected seed. The runner owns the sleep and attempt counter.

clauses.subject: partial-failure
clauses.statement: A run failing after it staged batches commits none of them under {{run.own.one-commit-per-run}} and closes `failed`, holding its owner so the journal keeps the resume point; only {{run.record.orphan-reap}} closes a run `partial_failure`.

clauses.subject: no-compensation
clauses.statement: The engine offers no compensation combinator; undoing a partial effect is an author-written recorded step, replayed like any other.
clauses.why: because compensation depends on each vendor's undo semantics, which the engine cannot know

clauses.subject: attempt-counter
clauses.statement: An in-flight schedule's attempt counter persists on its step's journal row, so a crash mid-backoff resumes the remaining budget instead of restarting it.
clauses.why: because a budget restarting at each crash retries a failing vendor without bound

clauses.subject: pressure-is-local
clauses.statement: Rate-limit pressure against one source paces only that source's runs.

clauses.subject: bound-hit-is-transient
clauses.statement: A connector striking {{connector.package.linear-memory}} or {{connector.package.call-deadline}} fails the attempt `Transient`, the failure naming the bound it struck.

clauses.subject: bound-hit-recorded
clauses.statement: The run record lists every bound hit with its step label, attempt and bound, a hit a later attempt recovered from included.

clauses.subject: execution-owner
clauses.statement: One durable execution owner exists per scope; a table or chunk owner holds the connector identity with its component world, the pipeline `content_hash` and the input hash.

clauses.subject: host-scope
clauses.statement: The catalog keys every owner on its scope — live table, backfill chunk or host-declared id — a table owner keeping its stored key byte for byte, and a host owner pinning the plan reference and identities the host supplies.

clauses.subject: body-implementation
clauses.statement: Store-driven owner pins include the host-verified digest of its executing binary and concrete registered body type; configuration selects a body name and supplies no implementation identity.

clauses.subject: body-dependencies
clauses.statement: Registration declares prompt/template, public provider/model configuration and policy identities affecting execution; owner pins carry their digests independently of structural input and output declarations.

clauses.subject: body-admission
clauses.statement: Body implementation and dependency pins bind before input reads, recorded-call replay or body entry; unavailable or changed pins follow {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}}.

clauses.subject: body-compatibility
clauses.statement: Registrations without dependency declarations declare none and receive the verified host implementation pin; pending owners without implementation pins refuse before input reads or body entry under {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}}.
clauses.why: because an unversioned record cannot establish which executable produced its paid calls

clauses.subject: body-fresh
clauses.statement: A fresh execution under changed implementation or dependencies receives a distinct plan identity and preserves earlier run records; pending work requires its recorded host build and registered dependencies.

clauses.subject: body-public-configuration
clauses.statement: Semantic provider configuration contains public endpoint, model and generation parameters; credential-bearing endpoints refuse registration, credentials enter neither exported diagnostics nor recorded pins, and credential rotation alone changes no semantic identity.
clauses.why: because credential custody and executable semantics are independent identities

clauses.subject: execution-id-keys-the-journal
clauses.statement: Recorded work keys on the execution id; a catalog run id is the provenance of one attempt, so attempts under one owner resolve the same recorded values.

clauses.subject: retirement
clauses.statement: Retiring an owner and caching its committed position share one catalog transaction; a later fire receives a fresh execution id even at a byte-identical position. A completed backfill chunk retires the same way.

clauses.subject: marker-reconciles
clauses.statement: At run open, a commit marker newer than the catalog's cached position retires the pending owner that produced it before any replay.
clauses.why: because a crash between marker and catalog otherwise replays a recorded pull into rows already committed

clauses.subject: pinned-plan-changed
clauses.statement: While an owner is pending, a changed pin — connector identity, component world, pipeline `content_hash`, or a host's plan reference or identities — raises `ExecutionPinMismatch` before replay, terminal and non-retryable, naming the scope and both pin sets.
scenarios: WHEN a host scope's pending owner pins plan reference `plan-a` and an open asks for `plan-b`, THEN the open refuses with `ExecutionPinMismatch` and its run row closes `failed`.

clauses.subject: pin-recovery
clauses.statement: Restoring the recorded build and resuming to completion clears a pending owner; {{run.own.rewind}} retires a host or table owner, and an explicit chunk rewind retires the owners its window covers.

clauses.subject: pin-mismatch-recovery
clauses.statement: The {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}} refusal names restoring the recorded build or plan and, under a host or table scope, {{run.own.rewind}} with the pending execution id; it names no recovery the command line lacks.
clauses.why: because an operator acts on the refusal's text, and a recovery no verb provides leaves the scope refusing every fire

clauses.subject: rewind
clauses.statement: `contextful run rewind <execution-id> --reason <text>` retires the pending host or table owner holding that execution and leaves the scope's committed position alone, so the scope's next fire claims a fresh execution.
scenarios: WHEN job `score`'s pending owner pins `plan-a`, a fire asking `plan-b` refuses, and an operator rewinds that execution, THEN the next fire claims a fresh execution under `plan-b` and completes.

clauses.subject: rewind-record
clauses.statement: A retirement under {{run.own.rewind}} or {{run.own.apply-retires-superseded}} writes one `canceled` run row under the scope carrying the retired execution id, its pinned plan reference and the reason, started at the owner's open.
clauses.why: because a row started at the retirement reads as the job's latest start and postpones its next due fire

clauses.subject: rewind-not-pending
clauses.statement: A rewind naming an execution no pending host or table owner holds raises `ExecutionRewindNotPending`.
clauses.why: because a completed or retired execution holds nothing to release, and a chunk owner retires through its window's rewind

clauses.subject: rewind-plan-current
clauses.statement: If no attempt or refused open requested another plan reference, rewinding the owner raises `ExecutionRewindPlanCurrent`. The operator may override this refusal with `--force`.
clauses.why: because such an owner resumes on its next fire, and retiring it discards its recorded work

clauses.subject: rewind-unsafe
clauses.statement: Retiring an owner with an attempt on an unexpired {{run.record.owner-lease}}, a `waiting` attempt, or an awakeable pending before its deadline raises `ExecutionRewindUnsafe` naming it; `--force` overrides none.

clauses.subject: apply-retires-superseded
clauses.statement: A claimed `pipeline apply` retires a build or sweepless store-driven job's pending owner when the applied snapshot produces no matching declared plan reference: a verified body's `input` identity, otherwise its plan reference.
scenarios: WHEN applied v2 changes the model a build job targets while its pending owner pins v1's plan reference, THEN the apply retires that owner and the job's next fire completes.

clauses.subject: apply-retire-refused
clauses.statement: An applied retirement meeting {{run.own.rewind-unsafe}} leaves the owner pending and the snapshot claimed, and the apply names the execution and {{run.own.rewind}} on standard error.

clauses.subject: scope-independence
clauses.statement: A finishing table releases nothing another table's unfinished execution holds, and a seeding scope carries its own source identity.

clauses.subject: unclosed-execution
clauses.statement: An execution handle dropped without close records no status; its owner stays pending, and the next open under its scope resumes it once {{run.record.owner-lease}} lapses.
scenarios: WHEN a host execution records two steps and its process dies mid-third, THEN the next open under its scope after the lease lapses replays both steps without running their effects.

clauses.subject: live-owner
clauses.statement: An open under a host scope whose pending owner has an attempt on an unexpired {{run.record.owner-lease}} fails `Transient` naming that attempt, and its run row closes `failed` without joining the owner.
clauses.why: because two live handles on one owner share its journal, and either one retiring it strands the other
scenarios: WHEN attempt `job-a` holds host scope `index-42` open and `job-b` opens under it, THEN `job-b` fails `Transient` naming `job-a`, and `job-a` alone holds the owner.

clauses.subject: pin-release
clauses.statement: `success`, a failure that wrote no batch, and replay-stable failures under {{run.own.staged-bytes}}, {{run.land.late-type}}, or {{run.own.source-stage-schema}} release the owner; every other status holds it.

clauses.subject: admission-pin
clauses.statement: A run pins its connector identity at admission and a replay resolves the artifact from that pin; a connector rebuilt later reaches no in-flight or replayed run.

clauses.subject: backpressure
clauses.statement: The runner stages each shaped batch through the destination as one part before its next pull, so a run holds one pulled batch in memory; the commit names the staged parts.
clauses.why: because holding every batch until the commit sizes a run's memory by the sum of its pulls
scenarios: WHEN a source serves three pages, THEN the destination stages part 0 after the first pull, part 1 after the second and part 2 after the third, and one commit names all three.

clauses.subject: one-commit-per-run
clauses.statement: One run produces one atomic commit per table, plus one per {{run.own.checkpoint-commit}}; a crash mid-run leaves parts under that run's own directory, and a resumption continues from the last recorded step or commit.

clauses.subject: staged-bytes
clauses.statement: A stage carrying the parts a run staged since its last commit past 1 GiB raises `RunStagedBytesExceeded`, deterministic; the run commits nothing more and retires its owner, so the next fire pulls afresh from the stored cursor.
clauses.why: because a replay of the run's recorded pulls stages the same bytes past the bound and fails identically, holding the table's owner indefinitely
scenarios: WHEN each of three pulls of a replacing table stages a 400 MiB part, THEN the third stage fails the run `Permanent` with `RunStagedBytesExceeded`, the cursor stays where it stood, and the next fire pulls all three pages under a fresh execution.

clauses.subject: checkpoint-commit
clauses.statement: When the parts a run of a position-addressed source staged since its last commit reach 512 MiB, the run commits them with the position after its last staged pull before staging more rows, then keeps pulling under the same execution.
scenarios: WHEN each of sixteen pulls stages a 128 MiB part, THEN one fire commits four times, four parts each, carrying the positions `p4`, `p8`, `p12` and `p16`.

clauses.subject: checkpoint-frontier
clauses.statement: Under a `monotonic` cursor, a checkpoint commits only before a pull whose every clock passes the run's frontier, so no commit's position splits the rows of one instant.
scenarios: WHEN five pages of clocks `1 1`, `1`, `2`, `2` and `3` each stage a 512 MiB part, THEN the run commits at positions 1, 2 and 3, and no instant's rows span two commits.

clauses.subject: checkpoint-resume
clauses.statement: A checkpoint caches its position and marker in the catalog cursor while the owner stays pending, and collects the journal's recorded pulls, so a resumption pulls afresh from that position.
scenarios: WHEN a run commits checkpoints at `p4` and `p8` and dies pulling `p9`, THEN the next fire pulls from `p8` and lands every later row once.

clauses.subject: checkpoint-run-id
clauses.statement: A run's first commit lands under its run id and each later one under `<run id>.<n>`, `n` its zero-padded six-digit ordinal, so every commit names its own parts.
clauses.why: because the store holds one manifest per run id, and a later commit naming an earlier one's directory finds it committed

clauses.subject: checkpoint-id-length
clauses.statement: A checkpoint whose next `<run id>.<n>` passes {{store.lay-out.run-id-shape}} raises `RunCheckpointIdTooLong` before it commits; the run commits nothing and retires its owner.
clauses.why: because a run committing its first checkpoint and then failing on the next one's run id leaves a partial window published
scenarios: WHEN a run id of 122 chars stages sixteen 128 MiB parts, THEN the run fails with `RunCheckpointIdTooLong` and commits nothing.

clauses.subject: checkpoint-landed
clauses.statement: A run failing after a checkpoint's commit lands records on its row the rows and bytes every landed checkpoint commit carried, including one whose cursor update then fails.
clauses.why: because the checkpoints stay committed, and a failed row counting no rows hides rows every read returns
scenarios: WHEN a run commits checkpoints at `p4` and `p8` and its tenth pull fails, THEN its `failed` row counts eight rows.
WHEN a run's `p12` checkpoint commits and the cursor row moves before its update, THEN its `failed` row counts twelve rows.

clauses.subject: checkpoint-scope
clauses.statement: A source is position-addressed when each pull's position names a watermark, page token or stable offset. A {{connector.source.http-url-walk}}, a replacing table, a body's prepared landing, and a seeding or receiving scope commit once.
scenarios: WHEN an appending table's next-URL walk dies on its third page and the listing gains a first row, THEN the next fire lands each listed row once.
WHEN a replacing table's next-URL walk dies mid-walk on three fires, THEN the fourth fire succeeds with every listed row and no fire succeeds with zero.

clauses.subject: stage-schema
clauses.statement: A stage refuses against `schema.json` and the run's earlier stages, then merges its columns into the run's own staged schema; only the commit merges them into `schema.json`.
clauses.why: because otherwise rows no commit publishes fix a column's type in the table's schema
scenarios: WHEN run `run-s` stages `ts` as text and fails, THEN a later run lands `ts` as a timestamp, and `run-s`'s commit refuses with `StoreSchemaIncompatible`.

clauses.subject: source-stage-schema
clauses.statement: A deterministic `SchemaIncompatible` from staging an ordinary source batch, raw or prepared, retires its owner unless another live attempt holds it; the failed run changes neither committed cursor nor published rows. This exception excludes prepared body-emission staging.
clauses.why: because a recorded source batch that fails the same schema check on replay prevents a repaired source from being fetched

clauses.subject: stage-commit-seq
clauses.statement: A staged part carries no `_commit_seq`; the commit assigns it under {{store.reserve.commit-order}} and writes it into each part it names, so a run committing between a stage and that commit takes the lower value.
clauses.why: because a value fixed at the stage orders a run by its first pull, and the readable runs then hold no prefix of the sequence
scenarios: WHEN run `run-s` stages a part, run `run-c` then commits as `_commit_seq` 1, and `run-s` commits after it, THEN every row of `run-s` reads `_commit_seq` 2.

clauses.subject: stage-instant
clauses.statement: A staged part carries no `_ingested_at`; the commit writes its commit instant into each part it names, so every row of a run carries the instant its marker carries.
clauses.why: because a stage-time instant ranks a run by its first pull, so under {{store.declare.dedup-view}} an earlier committer outranks a later one on a shared key
scenarios: WHEN run `run-a` stages key `k` at 00:01, run `run-b` commits `k` at 00:03 and `run-a` commits at 00:05, THEN the keyed read returns `run-a`'s row, `_ingested_at` 00:05.

clauses.subject: stage-discard
clauses.statement: A run that fails removes every part it staged, and a commit failing before its manifest exists removes the parts it copied; a run's crash leaves its staged parts.
clauses.why: because a run id names one attempt, so no later commit names a failed run's staged parts
scenarios: WHEN a run stages its first page and its second pull fails, THEN its run directory holds no staged part.

clauses.subject: body-parent
clauses.statement: Prepared body outputs require the unchanged parent execution and current in-flight, unstopped attempt at admission, staging and commit; a stopped parent reaches {{run.cancel.abandoned-work}} independently of the output table's stop policy.

clauses.subject: catalog-channel
clauses.statement: The catalog stores each stop request on the run row: requested-at instant, scope and optional reason. The catalog is the only stop-request channel.

clauses.subject: two-grains
clauses.statement: A `run`-scoped stop halts one run and the fire continues; a `pipeline`-scoped stop halts every in-flight run of the pipeline and every table or chunk the fire had left. An unrecognized stored scope reads as `run`.

clauses.subject: host-grain
clauses.statement: A `pipeline`-scoped stop on a host execution's run halts every in-flight run under the same host-declared scope and no run of another scope.

clauses.subject: one-token
clauses.statement: Each run holds one cancellation token that every await selects on: the pull, a retry sleep, an awakeable wait and a subprocess wait. A meter reservation holds no wait of its own, under {{connector.meter.acquire-call}}.
clauses.why: because a stop observed only at the pull leaves sleeps and child processes running after the record reads canceled

clauses.subject: poll-interval
clauses.statement: The engine updates the token from one catalog read before the run's first await, then every 500 ms. Each await evaluates cancellation before work.

clauses.subject: engine-keeper
clauses.statement: One keeper per engine renews every registered execution's owner lease and feeds its token, sleeping until the earliest deadline; opening an execution registers it, and close or drop deregisters it.
scenarios: WHEN 20 executions are open on one engine, THEN one keeper thread renews all 20 owner leases, and it exits once the last one closes or drops.

clauses.subject: keeper-panic
clauses.statement: A keeper job that panics warns and leaves the keeper running: every other registration keeps its cadence, the panicking one retries at its next deadline, and dropping it returns.
clauses.why: because the keeper is shared, so one adapter's panic that ended its thread lapses every open execution's lease under a live run

clauses.subject: land-path-uncut
clauses.statement: A table run's own stop does not interrupt landing. The engine finishes landing bytes already received and records the unfulfilled stop. Prepared body outputs additionally require {{run.own.body-parent}}.

clauses.subject: abandoned-work
clauses.statement: Abandoned work surfaces as the `Canceled` tag through the ordinary failure path, which settles the request ledger, closes the record and leaves the position alone.

clauses.subject: child-reaped
clauses.statement: A stop signals a running subprocess chain's process group. The engine records `canceled` only after reaping the group.
clauses.why: because a record reading canceled while a child still runs misstates what the machine is doing

clauses.subject: storage-blip
clauses.statement: A failed poll read warns and keeps polling.

clauses.subject: not-in-flight
clauses.statement: Only a `pending`, `running` or `waiting` row accepts a mark; a stop matching none raises `CancelTargetNotInFlight`, answering `409` over HTTP and exiting non-zero at the terminal.

clauses.subject: re-mark
clauses.statement: Marking an already-marked row overwrites it with the newer request.

clauses.subject: distinct-terminal-status
clauses.statement: `canceled` is a terminal status apart from `failed`, and upstream health observations skip it.

clauses.subject: resumable-remains
clauses.statement: A stopped run's recorded pull keeps its owner and replays next attempt; a stopped pull that recorded nothing releases it. A stopped chunk returns to pending, its attempt count unchanged. A stop advances no position.

clauses.subject: authority-from-the-record
clauses.statement: A stop authorizes against the pipeline read off the run record, never off the request.

clauses.subject: stop-unauthorized
clauses.statement: A credentialed stop needs an `execute` grant covering the pipeline read off the run record; an uncovered or unrecorded run raises `CancelUnauthorized` without naming the pipeline, answering `403` over HTTP.
clauses.why: because a stop halts work `execute` fires, and a refusal naming the pipeline discloses it to a credential that cannot read it

clauses.subject: stop-route
clauses.statement: `POST /runs/:run_id/stop` writes a stop under a per-request network credential, its optional JSON body carrying `scope` and `reason`, and answers `200` with the marked run ids.

clauses.subject: reserved-table
clauses.statement: The durable run record is a reserved store table holding two append-only rows per run, one at plan and one at commit; the latest row per run and phase wins. The local catalog is a cache in front of it.

clauses.subject: columns
clauses.statement: A run row carries run id, pipeline id, site id, status, owner, start and end instants, row and byte counts, error kind and message, connector id, version and hash, trace id and phase.

clauses.subject: trace-context
clauses.statement: A run a command opens takes as trace id the trace of the caller's `traceparent`, read from `TRACEPARENT` and `TRACESTATE`, or a fresh trace; both run rows carry it.

clauses.subject: run-span
clauses.statement: With an exporter configured, a run exports one span, child of the caller's span, carrying run id, pipeline, table, status, row and byte counts, and the failure tag.

clauses.subject: status-set
clauses.statement: A run status is `pending`, `running`, `waiting`, `success`, `partial_failure`, `failed` or `canceled`, spelled identically on the record and the wire snapshot; every surface classifying a run covers all seven.
clauses.why: because two vocabularies for one lifecycle leave a suspended or partly failed run without a reading

clauses.subject: row-at-open
clauses.statement: The engine writes a run row at open, before the first pull. Readers distinguish zero-row `success`, `failed` with an error kind, and no run row.

clauses.subject: record-folds
clauses.statement: An append to {{run.record.reserved-table}} runs a pass on it once {{store.fold.triggers}} fires; a pass that fails leaves the row appended and the append succeeding, and the next append retries it.

clauses.subject: rebuild-restores-history
clauses.statement: A catalog rebuild restores run history from {{run.record.reserved-table}}, so a rebuilt catalog lists every run the store recorded instead of starting empty.
clauses.why: because the catalog is a cache, and a rebuild dropping history loses the only record of failed runs

clauses.subject: time-travel
clauses.statement: Run history inherits the store's transaction-time bound, so one as-of selector rewinds it with every other table.

clauses.subject: owner-lease
clauses.statement: A `running` or `waiting` row carries an owner of process id, boot id and a lease expiry, renewed every 10 s with a 30 s time-to-live.
clauses.why: because a second process sharing the catalog needs a liveness signal to tell a live run from an orphan

clauses.subject: orphan-reap
clauses.statement: Startup marks only non-terminal rows with expired owner leases as `partial_failure`. Startup leaves rows held by live processes unchanged.

clauses.subject: writing-site
clauses.statement: Every landed row carries its run's site id in the `_site_id` column {{store.reserve.injected}} writes, so a row names the site that wrote it.

clauses.subject: site-id-length
clauses.statement: A site id matches letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen, from 1 chars to 64 chars.
clauses.why: because it is interpolated into run directories and request-ledger filenames

clauses.subject: site-id-unresolved
clauses.statement: A site id comes from the manifest's `site_id`, or the variable its `site_id_env` names, and a run's `--site-id` or `--site-id-env` replaces that declaration; no declaration, both keys in one place, or an unset variable raises `SiteIdUnresolved` at startup.

clauses.subject: history-window
clauses.statement: History requests specify an inclusive start-instant lower bound and row ceiling, returning newest first. A SQL catalog applies the bound in `WHERE` over an indexed start column and the ceiling as `LIMIT`.
clauses.why: because filtering after the read scans every run a pipeline ever recorded, so a describe call grows with history rather than with its window

clauses.subject: describe-window
clauses.statement: The describe surface answers with 5 rows by default and clamps a caller's ceiling at 500 rows.

clauses.subject: bound-spelling
clauses.statement: A window lower bound is `YYYY-MM-DD` or a UTC RFC3339 instant ending `Z`; any other spelling raises `HistoryBoundSpelling` at every caller-facing surface.
clauses.why: because a bound read under a guessed zone silently moves the window

clauses.subject: truncation-flag
clauses.statement: A history response echoes its window and flags truncation when the pipeline recorded more runs inside it than the ceiling returned.

clauses.subject: empty-window
clauses.statement: An empty window answers `[]` and raises nothing.

clauses.subject: history-export
clauses.statement: History leaves the machine as a process listing and an NDJSON export over one run projection; the export's first line carries store, window, count and truncation flag, then one run per line. It resolves no bucket.

clauses.subject: export-ceiling
clauses.statement: The export returns 500 rows by default and clamps at 5000 rows. Each pipeline's window takes the full ceiling; the export clips the merged result once.

clauses.subject: error-cap
clauses.statement: The shared run projection masks credential-shaped spans in recorded errors and caps each error at 2 KiB with an ellipsis marker. Every surface serves that projection.

clauses.subject: failure-publishes
clauses.statement: The bucket push runs on the failure arm as on the success arm, for every failure past run open.

clauses.subject: per-table-accounting
clauses.statement: A table failing inside a multi-table fire leaves one row with its error kind, a step-failure and a run-failure event, and a position where the next run resumes, under either `on_table_error` setting.

clauses.subject: counts-at-destination
clauses.statement: The engine measures row and byte counts at the destination rather than at the source.

clauses.subject: skipped-count
clauses.statement: A pull's optional `skipped` field counts inputs the source declined to land whole; the run row sums it over the run's pulls, replayed pulls included, beside the destination counts.
clauses.why: because a skipped input raises no error, and a count on the record surfaces it without reading the landed rows

clauses.subject: input-bounds
clauses.statement: A store-driven run's row carries its input: the resolved `as_of`, the snapshot id per table and the input row count.

clauses.subject: sweep-bounds
clauses.statement: A sweep origin's run row carries, beside {{run.record.input-bounds}}, its `available_as_of`, any `valid_as_of` it read under, the sweep id and the origin.
clauses.why: because a score reported per origin is auditable only when each run names the bounds it read under

clauses.subject: plan-identity
clauses.statement: A run row retains its admitted plan reference after owner retirement; a record lacking that field decodes with no plan identity.

clauses.subject: schema-diff-home
clauses.statement: A table's run manifest holds its committed downgrade events with its parts and cursor; run history reads them under that run id.
scenarios: WHEN a nested column downgrades and its table commits, THEN run history and that table's run manifest carry the same event; a failed stage carries none.

clauses.subject: schema-diff-shape
clauses.statement: Each downgrade event names the table, column path, source type, landed type and reason; a stage that does not commit contributes none.

clauses.subject: best-effort
clauses.statement: Live run state is a best-effort projection of events the runner emits after durable state changes; execution never reads it.

clauses.subject: wire-snapshot
clauses.statement: The wire snapshot carries run id, workflow id, a status from {{run.record.status-set}}, an ordered step list, an application metadata map, optional start and end instants, an optional tagged error and a version. Every deploy target emits it identically.

clauses.subject: step-view
clauses.statement: A step view carries its label, a status of `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed` or `retrying`, its attempt count, optional instants, an optional output reference with byte count, and an optional tagged failure.

clauses.subject: stopped-step
clauses.statement: A stopped run reports its executing step `failed` with the `Canceled` tag and leaves the run-level error unset.

clauses.subject: emission-never-blocks
clauses.statement: Progress emission is no journal step: events reach an in-process observer over a bounded channel that drops when full and never blocks the runner.

clauses.subject: terminal-slot
clauses.statement: A terminal transition bypasses the lossy channel through a per-run slot that is never dropped; a projection reading non-terminal behind a terminal run record reconciles from the record.
clauses.why: because a dropped terminal event otherwise leaves a finished run reading running forever

clauses.subject: coalescing
clauses.statement: The hub coalesces snapshot broadcasts to at most one per 100 ms, keeping only the latest. A terminal transition flushes immediately. The hub uses an injected clock.

clauses.subject: metadata-too-large
clauses.statement: A metadata write whose serialized size exceeds 16384 B raises `RunMetadataTooLarge` naming size and bound, and the snapshot stands unchanged.
clauses.why: because a silently clipped map reads as the complete metadata

clauses.subject: version
clauses.statement: The snapshot version is `(epoch, counter)`, the epoch being the hub's start instant, compared lexicographically; a client discards any delta at or below the highest version it holds.
clauses.why: because a bare counter restarts at zero with the process and freezes every client's view

clauses.subject: reducer-is-total
clauses.statement: The reducer is total: nothing overwrites a terminal step or run status, a new step label appends, an existing one merges field-wise, and a stale delta is a no-op.

clauses.subject: outputs-by-reference
clauses.statement: A step output appears as a post-redaction reference and a byte count, never inline; fetching the payload is a separately authorized request.

clauses.subject: connect
clauses.statement: A subscriber receives the folded snapshot and its update receiver under one lock, missing and duplicating no update.

clauses.subject: broadcast-ring
clauses.statement: The per-run broadcast holds 256 entries; a subscriber that overruns it resynchronizes to the latest snapshot.

clauses.subject: catch-up
clauses.statement: A late joiner may subscribe from the oldest snapshot {{run.project.broadcast-ring}} holds, reading each held snapshot in order before live updates.
clauses.why: because the folded snapshot shows where a run stands, and a late joiner animating the catch-up needs how it got there

clauses.subject: channel-eviction
clauses.statement: The hub evicts a run's channel 60 s after it folds the run's terminal event; a later subscriber recovers from the durable record as after {{run.project.restart-discards}}.
clauses.why: because a channel allocated per run otherwise grows a long-lived process by every run it has seen

clauses.subject: unauthenticated-upgrade
clauses.statement: The run-stream socket, `GET /runs/:run_id/stream`, authenticates on the HTTP request before the upgrade; a missing or invalid credential raises `RunStreamUnauthorized` with `401`, and an unseen run answers `404`.

clauses.subject: read-only-socket
clauses.statement: A subscription permits reads only. Stop requests use an authenticated route.

clauses.subject: restart-discards
clauses.statement: A restart discards in-memory snapshots; a subscriber recovers history from the durable record.

clauses.subject: delegated-progress
clauses.statement: A heavy step delegated to another host reports progress by posting to the awakeable callback route, and the orchestrating run folds it into its own snapshot.

clauses.subject: origins
clauses.statement: A store-driven `[[job]]` declaring `sweep = { start, end, step, state }` opens one run per origin from `start` through `end` at each `step`, a `<n><unit>` interval in {{surface.arm.grammar}} units, each reading with `available_as_of` equal to its origin.
clauses.why: because an origin reading rows published after it scores a forecast against its own answer
scenarios: WHEN a `fresh` sweep of 12 origins, `7d` apart from `2014-03-05T00:00:00Z`, reads a 2026-backfilled table holding a planted row available `2014-04-30T00:00:00Z`, THEN origins 1 to 8 return no planted row and origins 9 to 12 return it.

clauses.subject: sweep-id
clauses.statement: A sweep's id is the execution id of the fire that opens it; every origin's run records it, so run history groups one sweep's origins.

clauses.subject: frozen-as-of
clauses.statement: Every origin of one sweep reads at one `as_of`: the job's declared `as_of`, else the instant the sweep opens, recorded once as {{run.journal.open-as-of}} records it for resumes.

clauses.subject: origin-after-open
clauses.statement: A sweep whose `end` is later than its `as_of` raises `RunSweepOriginAfterOpen`, at validation for a declared `as_of` and at sweep open otherwise, and opens no origin.
clauses.why: because an origin past the frozen corpus reads nothing newer than it, and that empty answer looks like a forecast

clauses.subject: carried-state
clauses.statement: Under `state = "carried"`, origins run in ascending order one at a time, each reading the job's output `tables` at the commit of the preceding origin and every other table at the sweep's `as_of`.

clauses.subject: fresh-state
clauses.statement: Under `state = "fresh"`, the default, every table an origin reads, its output tables included, resolves at the sweep's `as_of`, so no origin reads a row another origin wrote.

clauses.subject: simulated-write
clauses.statement: A row an origin lands into a table declaring `available_time` carries the origin as its availability instant, so a later origin reads it and an earlier origin never does.
clauses.why: because notes an agent wrote at a 2014 origin were available in 2014, not at the instant they committed

clauses.subject: origin-pin
clauses.statement: An origin's plan reference hashes the sweep declaration and its origin beside the fields {{run.journal.input-pin}} hashes, so a resume under a changed sweep meets {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}}.

clauses.subject: no-collapse
clauses.statement: A sweep runs every declared origin, regardless of elapsed time. {{surface.arm.catch-up}} collapses no origin. A failed origin in a `carried` sweep prevents every later origin from opening.
clauses.why: because each origin is a distinct question, and a collapsed or skipped origin drops silently from the score

clauses.subject: cache-key
clauses.statement: No recorded or cached value crosses origins: each origin runs under its own execution id, which keys {{run.journal.entry-key}}, and carries its origin as `available_as_of` among the bounds {{read.cache.result-key}} keys on.
clauses.why: because a cache keyed without the bound passes one origin's answer to another

clauses.subject: role
clauses.statement: A target's orchestrator implements every operation in {{run.journal.substrate-port}}. The engine runner over {{run.journal.storage-ports}} is the reference implementation.

clauses.subject: provider-step
clauses.statement: A provider adapter runs one provider step per table pull or backfill chunk, recording that table's or chunk's commit pointer. The engine's journal entries under {{run.journal.entry-key}} remain inside the provider step.

clauses.subject: semantics
clauses.statement: Every `run.journal`, `run.retry`, `run.suspend` and `run.cancel` clause holds inside a provider step. An adapter's conformance suite demonstrates these clauses before a target profile names the adapter.

clauses.subject: resume
clauses.statement: A provider replay of a completed step returns its recorded commit pointer and re-enters nothing; a crash inside a step resumes under the engine's entry keys, so the parts land byte-identical to an uninterrupted run under {{run.journal.replay-lands}}.
clauses.why: because a replay the provider owns below the commit pointer lands per-target bytes, and the proofs over the journal then cover no managed target
scenarios: WHEN a backfill chunk's provider step crashes after half its pages and the provider replays the step, THEN the engine resumes from its recorded pages and the chunk's parts match the uninterrupted run's bytes.

clauses.subject: one-retry-layer
clauses.statement: A provider adapter disables provider per-step retries. The schedule in {{run.retry.one-layer}} is the only retry layer. A failed step closes its table or chunk as the engine closes it.
clauses.why: because a provider retry around an engine schedule multiplies attempts against a shared quota
scenarios: WHEN a provider step's pull meets a throttle, THEN the engine's schedule retries inside the step and the provider records one step attempt.

clauses.subject: delegate-inside
clauses.statement: Every orchestrator runs a delegate under {{surface.delegate.binding}} inside the engine's journaled step within a provider step. No adapter dispatches a delegate as a separate provider step.
clauses.why: because a delegate reached outside the engine's step escapes the entry key, the fence and the item budget

clauses.subject: pipeline-spec
clauses.statement: A specification carries `id`, `source` and `tables`, plus the optional `destination`, `schedule`, `incremental`, `transforms`, `redaction`, `normalize`, `backfill`, `seed`, `queries` and `on_table_error`.

clauses.subject: serialization
clauses.statement: TOML and JSON deserialize into one `PipelineSpec`; the JSON Schema derived from it is the contract, and `contextful schema export` writes it to `.contextful/schema/pipeline.json`.

clauses.subject: source-block
clauses.statement: A `source` contains a connector name and free-form JSON config object. A `destination` contains the same two fields and defaults to the store.

clauses.subject: manifest-file
clauses.statement: Startup reads project config and inline `[[pipeline]]` blocks from `contextful.toml`, then reads `pipelines/*.toml` and `pipelines/*.json`. Startup collects specifications by `id`.

clauses.subject: manifest-missing
clauses.statement: `pipeline validate` reading no manifest file raises `PipelineManifestMissing`, naming the declaration path.
clauses.why: because a validation over a mistyped path otherwise checks nothing and exits zero

clauses.subject: duplicate-id
clauses.statement: One `id` declared twice raises `PipelineDuplicateId`, naming each file and the line its declaration starts on.
clauses.why: because a silent pick between two declarations hides which one runs

clauses.subject: spec-invalid
clauses.statement: A manifest file the canonical type cannot deserialize raises `PipelineSpecInvalid`, naming the file, the key path and the value found.
clauses.why: because a partly read manifest runs a pipeline its author did not write

clauses.subject: content-hash
clauses.statement: `content_hash` is the sha256 of the specification's RFC 8785 canonical JSON with every optional field at its default elided, so an explicit default hashes as its absence.
clauses.why: because a replay pin that moves on a no-op edit strands pending work

clauses.subject: table-name
clauses.statement: The engine names destination tables `<pipeline id>_<table name>`, replacing each non-alphanumeric character with `_` and lowercasing each ASCII uppercase letter.

clauses.subject: table-name-collision
clauses.statement: Two tables whose destination names fold to one spelling, or one whose name is another's `<name>_dead_letter`, within one pipeline or across pipelines, raise `PipelineTableNameCollision` at validation, naming both declarations.
clauses.why: because two tables folding to one name land in one store table and interleave their rows

clauses.subject: unbound-table-name
clauses.statement: A job target or model reference naming a destination table in a spelling the fold does not produce raises `PipelineUnboundTableName`, printing the expected spelling.

clauses.subject: table-entry
clauses.statement: A `tables` entry is a bare name or an object carrying that table's configuration; the two forms mix in one array.

clauses.subject: order-by-default
clauses.statement: `order_by` defaults to the injected ingest stamp and is inert on a keyless table; key semantics are {{store.declare.unkeyed-union}}.

clauses.subject: write-mode
clauses.statement: `write_mode` is `append`, the default, or `replace`. Under `append` a run adds rows and no key retires; under `replace` the landing run is the table's whole current state.

clauses.subject: replace-unsupported
clauses.statement: `replace` beside a `monotonic` or `opaque-token` cursor, a backfill chunk plan or a seed ceiling raises `PipelineReplaceUnsupported`, naming the table.

clauses.subject: config-key
clauses.statement: A source config key outside the set that source enumerates raises `PipelineUnknownConfigKey` before any I/O, naming the key and the accepted keys; request headers and the forwarded guest table are exempt.

clauses.subject: lifecycle-verbs
clauses.statement: `plan` compares desired state with the store without side effects; `--json` emits a structured diff. `apply` reconciles one or all pipelines. `run` fires one pipeline once. `serve` reconciles continuously.

clauses.subject: plan-externals
clauses.statement: `plan` reports added, removed, changed and unchanged external steps against the applied snapshot in text and under `externals` in `--json`, with the same change fields as other declaration kinds.
clauses.why: because external-only edits affect the applied snapshot and need a visible diff

clauses.subject: apply-fires-nothing
clauses.statement: Applying a manifest triggers no run by itself. Repeating `apply` over unchanged sources performs no work except for elapsed schedules.

clauses.subject: table-error
clauses.statement: `on_table_error = abort`, the default, halts the fire at the first failing table. `continue` lands every other table and reports failed run ids through {{run.declare.table-error-exit}}.

clauses.subject: table-error-exit
clauses.statement: Under continue, `run` exits non-zero naming the failed runs, and a scheduled fire appends its failure count to its log line.

clauses.subject: chunked-load
clauses.statement: `on_table_error` governs the single-pass live pull alone; a seed or backfill chunk plan halts the fire on failure under either setting.

clauses.subject: incremental-field
clauses.statement: `incremental = "<field>"` names the pipeline's stream clock. With this declaration, the source reports a `monotonic` cursor committing {{run.advance.watermark-shape}}. Without this declaration, the source refetches in full.

clauses.subject: incremental-pointer
clauses.statement: An `incremental` value opening with `/` is an RFC 6901 pointer read from each fetched row, so a nested clock such as `/commit/committer/date` orders the stream and names its watermark.

clauses.subject: authoring-surface
clauses.statement: Authoring code runs only at build time and emits a content-hashed plan. No authoring code executes in the serving environment. No build profile embeds a scripting runtime.

clauses.subject: plan-node
clauses.statement: A plan is a flat node list with predecessor edges: `step` (connector, optional retry), `sleep` (duration string), `awaitEvent` (optional timeout), `branch` (predicate, label-to-node-id map), `parallel` (node ids) and `join` (parallel node id, `allow_partial`).

clauses.subject: plan-version
clauses.statement: A plan's version is the leading 16 chars of the sha256 over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of its `{id, nodes}`.

clauses.subject: plan-schema
clauses.statement: One schema library defines the plan type. Every language binds to its JSON Schema. The execution engine deserializes plan JSON against that schema.

clauses.subject: inline-step-body
clauses.statement: A `step` body other than a connector reference raises `PipelineInlineStepBody`.

clauses.subject: control-flow
clauses.statement: A data-dependent conditional or loop in a workflow body raises `PipelineUndeclaredControlFlow`; branching travels as `branch` and fan-out as `parallel`.

clauses.subject: node-id-collision
clauses.statement: A node id repeated in one plan raises `PipelineNodeIdCollision`, naming the id and both positions.

clauses.subject: lowering
clauses.statement: A plan lowers node by node onto {{run.journal.substrate-port}}.

clauses.subject: unjoined-parallel
clauses.statement: A `parallel` node no `join` node names, or a node other than its join reading it or one of its bodies, raises `PipelineParallelUnjoined` at compile.
clauses.why: because an output read around its join reaches a partial result no run record marks as partial

clauses.subject: branch-arm
clauses.statement: A `branch` node records its predicate node's output once, trimming surrounding whitespace to produce the arm label. Every replay selects that recorded arm and skips the other arms' nodes.

clauses.subject: branch-scope
clauses.statement: Each body of a `parallel` node runs under step labels prefixed by the parallel node's id, and its outcome reaches only the join, as {{run.journal.fan-out-join}} states.

clauses.subject: chain
clauses.statement: The chain is an ordered list of `select`, `rename`, `cast`, `extract` and a single-column `filter`, declared once per pipeline and bound to the root table.

clauses.subject: arity
clauses.statement: A chain operation emitting more rows than it consumed raises `PipelineTransformArity`.

clauses.subject: filter
clauses.statement: A filter dropping a root row drops that row's nested children with it.
clauses.why: because a child landing under a parent id no surviving row carries is a dangling reference

clauses.subject: column-missing
clauses.statement: A value filter or cast naming a column the batch does not carry raises `PipelineTransformColumnMissing`, printing the column and the table.
clauses.why: because a cast over an absent column otherwise lands the batch untransformed

clauses.subject: cast
clauses.statement: A cast rewrites one column's type and keeps its name and position.

clauses.subject: projection
clauses.statement: `select` fixes the outgoing column set by name, and `rename` maps an incoming name onto an outgoing one.

clauses.subject: typed-cast
clauses.statement: A cast to `binary`, `binary(n)`, `float32[n]` or `float16[n]` keeps a value that type's JSON form reads, nulls any other, and lands the column in that type.

clauses.subject: type-carry
clauses.statement: A `rename` carries a pulled column type to the new name, a `select` drops it with its column, and a cast to a scalar type drops it.

clauses.subject: extract
clauses.statement: `extract` copies the value at an RFC 6901 pointer into a named column, null where the pointer names nothing, keeps the source column, and lands the new column with no pulled type.

clauses.subject: presence-filter
clauses.statement: A `filter` naming `absent` keeps the rows whose column is missing or null, and one naming `present` keeps the rest; neither requires the batch to carry the column.

clauses.subject: host-stage
clauses.statement: Type inference over deferred-typing JSON, struct flattening, list-to-child extraction and id assignment run in engine code; no connector reimplements them and no dataframe library participates.

clauses.subject: normalized-form
clauses.statement: The canonical form uses nested Arrow structs and lists. The sink projects this form into relational tables late, so a source landing in two sinks normalizes once.

clauses.subject: mode
clauses.statement: `native` keeps nesting the sink supports and expands unsupported nesting with {{run.record.schema-diff-home}}. `relational` flattens structs into parent-child column names and converts lists into child tables joined by a foreign key.
scenarios: WHEN a relational stream holds a struct and a two-item list, THEN the store holds flattened parent columns and two indexed child rows joined to that parent.
WHEN a native sink cannot retain a nested column, THEN the committed table's run manifest carries that column's downgrade event.

clauses.subject: mode-resolution
clauses.statement: Mode resolves per stream per sink: explicit declaration, then sink capability, then `native`.

clauses.subject: mode-unknown
clauses.statement: A mode outside the two raises `PipelineNormalizeModeUnknown`, printing both spellings.

clauses.subject: identity-columns
clauses.statement: Normalize injects a content-hash row id on every table, a load id on the root, a parent id and list index on each child, and a root id on a child nested deeper than one level.

clauses.subject: field-collision
clauses.statement: A relational source field flattening onto an occupied column takes the first free `source_`-prefixed name, preserving injected identity columns and the source value.

clauses.subject: row-id
clauses.statement: The row id hashes the row's own content, so a re-run of one input emits byte-identical ids.

clauses.subject: list-index-missing
clauses.statement: A relational child table emitted without the list index that makes its projection reversible raises `PipelineListIndexMissing`, naming the parent and the list.

clauses.subject: native-store
clauses.statement: On the store sink, `native` lands each undeclared column of objects and arrays as a struct or list column inferred over the batch; a column mixing kinds, or one `schema.json` holds as a scalar, lands as `Json`.

clauses.subject: nesting-depth
clauses.statement: Recursion stops at the declared `depth`, default 5 levels, landing a deeper subtree as one `Json` value.

clauses.subject: placement
clauses.statement: The secret guard runs at the one pull path streaming and backfill share, ahead of the recorded pull and the land path, so a replay reintroduces no credential.

clauses.subject: matchers
clauses.statement: Matchers are linear-time, regex-free forward scans, each anchored on a literal prefix; the credential catalogue lives in code under a precision and recall fixture test.

clauses.subject: llm-candidate
clauses.statement: An LLM candidate starts with `sk-` at input start or after a byte outside ASCII alphanumerics, `-` and `_`; its tail spans that alphabet. Admission masks the whole candidate.

clauses.subject: llm-admission
clauses.statement: An LLM candidate needs 32 B of tail: a `proj-`, `svcacct-`, `service-`, `admin-` or `ant-` prefix permits the whole tail; otherwise its first 32 bytes are ASCII alphanumerics.

clauses.subject: assignment-key
clauses.statement: An assignment key qualifies when it is a keyword or ends in one after `_`, `-` or `.`, reading `-` as `_`, so `client_secret`, `x-api-key` and `db.password` qualify and `clientsecret` does not.
scenarios: WHEN a cell holds `x-api-key: zK9s8d7f6g5h`, THEN it lands as `x-api-key: [REDACTED:secret]`.
WHEN a cell holds `token_type=abcdefgh12`, THEN it lands unchanged.

clauses.subject: mask-span
clauses.statement: The replacement covers only the matched byte ranges, widened to character boundaries; overlapping spans merge under the higher-priority pattern.

clauses.subject: mask-replacement
clauses.statement: The replacement is the fixed `[REDACTED:secret]` marker, never a shape-preserving transform; an assignment keeps its `key=` prefix.

clauses.subject: mask-only
clauses.statement: The guard is on by default and blocks no run; each pull logs the count of masked cells per column.

clauses.subject: coverage
clauses.statement: The guard reads pre-normalize string cells for plaintext shapes; encoded material and a credential split across two cells pass through.

clauses.subject: dead-letter-reason
clauses.statement: A dead letter's `key`, `reason` and `sha256` pass the guard as a pulled row's cells do, so a reason quoting a credential lands masked.

clauses.subject: recorded-body
clauses.statement: Registered body results pass through the same guard before shaping and canonical preparation; the engine reports per-column counts once per fresh paid preparation, excluding counts from the recorded wire and replay.

clauses.subject: stage-order
clauses.statement: A batch passes pull, the secret guard, the recorded pull, normalize, the transform chain, write-path redaction, shredding and batch write; the run then commits rows and position together through {{run.advance.commit-with-rows}}.

clauses.subject: unknown-destination
clauses.statement: The local context store is the only destination, and synthesized artifacts write back through it; any other `destination` raises `PipelineUnknownDestination` at assembly, before any row moves.

clauses.subject: no-host-arm
clauses.statement: The destination world declares no host arm, so a guest supplies no destination.

clauses.subject: batch-write
clauses.statement: The store creates a landing table on first schema observation, {{store.reconcile.first-sight}}. The store writes each batch durably in a separate call. A batch may carry its ordinal for joining the run's request ledger.

clauses.subject: typed-pull
clauses.statement: A pull's `types` object maps a column to a type spelled as {{store.reconcile.typed-landing}} reads it, and the run commit lands that column in it; an unreadable spelling fails the pull as {{store.reconcile.incompatible}}.

clauses.subject: late-type
clauses.statement: A pull declaring a type for a column an earlier staged batch of its run carried undeclared raises `PipelineTypeDeclaredLate`, deterministic, naming the column; the run commits nothing and retires its owner.
clauses.why: because that batch's part already holds the column in its inferred type, and a staged part is immutable

clauses.subject: irreconcilable-schema
clauses.statement: An arriving schema the store cannot reconcile fails the batch as {{store.reconcile.incompatible}}.

clauses.subject: commit-visibility
clauses.statement: A commit makes a run's rows visible for one table in one step; a crash before it leaves a recoverable partial run.

clauses.subject: session
