clauses.statement: A landing session holds one store, node and table declaration across runs and commits each micro-batch as its own run; a later run rewrites no earlier run's parts or manifest.
clauses.why: because a writer flushing every second otherwise pays a process start, a store open and a node resolution per batch

clauses.subject: session-input
clauses.statement: `contextful context land --session` reads one JSON object per stdin line — `run_id`, `rows`, optional `now` — lands each as its own run through one landing session, and prints that run's outcome before reading the next line.
clauses.why: because a host running no serving process still needs one session across its batches
scenarios: WHEN stdin carries `run-1`, `run-2` and `run-1` again, THEN the session prints two commits and one replay, one line each.

clauses.subject: session-schema
clauses.statement: A landing session parses `schema.json` again only when its version — length, modification instant, file identity — moves; a land adding no column or type replaces no `schema.json` and takes no schema lock.
clauses.why: because a land per second otherwise rereads and rewrites the schema under the lock every writer of the table waits on
scenarios: WHEN a session lands 300 single-row runs under one schema, THEN it parses `schema.json` once and leaves the file's bytes and identity unchanged.

clauses.subject: receive-entry
clauses.statement: A delivered batch enters at the pull position of {{run.land.stage-order}}: each declared table it touches lands as one run whose single pull yields that table's rows.
clauses.why: because a pushed row needs the guard, the recorded pull and redaction a pulled row passes
scenarios: WHEN a delivered row carries a credential-shaped cell, THEN the table lands it masked.

clauses.subject: receive-applied
clauses.statement: A served delivery loads its source from one immutable applied version, falling back to declarations only when no version exists; its source outcome follows {{surface.open-console.source-run-evidence}}.

clauses.subject: receive-version-group
clauses.statement: An applied receive group admits spooled members only from its loaded configuration digest and version; declaration fallback occupies a separate namespace, while queue capacity and the land lock remain shared.

clauses.subject: receive-ack
clauses.statement: `contextful pipeline receive <id> --key <key>` reads one batch on stdin and answers after every touched table commits, in declaration order, naming the batch id and each table's run id; a failed table answers retryable only under {{run.retry.retryable-classes}}.
clauses.why: because no commit spans two tables, so a sender learns success only once the last table commits
scenarios: WHEN one `jsonl` batch carries rows for two declared tables, THEN the answer follows both commits and names the batch id and each table's run id.

clauses.subject: receive-batch-key
clauses.statement: A batch key fixes each touched table's run id stem `receive-<digest>.<table>` and owner scope, a later attempt taking `.2`, `.3`; a table whose run under the key, or under the group its scope names, committed replays it and lands nothing.
clauses.why: because a sender retrying after a lost answer must not duplicate committed tables
scenarios: WHEN a batch whose tables all committed arrives again under its key, THEN the answer names the original run id and no row lands.

clauses.subject: receive-resume
clauses.statement: A table under a batch key whose run did not commit resumes the key's pending owner, recorded pull included, and no other key's.
clauses.why: because a sender retrying after a lost answer must not lose uncommitted tables
scenarios: WHEN the receiver dies after recording a delivered batch and the batch is resent under its key, THEN every landed cell but the run id is identical to the uninterrupted run's.

clauses.subject: receive-batch-too-large
clauses.statement: A body exceeding the source's `max_batch_bytes` raises non-retryable `ReceiveBatchTooLarge`. The reader stops one byte past the bound. No table lands.
clauses.why: because an unbounded body is an unbounded allocation the sender controls
scenarios: WHEN a body passes `max_batch_bytes` by one byte, THEN the receiver raises `ReceiveBatchTooLarge` and no table lands.

clauses.subject: receive-queue
clauses.statement: Up to `max_queue_depth` batches per pipeline hold queue slots while waiting or landing. Each batch holds its slot before body reading until the answer. One group lands at a time.
clauses.why: because concurrent senders share each table's single-writer cursor lease

clauses.subject: receive-spool
clauses.statement: A batch decodes and validates alone, so a malformed body answers alone, then spools, synced, to its pipeline's queue before waiting for the land lock; a leader lands every spooled batch, a dead receiver's included.
clauses.why: because a batch whose receiver died must land without its sender, and one malformed body must fail no other batch
scenarios: WHEN a receiver dies after spooling its batch, THEN the next leader lands that batch in its group and a resend under its key replays.

clauses.subject: receive-group
clauses.statement: The land lock's holder lands the batches spooled under its credential, up to `max_queue_depth` members and 64 MiB, as one run per touched table, keyed by the group or a lone member, then pushes once and answers each.
scenarios: WHEN 16 one-row batches spool behind a held land lock that then releases, THEN one run commits all 16 rows, one push follows, and every batch answers committed.

clauses.subject: receive-adopt
clauses.statement: A leader first lands the batches a dead leader claimed as that leader's group, resuming or replaying its run, before any new group forms, so each member key lands once.
clauses.why: because each member's scope names the dead group, so a new group leaves that group's owner pending and its members' scopes renamed
scenarios: WHEN a group's leader dies after opening its run, after staging its parts, or after its commit, THEN a later batch lands apart and each member's resend replays the group's run, every row landed once.

clauses.subject: receive-torn
clauses.statement: An attempt of a batch key, of the group its scope names, or of a new group's key, whose commit the store holds while its run row never closed, closes committed with its stored rows, retires its owner and replays.
clauses.why: because a leader dying between its commit and its run's close otherwise lands the committed rows again
scenarios: WHEN a group of two commits and its run row stays open, THEN one member resent beside a new batch and the other resent alone both replay the group's run, and every row lands once.

clauses.subject: receive-group-isolation
clauses.statement: A group run failing with a class outside {{run.retry.retryable-classes}} lands each member's rows alone under its own key, so a batch the land path refuses answers alone and the group's other members commit.
clauses.why: because one malformed body must fail no other batch, and a sender honoring a non-retryable answer drops its rows
scenarios: WHEN a well-formed batch and one whose row sets a reserved column spool into one group, THEN the well-formed batch commits and only the other answers non-retryable.

clauses.subject: receive-wait
clauses.statement: A spooled batch that neither holds the land lock nor joins a group within the wait of {{store.reserve.commit-wait}} withdraws its spool and answers as {{run.land.receive-backpressure}}.
clauses.why: because a batch no group takes must free its queue slot and tell its sender to resend
scenarios: WHEN a spooled batch waits 30 s behind a held land lock, THEN it leaves the spool and answers `ReceiveBackpressure`, retryable.

clauses.subject: receive-backpressure
clauses.statement: If batches hold every pipeline queue slot, the receiver raises retryable `ReceiveBackpressure` before reading the arriving batch's body.
clauses.why: because a sender told to wait sheds load the receiver cannot absorb
scenarios: WHEN two batches hold both slots of a depth-2 pipeline, THEN a third raises `ReceiveBackpressure` with a 1 s retry interval.

clauses.subject: receive-retry-after
clauses.statement: A {{run.land.receive-backpressure}} answer carries a retry interval of 1 s.

clauses.subject: receive-push-wait
clauses.statement: A delivered batch's `pull_before_run` and `push_after_run` wait at most 30 s for {{store.push.in-flight}}'s push guard, then answer retryable; a resend under the key pushes its committed tables.
clauses.why: because a sender's request outlives no 300 s wait, and a freed queue slot serves the next batch sooner

clauses.subject: receive-write-not-granted
clauses.statement: If a credential lacks `write` over any declared table of a `receive` pipeline, the receiver raises `ReceiveWriteNotGranted` before reading the body. No table lands.
clauses.why: because a sender whose grant falls short learns it before spending the transfer
scenarios: WHEN a credential holds `write` over one of two declared tables, THEN the receiver refuses before reading the body and no table lands.

clauses.subject: receive-key-expired
clauses.statement: A batch key replays or resumes only within the source's `key_retention_secs` of its first attempt. After that window, the receiver raises non-retryable `ReceiveBatchKeyExpired` before reading the body. No table lands.
scenarios: WHEN a key's first attempt is 3601 s old under a 3600 s window, THEN the resend raises `ReceiveBatchKeyExpired` and no row lands.

clauses.subject: receive-endpoint
clauses.statement: `POST /receive/:pipeline` on the served face takes the batch key in the `Contextful-Batch-Key` header, admits the credential before reading the body, and answers `200` with the {{run.land.receive-ack}} answer.
clauses.why: because a sender refused for its credential or grant must not have spent the transfer
scenarios: WHEN a request carries no credential and a body past `max_batch_bytes`, THEN the route answers `401` without reading the body.

clauses.subject: receive-key-missing
clauses.statement: If a delivery names no batch key, the receiver raises non-retryable `ReceiveBatchKeyMissing` before reading the body. No table lands.
clauses.why: because a batch without a key can neither replay nor resume under {{run.land.receive-batch-key}}

clauses.subject: receive-pipeline-unknown
clauses.statement: If a delivery names an undeclared pipeline or a pipeline whose source is not `receive`, the receiver raises `ReceivePipelineUnknown` before reading the body. No table lands.
clauses.why: because a sender's misaddressed batch must not land in another pipeline's tables

clauses.subject: receive-endpoint-status
clauses.statement: The receive route answers `400` for {{run.land.receive-key-missing}}, `404` for {{run.land.receive-pipeline-unknown}}, `403` for {{run.land.receive-write-not-granted}}, `413` for {{run.land.receive-batch-too-large}}, `410` for {{run.land.receive-key-expired}}, `503` with `Retry-After` for {{run.land.receive-backpressure}}, {{run.land.receive-push-wait}} or a retryable failed table, and `422` otherwise.

clauses.subject: receive-queued
clauses.statement: Under {{topology.compose.queue-extension}}, a request asking for a queued answer receives `202` with its batch key after admission and queuing. `202` acknowledges queue custody, without claiming {{run.land.receive-ack}}'s success.
clauses.why: because a sender must not read a queued batch as committed when a later landing can still refuse it

clauses.subject: receive-queued-admission
clauses.statement: A queued delivery passes every check {{run.land.receive-endpoint}} runs before reading a body, and a refused delivery queues nothing.
clauses.why: because a revoked or under-granted sender must learn its refusal before handing over custody

clauses.subject: receive-queued-outcome
clauses.statement: `GET /receive/:pipeline/:key` answers a queued batch's outcome: `pending`, each table's committed run, or the typed refusal its landing raised.
clauses.why: because a sender holding only a queued receipt reads success or refusal from one place

clauses.subject: receive-queued-window
clauses.statement: A queued batch's key window opens when it queues; a consumer reaching it past {{run.land.receive-key-expired}}'s window records that refusal as its outcome and lands nothing.
clauses.why: because a batch delayed in the queue must end typed rather than land after its replay guarantee lapsed
scenarios: WHEN a consumer reaches a batch queued 3601 s earlier under `key_retention_secs = 3600`, THEN its outcome reads `ReceiveBatchKeyExpired` and no table lands.

clauses.subject: receive-queued-spill
clauses.statement: If a body exceeds the queue's message cap, the receiver writes the body to the bucket under its batch key before queuing. The body is deleted after its outcome records.
clauses.why: because a queue message carries a reference when a body under `max_batch_bytes` still exceeds the provider's cap

clauses.subject: receive-queued-ask
clauses.statement: A served delivery carrying `Prefer: respond-async` asks for {{run.land.receive-queued}}'s answer; a delivery without that preference answers as {{run.land.receive-endpoint}}.
clauses.why: because a sender reading the committed answer keeps it, and the preference is HTTP's standard asynchronous request

clauses.subject: receive-queued-credential
clauses.statement: A queued message carries the credential its route admitted; the consumer admits it again against the pinned keys, expiry and revocation, with possession and audience settled at the route, and records a refusal as the batch's outcome.
clauses.why: because a credential revoked or expired while its batch waits must land no row under it

clauses.subject: receive-queued-consume
clauses.statement: A consumer receives up to the queue's batch size, lands each pipeline's queued batches per credential as {{run.land.receive-group}}, pushes, then acknowledges each message whose outcome recorded; a retryable failure leaves its message queued.
clauses.why: because a message acknowledged before its push loses the batch when the engine dies between commit and push

clauses.subject: receive-queued-redelivery
clauses.statement: A redelivered message lands through its batch key under {{run.land.receive-batch-key}}, so a message delivered twice lands its rows once.
clauses.why: because a managed queue delivers at least once
scenarios: WHEN a consumer lands a queued batch and dies before acknowledging it, THEN the next consumer replays the batch key and every row lands once.

clauses.subject: receive-queued-outcome-grant
clauses.statement: The outcome route answers a credential holding `write` over every table of the pipeline and refuses any other as {{run.land.receive-write-not-granted}}.
clauses.why: because the outcome names the runs a sender's rows landed in, which only a sender of those tables reads

clauses.subject: object-arrival-wake
clauses.statement: An object-arrival key only wakes its prefix read, which lists from its held position as a scheduled fire does; a duplicate or reordered key lands nothing twice, and the source's cadence still fires to catch a missed one.
clauses.why: because a notification is a hint a provider may repeat, reorder or drop, and the held position already decides what lands

clauses.subject: ingest-tally
clauses.statement: A fire reports `fetched`, `kept`, `skipped`, `failed` and `dropped_low_quality`, the rows its declared `filter` operations drop, in total and per table; a non-zero `failed` exits non-zero.
clauses.why: because a fire pulls one declared source through its tables, and a `filter` is the one stage that drops a fetched row

clauses.subject: unreadable-input
clauses.statement: Input a parser cannot read raises `PipelineUnreadableInput`, naming the path and the position inside it, permanent against the retry schedule and failing one table's pull unless its source dead-letters it.

clauses.subject: input-fault
clauses.statement: A failure over one input carries its fault: `input` when the input's own bytes defeat the decoder, `configuration` when the declaration or the build does. A source dead-letters an `input` fault alone, never by message.
clauses.why: because a message names an error for people, and branching on its text dead-letters any refusal that repeats the name

clauses.subject: dead-letter
clauses.statement: A pull's dead letters land in the table `<table>_dead_letter`, one row per input carrying its `key`, `reason` and `sha256`, committed in the same run as the table's rows.

clauses.subject: dead-letter-replace
clauses.statement: A replacing table whose read dead-letters any input fails the pull under {{run.land.unreadable-input}}, naming each input, and commits neither its rows nor its dead letters.
clauses.why: because dead letters committing alone record a success while the table stays stale, and repeat each dead letter every fire

clauses.subject: dead-letter-occupied
clauses.statement: Dead letters whose `<table>_dead_letter` already holds a relational child table, or a store table lacking `key`, `reason` or `sha256`, refuse the pull under {{run.declare.table-name-collision}} and land nothing.
clauses.why: because two shapes committing into one table mix their schemas

clauses.subject: partial-parse
clauses.statement: A reader stopping partway through a multi-part input raises `PipelinePartialParse` over the whole input and lands none of its parts.

clauses.subject: parse-boundary
clauses.statement: A decoder subject to process failure runs outside the serving process. The serving process bounds the decoder's wall clock and memory and supports terminating the decoder.

clauses.subject: parse-child
clauses.statement: Each input whose decoder is subject to process failure runs in a separate child process. That process decodes no second input.
scenarios: WHEN two PDF inputs decode in one fire, THEN each input starts a separate child process.

clauses.subject: parse-deadline
clauses.statement: A decode runs for at most 60 s from child spawn; expiry kills its process group and raises {{run.land.parse-crashed}}.
scenarios: WHEN a decoder holds its output pipe past 60 s, THEN its process group dies and that input fails by name.

clauses.subject: parse-memory
clauses.statement: A decoder child receives at most 512 MiB of memory; exceeding the bound fails that input under {{run.land.parse-crashed}}.
scenarios: WHEN a decoder exceeds 512 MiB, THEN that input fails and the serving process continues.

clauses.subject: parse-crashed
clauses.statement: A non-zero exit or fatal signal from the decode process raises `PipelineParseCrashed` naming the input; no input ends the serving process.

clauses.subject: table-failed
clauses.statement: A table whose pull fails raises `PipelineTableFailed` carrying the table, the error kind and the run id; the fire then follows `on_table_error`.
clauses.why: because a failure is answerable by name only when it carries its table and run

clauses.subject: observed-schema
clauses.statement: Planning fetches no source schema. Staging assigns each observed batch's types under {{run.own.stage-schema}} and validates the batch against declared columns.
scenarios: WHEN a source exposes no schema before its first batch, THEN planning succeeds and staging checks that batch against the declared table columns.

clauses.subject: export-block
clauses.statement: An OTLP `[[export]]` block declares `name`, one landed `table`, an HTTP `endpoint`, `signal = "logs"` and optional `headers`; `contextful export run <name>` delivers every row its cursor has not passed.

clauses.subject: signal-unknown
clauses.statement: If `signal` is not `logs`, the exporter raises `ExportSignalUnknown` before reading any row.
clauses.why: because the one built-in arm maps a row onto a log record, and a span or metric needs a column mapping no block declares

clauses.subject: post-commit-read
clauses.statement: Export reads committed runs only, through the read face under the admitted credential, so its grants, row policy and masks hold; no landing waits on an export.

clauses.subject: commit-order
clauses.statement: Export reads rows past its cursor ordered by `_commit_seq`, then `_row_seq`. Export does not order by `_ingested_at`; {{store.reserve.commit-seq}} keeps late-committing runs eligible.

clauses.subject: commit-seq-missing
clauses.statement: A table holding rows whose `_commit_seq` is null, from parts landed without the column, raises `ExportCommitSeqMissing` naming the export and the row count, before any batch leaves.
clauses.why: because a null never passes a cursor, and a row an export skips in silence is a row its mirror loses

clauses.subject: batch-rows
clauses.statement: One delivery batch holds at most 500 rows.
clauses.why: because a batch that size sits below the face row ceiling and the request limits common collectors apply

clauses.subject: log-record
clauses.statement: Each row becomes one OTLP log record: `timeUnixNano` from `_ingested_at`, each non-null column outside the `_` namespace an attribute, beside `contextful.table`, `contextful.run_id`, `contextful.commit_seq` and `contextful.row_seq`.
clauses.why: because the attributes a target deduplicates on travel with the record, and the engine's own columns stay its own

clauses.subject: delivery
clauses.statement: The exporter sends each batch as one OTLP/HTTP JSON `POST` through the mediated client. The allowlist contains only the endpoint host. Each header follows {{connector.resolve.hydration-is-just-in-time}}.

clauses.subject: secret-preflight
clauses.statement: If no adapter resolves a header reference, the exporter refuses at preflight as {{connector.resolve.unresolved-name}} before reading any row.
clauses.why: because a target the export cannot authenticate to is known before a batch is built

clauses.subject: cursor-after-ack
clauses.statement: The cursor, the last delivered `_commit_seq` and `_row_seq`, commits only after the target answers 2xx for the batch.
clauses.why: because an unacknowledged batch remains eligible for delivery after a restart

clauses.subject: queue-wake
clauses.statement: A post-commit queue message only wakes an exporter, which reads through {{run.export.commit-order}} and advances under {{run.export.cursor-after-ack}}; a lost message delays delivery to the next wake and skips no row.
clauses.why: because a message lost between commit and enqueue must not lose the rows it announced

clauses.subject: local-state
clauses.statement: The local storage profile keeps log cursors in `.contextful/exports/<project>/<name>.json`, outside corpus sync, and typed delivery state in `machine.sqlite`.

clauses.subject: remote-state
clauses.statement: Under {{run.journal.container-profile}}, PostgreSQL holds typed outboxes, acknowledged keyed state and log checkpoints in the execution database; a replacement reoffers identical pending event ids before advancing its acknowledged frontier.

clauses.subject: d1-state
clauses.statement: Under {{run.journal.d1-profile}}, D1 commits export outboxes, acknowledged keyed state and log checkpoints; a sink commit without its D1 acknowledgement reoffers the same delivery identity.

clauses.subject: writer-fenced
clauses.statement: A PostgreSQL exporter whose durable writer lease has transferred raises `ExecutionWriterFenced` before dispatch or state publication; its lease row stays locked throughout an admitted outbound call, and takeover waits for that call.

clauses.subject: at-least-once
clauses.statement: A run ending between a target's acknowledgement and the cursor commit resends that batch on the next run; a target deduplicates on `contextful.commit_seq` and `contextful.row_seq`.

clauses.subject: delivery-refused
clauses.statement: A target answering other than 2xx, or unreachable, raises `ExportDeliveryRefused` naming the export and the answer, and the cursor stays where it stood.
clauses.why: because an unacknowledged batch is resent from the cursor, never skipped

clauses.subject: typed-block
clauses.statement: A typed `[[export]]` block declares `format = "changes-v1"`, nonempty `key` columns and `schedule`, beside `name`, `table`, `endpoint` and optional `headers`.
clauses.why: because a consumer needs stable row identity and a delivery cadence

clauses.subject: typed-state
clauses.statement: A typed export compares the latest stable committed table read through {{run.export.post-commit-read}} with its last acknowledged state; commits between reads coalesce into one publication.
clauses.why: because a scheduled state export promises the observed frontier rather than every intermediate write

clauses.subject: typed-view-recheck
clauses.statement: A typed export re-reads its admitted table even without a source commit frontier change. The exporter stages a publication when its key, schema, policy or visible state changes.
clauses.why: because a commit hash alone cannot identify the view delivered to a consumer

clauses.subject: typed-publication-id
clauses.statement: A typed publication identifier covers the source frontier, read identity and visible keyed state, so distinct delivered views carry distinct identifiers without requiring another source commit.
clauses.why: because a receiver must not mistake a changed view for a retry of the prior publication

clauses.subject: typed-events
clauses.statement: Each changed key yields a versioned upsert with its visible row or a deletion with its key; unchanged keys yield no event.
clauses.why: because a generic consumer applies the same keyed operations regardless of table shape

clauses.subject: typed-order
clauses.statement: Typed events order by encoded key and carry consecutive sequences and stable ids; a repeat delivery carries the same bytes and ids.
clauses.why: because acknowledgement can fail after the target applies a batch

clauses.subject: typed-complete
clauses.statement: A publication-complete event follows every change, including an empty set, and states that publication's change count.
clauses.why: because a consumer needs a boundary after which its keyed state represents one observed frontier

clauses.subject: typed-outbox
clauses.statement: Events and their next keyed state stage together in the configured execution store; a pending publication blocks staging a later frontier.
clauses.why: because a failed send must retain its exact payload and order across restarts

clauses.subject: typed-identity-changed
clauses.statement: Pending events under a changed read identity, or an export redirected to another target under the same name, raise `ExportIdentityChanged` without delivery; watch exits.
clauses.why: because an old outbox cannot prove authorization under a changed view or establish a new target's baseline

clauses.subject: typed-ack
clauses.statement: A typed export advances its durable acknowledgement sequence only after HTTP 2xx; acknowledging the completion event promotes its staged state in the same transaction.
clauses.why: because a receiver acknowledgement and local state promotion have one durable order

clauses.subject: typed-watch
clauses.statement: `contextful export watch <name>` fires the typed export on its schedule and retries a refused send with capped exponential delay from the pending outbox.
clauses.why: because delivery resumes without another operator invocation

clauses.subject: typed-byte-limit
clauses.statement: One typed JSON request holds at most 65536 B.
clauses.why: because a row-count bound alone admits an unbounded request body

clauses.subject: typed-event-too-large
clauses.statement: If a typed event exceeds one request's capacity, the exporter raises `ExportEventTooLarge`. Watch stops without retrying that event.
clauses.why: because an unchanged oversized event cannot make progress on retry

clauses.subject: group-block
clauses.statement: A local `[[publication]]` declares `name`, producer `job` and typed export `members`; members cover every producer output exactly once and share one destination and header binding.

clauses.subject: group-source
clauses.statement: A successful store-driven job or materialized model build records one immutable completion binding its run identifier, pinned input frontier and all output table frontiers, including empty outputs.

clauses.subject: group-source-latest
clauses.statement: The sqlite and D1 publication ledgers keep 1 completion per publication, the latest: the latest run recorded again with different bytes refuses, and a completion naming another run replaces it.
clauses.why: because a run is re-recorded only by its own retry, and history kept past it grows with every build

clauses.subject: group-delivery
clauses.statement: `contextful export group <name>` reads every completed producer member through {{run.export.post-commit-read}}, rechecks every frontier, and stages one ordered outbox with explicit member-complete events followed by one group-complete event.

clauses.subject: group-identity
clauses.statement: A group's identity binds its store incarnation, destination, namespace, read identity, predecessor, publication order, input frontier, membership, delivered base and next state; each event identifier binds that group and its sequence.

clauses.subject: group-activation
clauses.statement: A receiver stages member events transactionally and activates every member together only after validating the complete group; interrupted delivery preserves the active group, and acknowledged retries preserve its bytes and visibility.

clauses.subject: group-checkpoint
clauses.statement: `contextful export checkpoint` saves delivery state; `contextful export restore` replays compatible immutable events while the receiver retains its accepted groups and active frontier, so an older checkpoint reverses no deletion or later publication.

clauses.subject: group-rebuild
clauses.statement: `contextful export rebuild <name> --namespace <epoch>` exports the completed producer's full admitted state into a fresh namespace without executing its effects; the receiver keeps its active namespace until the replacement group completes.

clauses.subject: group-input-digest
clauses.statement: A group plan's `input` carries the lowercase hex SHA-256 of its producer completion's JSON rather than the completion, so every request repeats a header of bounded size whatever the producer's input frontier holds.
clauses.why: because a producer's input frontier is caller-shaped JSON of any size, and each request repeats the group header

clauses.subject: group-request-bound
clauses.statement: Staging refuses a group whose header beside its smallest event exceeds {{run.export.typed-byte-limit}} with `PublicationHeaderTooLarge`, and one holding an event unable to fit beside its header with {{run.export.typed-event-too-large}}; the outbox stays unchanged.
clauses.why: because a staged group blocks every later frontier until acknowledged, so an unsendable one strands its outbox

clauses.subject: group-stranded
clauses.statement: Staging replaces a pending group unable to form its first request, which therefore no receiver holds, with the current frontier's group; a group with an acknowledged prefix stays immutable.
clauses.why: because a group never offered carries no delivery obligation, while a receiver may already stage an acknowledged prefix
scenarios: WHEN an earlier sender staged a group whose header alone exceeds the request ceiling, THEN the next `contextful export group` replaces it with a digest-headed group and delivers it.

clauses.subject: group-quiesce
clauses.statement: `contextful export group <name>` first takes the publication's dispatch intent, so serve starts no unit over its inputs, then holds those inputs exclusively through its pull, read, staging and delivery.
clauses.why: because a commit during the export moves the producer frontier the export rechecks
scenarios: WHEN serve's cycle finds the producer due while an export of its publication awaits the receiver, THEN the cycle reports the producer pending and the export acknowledges its group.

clauses.subject: group-quiesce-wait
clauses.statement: An export still waiting for the publication's intent and inputs 300 s after it began waiting for either raises `PublicationInputsBusy` before its pull, read or staging; the outbox stays unchanged.
clauses.why: because a running producer ends on its own schedule, and the next attempt exports its completed frontier

clauses.subject: group-incompatible
clauses.statement: Membership drift, incarnation mismatch, a changed pending read identity, an incompatible checkpoint, an incomplete producer frontier, or a predecessor/order mismatch raises `PublicationIncompatible` before delivery or activation.

clauses.subject: group-storage
clauses.statement: A coordinated publication under `postgres` raises `PublicationStorageUnsupported` naming the coordinated-group-outbox capability before execution, staging or delivery; a `cloudflare-d1` sender state over 8 MiB raises it before staging.

clauses.subject: group-sender-profile
clauses.statement: {{run.export.group-storage}} reads the sender's storage profile alone; under the local profile a group keeps its sender state in `machine.sqlite` and delivers to any `changes-v1` receiver, a D1-backed one included.
clauses.why: because the outbox is the sender's durable state, and a receiver's storage is behind its endpoint

clauses.subject: group-d1-state
clauses.statement: Under {{run.journal.d1-profile}}, D1 holds each group's producer frontier, sender outbox and active namespace; one D1 batch commits a completing acknowledgement with its promoted state and active namespace.
scenarios: WHEN a replacement loses the acknowledgement of the group-complete batch, THEN it reoffers that batch, and the receiver's accepted group absorbs the retry without a second activation.

clauses.subject: group-d1-lease
clauses.statement: A `cloudflare-d1` group writer holds one durable D1 lease per publication, and every sender write predicates on that lease and the row's prior version.

clauses.subject: group-d1-spill
clauses.statement: A `cloudflare-d1` sender row over 64 KiB holds the SHA-256 of an R2 object written before the row commits; the blob sweep keeps every object a publication row references.
clauses.why: because a D1 write crosses the binding once and never resends, an R2 put resends, and an object reached only through a committed row is never half visible

clauses.subject: group-d1-acknowledge
clauses.statement: A `cloudflare-d1` acknowledgement short of group completion advances the sender row's version and records the group and acknowledged sequence in a row of its own, leaving the outbox body unwritten.
clauses.why: because the outbox holds the group's delivered base and next state, so rewriting it per batch scales every acknowledgement with the published tables
scenarios: WHEN a receiver completes a group of 880 deletes whose final acknowledgement the sender lost, THEN the replacement reoffers from the last recorded sequence, the receiver absorbs the retry, and the sender promotes the group.

clauses.subject: group-d1-resume
clauses.statement: Reading a `cloudflare-d1` outbox resumes after the event carrying its recorded acknowledged sequence, whatever batch boundaries the reading binary cuts; a sequence naming no unacknowledged event of the pending group fails every read.
clauses.why: because batch boundaries follow the reading binary's request ceiling, row cap and event encoding, which a replacement binary may change
scenarios: WHEN a replacement whose batches end elsewhere reads an outbox acknowledged through a sequence inside its first batch, THEN it offers from the next event.

clauses.subject: group-d1-takeover
clauses.statement: `contextful export group <name> --take-over` under `cloudflare-d1` takes the publication lease whatever its holder or expiry and advances its fence, so the prior holder's next write, a producer completion included, matches no lease and refuses.
clauses.why: because a delivery killed at its caller's time bound holds the lease until expiry, and a fenced producer's build retry records its completion again
scenarios: WHEN a delivery is killed before its acknowledgement while its lease runs, THEN a retry with `--take-over` delivers at once and the killed writer's next write refuses as fenced.

clauses.subject: group-d1-recovery
clauses.statement: After an empty-disk replacement, `contextful export group` resumes a staged or partially acknowledged `cloudflare-d1` group from D1, reoffering identical group and event identifiers before staging a later frontier.
scenarios: WHEN the container stops after D1 commits a staged group and before any delivery, THEN its replacement delivers that group's exact bytes and the receiver activates every member together.

clauses.subject: phase
clauses.statement: The catalog records one phase per pipeline: `planning` computes the chunk plan with nothing fetched, `seeding` loads consumer-held history, `backfilling` runs chunks across ticks, `streaming` pulls the incremental delta.

clauses.subject: chunk-plan
clauses.statement: Plan shape follows cursor kind: `monotonic` plans independent time-window or id-range chunks, `opaque-token` one sequential chunk walked in order, `snapshot-id` version ranges sequential per stream and parallel across streams.

clauses.subject: chunk-parallelism
clauses.statement: A sequential chunk plan declared beside a parallelism above one raises `PipelineChunkParallelism`, naming the plan and the value.
clauses.why: because two workers walking one continuation token skip or duplicate pages silently

clauses.subject: chunk
clauses.statement: A chunk row carries pipeline id, chunk id, predicate, status, attempt count, start and completion instants and a cursor-committed flag; an interrupted plan resumes at the first chunk not done.

clauses.subject: chunk-lease
clauses.statement: A worker leases a chunk row, recording node id and attempt, for a 300 s time-to-live renewed every 60 s, and writes under a path segmented by run, node, chunk and attempt.
clauses.why: because an unquantified lease cannot be tested against a paused worker

clauses.subject: fenced-commit
clauses.statement: A chunk commits in one catalog update conditioned on `attempt = :mine AND status != 'done'`; an update matching no row leaves that worker's files uncommitted.
clauses.why: because an expired holder otherwise commits over its successor

clauses.subject: commit-signal
clauses.statement: The catalog row signals commit; directory presence does not. Retention collects files under paths without a done row according to a retention window.

clauses.subject: attempt-isolation
clauses.statement: An expired lease lets a second worker claim the chunk, increment the attempt and write under its own path.

clauses.subject: tick
clauses.statement: While a pipeline backfills, a tick dispatches up to the per-tick chunk cap or no-ops when the queue is full; the declared cadence resumes once the position catches up.

clauses.subject: block
clauses.statement: `[pipeline.backfill]` declares `max_chunks`, the bound on a plan's chunk count; `chunk_size`, one clock-ranged chunk's width in cursor units; and `start_from`, the floor, default zero.

clauses.subject: rewind
clauses.statement: A rewind returns every chunk overlapping the half-open range to pending and appends one reason row per rewound chunk to an audit log a catalog rebuild leaves untouched.

clauses.subject: rewind-invalid
clauses.statement: An inverted, empty or scale-incomparable rewind window raises `PipelineRewindWindowInvalid`; a window overlapping no chunk is a no-op.

clauses.subject: available-instant
clauses.statement: A backfill lands each row's availability column as {{store.available-time.declaration}} resolves it from the source, while `_ingested_at` stays the commit instant {{run.own.stage-instant}} writes.
clauses.why: because a 2026 backfill of 2014 history stamped with its commit instant answers no availability bound before 2026

clauses.subject: block
clauses.statement: `[pipeline.seed]` attaches a bulk-load source with a ceiling `below` expressed on the seeded table's `order_by` scale.

clauses.subject: one-land-path
clauses.statement: Seeded rows travel {{run.land.stage-order}} unchanged; attribution survives only in the load id and a run recorded under the `seeding` phase.

clauses.subject: available-instant
clauses.statement: A seeded row lands its availability instant and `_ingested_at` as {{run.backfill.available-instant}} lands a backfilled row's.

clauses.subject: declaration-missing
clauses.statement: A seeded table without `primary_key`, or with `order_by` left at the ingest stamp, raises `PipelineSeedDeclarationMissing` at plan and validate.

clauses.subject: ceiling-breached
clauses.statement: A seeded row whose ordering stamp reaches `below` raises `PipelineSeedCeilingBreached` naming the value; its chunk lands nothing, and the stamp is neither clamped nor dropped.

clauses.subject: ceiling-point
clauses.statement: The engine evaluates the ceiling on the root batch after normalization and the transform chain, before writing.

clauses.subject: ceiling-unevaluable
clauses.statement: A batch missing the ordering column, or a stamp unorderable against the ceiling, raises `PipelineSeedCeilingUnevaluable`; a text stamp orders only when `Z`-suffixed at the ceiling's fractional width.

clauses.subject: scope
clauses.statement: Seed chunk and cursor state live under a `<table>#seed` scope apart from the live pipeline's.

clauses.subject: connector-pin
clauses.statement: A seeding run is exempt from {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}} and records its connector identity as provenance.

clauses.subject: ceiling-binding
clauses.statement: On seed commit, an unset `monotonic` live position takes the ceiling when `below` parses as an integer; under the other cursor kinds the live position stays unset and starts from the source's beginning.

clauses.subject: fingerprint
clauses.statement: Each run probes the seed source for a cheap fingerprint, a stat or a HEAD and never a download, and compares it with the one stamped at commit.

clauses.subject: source-changed
clauses.statement: A differing fingerprint raises `PipelineSeedSourceChanged` naming both values; an equal one skips the load, and an unavailable one skips with a warning.

clauses.subject: commands
clauses.statement: `seed status` prints each seeded table's ceiling, commit state and fingerprint match; `seed reset <pipeline> [--table T]` clears the seed's chunk plan and commit stamp, so the next run loads it again.

clauses.subject: parity
clauses.statement: Over keys the vendor still returns, seeding then running live across an overlapping window yields a pure live backfill's row count and per-key winners; a key the vendor stopped returning keeps its seeded value.

clauses.subject: parity-audit
clauses.statement: `validate` audits the seed ordering over every landed row, not over the deduped view.

clauses.subject: compaction-cadence
clauses.statement: A seeded table that no job meeting {{store.declare.fold-job}} covers raises `PipelineSeedCompactionMissing` at validate and before a fire, naming the table.

clauses.subject: model-block
clauses.statement: A `[[model]]` block carries `id`, {{run.model.statement-source}}, optional `materialized`, `unique_key`, `publish`, `[model.contract]`, `[model.freshness]`, `[[model.test]]`, {{disclosure.release.model-policy}} and {{disclosure.set-mode.opt-out-record}}; an unknown key refuses as {{run.declare.spec-invalid}}.

clauses.subject: statement-source
clauses.statement: A model declares exactly one of inline `sql` and `sql_file`; the latter reads UTF-8 text relative to the manifest containing the model.
clauses.why: because a manifest-relative statement file keeps a model portable across project roots

clauses.subject: top-level-block
clauses.statement: A manifest's top-level key outside the set the engine enumerates raises `PipelineUnknownBlock`, naming the key, the file and the accepted set.
clauses.why: because a misspelled block parses as nothing, and its declaration silently never runs

clauses.subject: model-id
clauses.statement: A model's `id` names the store table it builds; an id declared twice, equal to a pipeline destination table, or naming a table a landing wrote refuses as {{run.declare.table-name-collision}}.

clauses.subject: sql
clauses.statement: A model statement is one read-only `SELECT` over store tables. The engine admits the statement under {{read.guard.whole-tree-walk}} before reading any row. A model reads another model's last published table.

clauses.subject: validate-statements
clauses.statement: `pipeline validate` admits each model's `sql` and every test's statement as a build does, counting every relation but the model's own id in `sql` as registered, holds each declared input to {{run.model.restricted-input}}, and raises the error the build raises.

clauses.subject: validate-undeclared
clauses.statement: `pipeline validate` names on stderr each relation a model's `sql` or test reads that no manifest table, pipeline destination or model declares, and still validates the model; `build` resolves that relation against the store.
clauses.why: because a table landed without a manifest declaration is a legal input, while a misspelled name otherwise surfaces only at `build`

clauses.subject: restricted-input
clauses.statement: A build reading a table that declares `class`, `policy` or `visibility` raises `ModelInputRestricted`, naming the table and the declared keys.
clauses.why: because a build reads its inputs unmasked, so the model's table serves their withheld cells to every reader

clauses.subject: materialized
clauses.statement: `materialized` is `table`, the default: each build replaces the model's rows whole.

clauses.subject: unique-key
clauses.statement: `unique_key` defines the model's row identity. A build with duplicate key values or a null in a key column refuses as {{run.publish.contract-mismatch}}.

clauses.subject: contract-block
clauses.statement: `[model.contract]` declares `version`, a `<major>.<minor>.<patch>` string, and `columns`, each a `name`, a `type` spelled as {{store.reconcile.typed-landing}} reads it, and `nullable`, default true.

clauses.subject: contract-required
clauses.statement: A model whose `publish` is true, the default, and which declares no `[model.contract]` raises `ModelContractUndeclared` at validation.
clauses.why: because a published table without a declared contract has no identity a reader can pin against

clauses.subject: unpublished
clauses.statement: A model declaring `publish = false` commits its rows with no manifest section, so no build entry, hold or contract history names it.

clauses.subject: contract-major
clauses.statement: Under the published build's major, a contract that drops or retypes a published column, makes a non-null one nullable, adds a non-null column or changes the grain refuses as {{run.publish.contract-mismatch}}, naming the column and the major to bump.

clauses.subject: contract-minor
clauses.statement: Under the published build's major, a contract that only adds nullable columns or makes nullable ones non-null publishes once its minor exceeds the published one, else refuses as {{run.publish.contract-mismatch}}, naming the added or tightened column and the bumped minor.
scenarios: WHEN contract `1.0.0` gains nullable column `tag` as `1.1.0`, THEN the build publishes and the manifest section carries `1.1.0` and the new fingerprint; as `1.0.0` it refuses naming `tag` and `1.1.0`.

clauses.subject: injected-columns
clauses.statement: A build lands `_ingested_at` as its start instant, `_run_id` as its build id, `_row_seq` as the row's position, `_commit_seq` as its commit's value and `_site_id`, replacing any injected column the SQL selects; `semantics_version` is 2.

clauses.subject: freshness-block
clauses.statement: `[model.freshness]` declares `max_lag` as an integer followed by `s`, `m`, `h` or `d`; a model declaring none publishes a null `max_lag` and never computes stale.

clauses.subject: test-block
clauses.statement: A `[[model.test]]` carries a `name` and one `SELECT` over the staged rows, registered under the model's id, and the store's tables; a test returning any row fails.
clauses.why: because a test must inspect the candidate build before its rows become visible to readers

clauses.subject: test-failed
clauses.statement: A failing test raises `ModelTestFailed`, naming the test and its row count; the build publishes nothing.
clauses.why: because a test exists to stop a build before readers trust it
scenarios: WHEN a test `SELECT * FROM daily WHERE n < 0` returns 2 rows, THEN the build raises `ModelTestFailed` naming the test and 2, and `daily` reads its prior build.

clauses.subject: build-verb
clauses.statement: `contextful build <model>` materializes the model into staging, checks its contract, runs its tests, then commits; `--json` prints the build id, row count and watermark.

clauses.subject: build-boundary
clauses.statement: A guarded model build admits its caller's execution boundary after staging and before changing the persistent schema or published pointer; a refusal discards staging and preserves prior schema, membership and watermark.
clauses.why: because a stopped execution must not publish its staged model

clauses.subject: unknown-model
clauses.statement: `build` naming no declared model raises `ModelUndeclared`, naming the declared models.
clauses.why: because a build of a misspelled id otherwise reports nothing to do

clauses.subject: build-frontier
clauses.statement: `build` reads each input at its committed frontier and fires no pipeline; a build ordered after a landing is a `build` job naming that pipeline in `after`, under {{surface.fire.build-dependency}}.
clauses.why: because `after` already orders builds behind pipelines, and a verb firing sources needs their credentials and quota, and repeats paid calls on every retry
scenarios: WHEN the `http` pipeline feeding a model's input points at an unreachable endpoint, THEN `build` succeeds, records no new run, and its watermark names only runs already committed.
WHEN a `build` job naming `orders` in `after` fires in the cycle that lands `orders` run `r`, THEN the published build's watermark `through` under `orders_items` reaches the `commit_seq` of `r`.

clauses.subject: model-cycle
clauses.statement: If a model's `sql` reaches its own id through one or more other models, `pipeline validate`, import, apply and `build` raise `ModelCycle`. The engine names every model on the cycle and reads no store.
clauses.why: because no member of a cycle has a first build, and once one exists each build folds in the other's previous output
scenarios: WHEN model `a` reads `b` and `b` reads `a`, THEN `pipeline validate` raises `ModelCycle` naming `a`, `b`, and `build a` reads no row.

clauses.subject: build-id
clauses.statement: A build's id is the snapshot id it publishes.

clauses.subject: watermark
clauses.statement: A build's watermark is `{at, inputs}`: per input table the snapshot id, `through`, the greatest `commit_seq` read, and `omitted`, the count and digest of runs read outside the snapshot chain; `at` is the newest commit instant.
clauses.why: because a list of omitted runs grows by one key per run on an input no fold covers

clauses.subject: watermark-digest
clauses.statement: `omitted.digest` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 over the sorted keys `<run-id>/<node-id>` of the omitted runs, each followed by a newline.

clauses.subject: watermark-listed-runs
clauses.statement: A watermark input carrying a `runs` list and no `omitted` reads with those runs included under {{run.publish.staleness}}; no build writes `runs`, and every echo of that watermark keeps the list.
clauses.why: because a manifest committed with listed runs stays readable

clauses.subject: build-horizon
clauses.statement: `contextful build <model> --available-as-of <t>` reads every input at `available_as_of` equal to `t` and records `t` as the watermark's `horizon`; a build without the flag records a null horizon.
clauses.why: because a build is reused across horizons only when its own bound is recorded beside it

clauses.subject: hold-verb
clauses.statement: `build hold --for <n>[smhd] <model> <build>` commits a hold until now plus the duration and prints `Held`, or `Renewed` over an unexpired hold; `--json` prints the receipt as an object.
scenarios: WHEN `build hold --for 7d daily <build>` runs twice, THEN the first prints `Held` and the second `Renewed`, each with the new expiry.

clauses.subject: status-verb
clauses.statement: `build status <model>` reports the last attempt separately from the published build; `--json` carries their ids, status, freshness and staleness computed at the requested instant.

clauses.subject: hold-unknown-build
clauses.statement: A hold naming a build no committed manifest of the model records raises `ModelBuildUnknown`.
clauses.why: because a hold on a build that does not exist protects nothing and reads as protection

clauses.subject: hold-manifest
clauses.statement: A hold commits as the hold manifest `holds/<build id>.json` in the model's table directory, replacing any earlier hold on that build.

clauses.subject: log-regeneration
clauses.statement: The history logs sit in the model's table directory; each build and hold rewrites them, replacing an entry a manifest disagrees with and keeping entries of collected builds.

clauses.subject: manifest-commit
clauses.statement: The snapshot manifest commit publishes a table's data, contract identity, freshness and current build together. No separate file is authoritative for these values.
clauses.why: because separately written artifacts make a torn publication representable

clauses.subject: contract-identity
clauses.statement: A published table's identity is `contract_version` beside `schema_fingerprint`, taken over the declared columns, their types and the grain.

clauses.subject: contract-mismatch
clauses.statement: A materialization whose columns, types or grain miss the declared contract raises `PipelineContractMismatch`, naming the column and the expectation.

clauses.subject: staging
clauses.statement: A build materializes into staging and publishes through {{run.publish.manifest-commit}}; a refused build leaves the last published state serving.

clauses.subject: history-logs
clauses.statement: `contract-history.jsonl`, `builds.jsonl` and `holds.jsonl` contain append-only history derived from committed manifests and build-attempt records. If a log disagrees with a source record, the engine regenerates the log from that record.

clauses.subject: build-entry
clauses.statement: A build entry carries build id, start and completion instants, a status of published, refused, partial or failed, the contract identity, and the partition values it left unfilled.

clauses.subject: failed-attempt
clauses.statement: A published model records an attempt before materialization; a dead attempt without a committed manifest reports `failed`, keeps the prior published build serving, and contributes a failed build entry.
clauses.why: because a process killed before publication cannot write its own failure, while its attempt record and released lock survive

clauses.subject: freshness
clauses.statement: Freshness carries the newest publishing build id, its watermark, `max_lag`, the last build status and a withheld-cells flag; staleness follows {{run.publish.staleness}} and is never stored.

clauses.subject: staleness
clauses.statement: A published model is stale at `t` when an input holds a committed run outside its watermark snapshot chain, its `commit_seq` above `through`, committed before `t` minus `max_lag`; `build status --json` names each such input under `stale_inputs`.
scenarios: WHEN no input lands after a build and `max_lag` is `1h`, THEN `build status` at 100 days later reports `stale` false.
WHEN `events` lands a run 1 second past the build and `max_lag` is `1h`, THEN status reports fresh at 1 hour after the landing and stale, `stale_inputs` `["events"]`, 1 second later.
WHEN a fold folds the runs a build read into a new snapshot, THEN status still reports the build fresh.

clauses.subject: staleness-omitted-check
clauses.statement: An input whose runs outside the watermark snapshot chain, at or below `through`, differ in count or digest from `omitted` holds a waiting run counted as committed before `t` minus `max_lag`.
scenarios: WHEN a run merged from another node carries a `commit_seq` below `through` and the build never read it, THEN status reports the input stale at once.
WHEN a relational run's group marker lands after a build read a plain run committed above it, THEN status reports the input stale at once.

clauses.subject: staleness-unsequenced
clauses.statement: A run carrying no `commit_seq` counts as at or below `through` when committed at or before the watermark's `at`.
clauses.why: because a run manifest may carry no sequence, and {{run.publish.staleness-omitted-check}} catches one the build never read

clauses.subject: staleness-collected-covered
clauses.statement: A run whose manifest retention collected counts as at or below `through` when the current snapshot folding it records a `commit_seq` at or below `through`.
clauses.why: because a snapshot's `commit_seq` bounds every run it folds

clauses.subject: staleness-model-input
clauses.statement: An input that is a model also waits on each of its published builds newer than the watermark snapshot, aged by that build's `created_at`.
scenarios: WHEN `daily` rebuilds after `weekly` read it and `max_lag` is `1d`, THEN `weekly` reports stale, `stale_inputs` `["daily"]`, 1 day after the rebuild.

clauses.subject: staleness-collected-run
clauses.statement: A waiting run whose manifest retention collected counts as committed before `t` minus `max_lag`.

clauses.subject: hold
clauses.statement: A hold records build id, placing principal and expiry; collection skips a held build, and a hold confers no other authority.

clauses.subject: manifest-section
clauses.statement: The manifest section carries `{contract_version, schema_fingerprint, build_id, build_started_at, last_built_at, watermark, max_lag, last_build_status, withheld_cells, disclosure_digest, partitions_failed?, semantics_version?, fingerprint_recipe?}` of the newest publishing build; `watermark` follows {{run.model.watermark}}.

clauses.subject: semantics-version
clauses.statement: `semantics_version` advances when the engine adds an injected column, and `fingerprint_recipe` names the fingerprint's inputs, that column included.

clauses.subject: disclosure-digest
clauses.statement: A build records a digest over its table's declared `class`, `policy` and `visibility`, sorting set-valued fields. The manifest and build log carry the digest. Any declaration sets `withheld_cells`.

clauses.subject: required-key
clauses.statement: Missing or blank `source_table` or `parent_id_column` raises `DeriveConfigKeyMissing`, naming the key and pipeline. For built-in tasks, missing or blank `engine` or `media_column` raises the same error.

clauses.subject: no-store-root
clauses.statement: A source built without a store root or without its pipeline id raises `DeriveNoStoreRoot`, naming which is absent.

clauses.subject: foreign-output-table
clauses.statement: The anti-join's pipeline id comes from the build alone; a config key naming another pipeline's output raises `DeriveForeignOutputTable`.

clauses.subject: rows-per-run
clauses.statement: `max_rows_per_run` truncates the outstanding list after the anti-join, at 25 rows by default; zero or below resolves to that default.

clauses.subject: attempts-per-unit
clauses.statement: `max_attempts` defaults to 3 attempts per unit. A non-positive value selects that default.

clauses.subject: seconds-per-run
clauses.statement: `max_seconds_per_run` bounds the serial unit loop at 300 s by default for `link_preview` and carries no default for `transcribe`.

clauses.subject: incomplete-unit
clauses.statement: If a parent row's key or media column is null, empty or whitespace, the derive source raises `DeriveUnitIncomplete`. The derive source skips the row and counts the row on the run record.

clauses.subject: journaled-pull
clauses.statement: A derive pipeline configured to journal its pulls raises `DeriveJournaledPull`.

clauses.subject: unmetered-grant
clauses.statement: A derive pipeline declaring a shared-quota grant for any task other than `link_preview` raises `DeriveUnmeteredGrant`.

clauses.subject: metered-client
clauses.statement: A `link_preview` pipeline opening a socket outside the mediated client raises `DeriveMeteredClient`; every request it makes enters the run's request ledger.

clauses.subject: anti-join
clauses.statement: Each tick recomputes the outstanding set: every parent row holding neither a passage nor a settled marker under its current {{run.emit.derivation-key}} in the pipeline's own output table, or, for a host task, its marker table.

clauses.subject: unit-parents
clauses.statement: A host task reads each joined table once after selection and before processing its first unit. Each unit carries every row whose join-column value equals that unit's key. Rows landed after that read are absent.

clauses.subject: join-keyed
clauses.statement: A task reads joined tables declaring `primary_key` through {{store.declare.dedup-view}}. Each unit joins one surviving row per key, excluding superseded versions.
clauses.why: because a raw file read hands a re-landed row in both versions, and the admitted read hands one

clauses.subject: join-absent
clauses.statement: A joined table the store holds no schema for fails the tick with a `Config` failure, settling no unit, so the next tick selects every unit again.
clauses.why: because an absent table read as empty settles each unit `ok` on a partial join that the anti-join never revisits

clauses.subject: latest-marker
clauses.statement: A unit's state under a key comes from its latest marker ordered by `_ingested_at`, `_run_id` and `_row_seq`. The highest attempt count does not determine that state.
clauses.why: because an `empty` marker records 1 attempt, so ranking by count lets an older retry revive a settled unit

clauses.subject: key-change
clauses.statement: Rows under the current key landed before the unit's latest `ok` or `empty` landing under another key count for nothing, so a key changed and changed back derives the unit again.

clauses.subject: derive-order
clauses.statement: A derive pipeline reading another derive pipeline's output table runs after that parent on the parent's tick, regardless of declaration order or its own schedule.
scenarios: WHEN configuration declares a scheduled child before its parent and the child reads the parent's output, THEN the parent's tick lands its new row before the child reads it.

clauses.subject: derive-failed-parent
clauses.statement: A child derive pipeline runs after its parent fails and reads only the parent's committed rows.
scenarios: WHEN a parent fails after earlier rows committed, THEN its child reads those committed rows in the same tick.

clauses.subject: parent-outcome
clauses.statement: A derived child starts only after its parent produces a completed run outcome; a local launch, wait or signal failure, or a worker dispatch error, stops the unit before that child starts.
scenarios: WHEN the parent process fails to start, THEN its derived child does not start in that unit.

clauses.subject: derive-cycle
clauses.statement: A build whose derive source-table dependencies return to a pipeline raises `DeriveCycle`, names every pipeline on the cycle and arms none.
scenarios: WHEN two derive pipelines read each other's output tables, THEN the build raises `DeriveCycle` naming both; a self-reference names itself.

clauses.subject: derive-after-conflict
clauses.statement: A derive child whose `after` names a pipeline other than its source-table parent raises `DeriveAfterConflict` and arms none.
scenarios: WHEN a derive child names another pipeline in `after`, THEN the build raises `DeriveAfterConflict` naming the child and both parents.

clauses.subject: parent-scan
clauses.statement: The derive source scans parent tables of at most 1000000 rows in memory. For larger tables, the source streams through the read engine in batches, holding one batch in memory.

clauses.subject: dry-run
clauses.statement: `pipeline run --dry-run` on a derive pipeline prints its eligible, already-derived and outstanding unit counts from one selection, calling no engine and landing no row.

clauses.subject: available-select
clauses.statement: A derive run carrying `available_as_of` selects only parent rows {{store.available-time.available-as-of}} admits at that bound, and each derived row lands its parent row's availability instant.
clauses.why: because content derived from a later source record otherwise answers an earlier horizon

clauses.subject: unbound-engine
clauses.statement: An engine with no `[derive.<name>]` block raises `DeriveEngineUnbound`, naming the pipeline, the engine, the file to edit and every bound engine.

clauses.subject: command-in-manifest
clauses.statement: `command`, `preprocess`, `env` or `allow_hosts` inside `[pipeline.source.config]` raises `DeriveCommandInManifest`.

clauses.subject: unknown-task
clauses.statement: `task` names `transcribe`, the default, `link_preview`, or a task the embedding binary registered; any other value raises `DeriveUnknownTask`, listing the built-in and registered names.

clauses.subject: host-task
clauses.statement: An embedding binary registers each compiled derive task by name before build. Configuration selects that registered name without supplying a command. A duplicate built-in or registered task name raises `DeriveTaskNameTaken`.

clauses.subject: join-repeated
clauses.statement: A host task whose joins name one table twice raises `DeriveJoinRepeated` at registration.
clauses.why: because a unit holds one joined list per table, so the second join's rows replace the first's

clauses.subject: driver-mismatch
clauses.statement: `driver` is `exec` or `"none"` behind `transcribe` and `fetch` behind `link_preview`, and a host task names no `engine`; any other pairing raises `DeriveDriverMismatch`.

clauses.subject: endpoint-host-bare
clauses.statement: An `endpoint_host` carrying a path, query, port or scheme raises `DeriveEndpointHostNotBare`.

clauses.subject: remote-url-unsupported
clauses.statement: An `http` or `https` media value for an engine declining remote addresses raises `DeriveRemoteUrlUnsupported`, naming the `when = "media_is_url"` preprocess step.

clauses.subject: media-unreadable
clauses.statement: A media value that is neither an address nor a readable local file raises `DeriveMediaUnreadable`, failing that unit alone.

clauses.subject: media-root
clauses.statement: The engine canonicalizes local media paths under the binding's `media_root` ({{store.init.declaration-base}}), defaulting to that declaration base. A path outside the root raises `DeriveMediaOutsideRoot` and fails only that unit.
clauses.why: because a parent row is third-party data, and an unconfined path reads any file the machine's user can

clauses.subject: confidence-range
clauses.statement: A `confidence` outside `0.0..=1.0` after adapter normalization raises `DeriveConfidenceOutOfRange` and lands null.

clauses.subject: upstream-excerpt
clauses.statement: An `Upstream` excerpt holds at most 4 KiB and no request body.

clauses.subject: engine-unavailable
clauses.statement: If a transcriber returns `EngineUnavailable`, the run ends. If a `LinkReader` returns `EngineUnavailable`, the derive source raises `DeriveLinkEngineUnavailable` and fails only that unit.

clauses.subject: advisory-zone
clauses.statement: A row zone taken from the binding's advisory `zone` key raises `DeriveAdvisoryZone`.

clauses.subject: locality-wider
clauses.statement: An engine whose declared locality is wider than the zones its source table admits raises `DeriveLocalityWider` at build, naming the engine, its locality and the table.
clauses.why: because a derived passage carries its parent's content, and an engine outside the parent's zones moves that content where the parent cannot go

clauses.subject: shell-command
clauses.statement: The executor runs `command` as an argument array without a shell. A string-valued `command` raises `DeriveShellCommand`.

clauses.subject: env-name
clauses.statement: An allowlist name that is not ASCII alphanumeric or underscore, or that leads with a digit, raises `DeriveEnvNameInvalid`.

clauses.subject: chain-deadline
clauses.statement: `timeout_secs` bounds one unit's whole chain at 1800 s by default.

clauses.subject: captured-output
clauses.statement: `max_output_bytes` bounds each step's captured standard output and error at 8 MiB by default.

clauses.subject: audit-entries
clauses.statement: A chain contributes at most 64 entries of captured output to the run record.

clauses.subject: step-error-excerpt
clauses.statement: A failing step's error text carries at most 4 KiB of its standard error.

clauses.subject: non-zero-exit
clauses.statement: A step exiting non-zero raises `DeriveStepExit` carrying its bounded error text into the run audit.

clauses.subject: deadline-elapsed
clauses.statement: If a chain exceeds its deadline, the executor raises `DeriveStepTimeout`, naming the running step.

clauses.subject: output-cap
clauses.statement: The executor counts and discards output past the bound without buffering. Crossing the bound kills the step and raises `DeriveOutputCap` with the byte count. The executor continues draining so the child does not block.

clauses.subject: silent-step
clauses.statement: A preprocess step exiting zero without writing its output file raises `DeriveStepProducedNothing`.

clauses.subject: missing-binary
clauses.statement: A `command[0]` that is not an executable file on this machine raises `DeriveBinaryMissing`, naming the binary and the step.

clauses.subject: unpinned-path
clauses.statement: A path-form `command[0]` without `sha256` raises `DeriveUnpinnedPath`, quoting the computed digest. A bare search-path name carries no digest.

clauses.subject: digest-mismatch
clauses.statement: A pinned file whose bytes differ from its recorded digest raises `DeriveDigestMismatch`.

clauses.subject: no-shell
clauses.statement: A step runs as its argument array with no shell, in a process group of its own, under a cleared environment holding only the binding's `env` table.

clauses.subject: step-condition
clauses.statement: A preprocess step runs only while its `when` holds: `media_is_url` for an `http` or `https` input, `engine_requires_pcm16_wav` for an input other than 16-bit PCM WAV; another name raises `DeriveStepConditionUnknown`.
clauses.why: because a misspelled condition otherwise skips or runs its step silently

clauses.subject: verified-spawn
clauses.statement: Before each spawn, the executor re-reads the step's binary and compares its bytes with the digest resolved at run start. A mismatch follows {{run.exec.digest-mismatch}}; matching bytes permit execution.

clauses.subject: engine-id
clauses.statement: An `exec` engine id reads `exec:<name>@<prefix>`, the prefix being 12 chars of lowercase hex over every step's binary digest and arguments.

clauses.subject: vendor-deadline
clauses.statement: A vendor engine, a binding naming an `endpoint_host`, holds `request_timeout_secs` as its engine step's deadline, clipped to the time {{run.exec.chain-deadline}} leaves, so a stalled vendor fails its unit before the chain elapses.
clauses.why: because a chain deadline alone lets one stalled vendor call spend the unit's whole budget with no step to name

clauses.subject: scheme
clauses.statement: An address whose scheme is neither `http` nor `https` raises `DeriveSchemeUnsupported` before any socket opens.

clauses.subject: address-literal
clauses.statement: A host written as an address literal raises `DeriveAddressLiteral`.

clauses.subject: redirect-chain
clauses.statement: A redirect chain runs to at most 5 hops.

clauses.subject: binding-key
clauses.statement: `env`, `preprocess`, `engine` or `max_output_bytes` on a fetch binding raises `DeriveFetchBindingKey`, naming the key.
clauses.why: because a silently ignored key leaves an operator believing a fetch carries a credential or runs a process

clauses.subject: document-prefix
clauses.statement: `max_document_bytes` bounds the scanned document prefix at 1 MiB by default, dropping the remainder.

clauses.subject: probe-prefix
clauses.statement: `max_probe_bytes` bounds one picture range request at 64 KiB by default.

clauses.subject: hop-timeout
clauses.statement: `request_timeout_secs` bounds one hop at 20 s by default.

clauses.subject: retry-after-default
clauses.statement: A `429` without a usable `Retry-After` maps to `RateLimited` carrying 60 s.

clauses.subject: charset
clauses.statement: A declared character set other than UTF-8 raises `DeriveCharsetUnsupported`, naming the value.

clauses.subject: not-utf8
clauses.statement: If a document declares no character set and fails UTF-8 validation, the fetch driver raises `DeriveBytesNotUtf8`. The validator tolerates a character split at the byte bound.

clauses.subject: head-rows
clauses.statement: A link preview lands one passage for non-empty head title or description and one passage per distinct advertised head image, each carrying the scrubbed page URL and each image its probe status.
clauses.why: because the head and its image claims remain separately citable, including an image whose probe fails
scenarios: WHEN a page head declares a title, description and one image, THEN the output holds one text passage and one image passage with its probe status.

clauses.subject: failure-off-table
clauses.statement: Per-unit failure state recorded outside the output table raises `DeriveFailureOffTable`.

clauses.subject: unit-status
clauses.statement: `unit_status` is `ok`, `empty` where the engine established nothing to derive, `unavailable` where it returned nothing and stated no reason, or `failed` on a typed error; any other value raises `DeriveUnitStatusUnknown`.

clauses.subject: reserved-discriminator
clauses.statement: A derive table declaring a column named `kind` raises `DeriveReservedDiscriminator`.

clauses.subject: settled-revived
clauses.statement: A unit that settles under its current key while a tick derives it raises `DeriveSettledUnitRevived`, and that tick lands none of its rows; a changed key revives nothing.

clauses.subject: attempts
clauses.statement: `attempts` is the prior count under the row's key plus one; `unavailable` and `failed` stop at {{run.select.attempts-per-unit}}, and `empty` receives 1 attempts in total.

clauses.subject: unredacted-error
clauses.statement: A non-null `last_error` write that has not passed address redaction raises `DeriveUnredactedError`.

clauses.subject: primary-key
clauses.statement: A derive output table or host marker table without `primary_key` `["unit_ref", "derivation_key", "cue_seq"]`, or a host content table whose key does not open with `unit_ref` and `derivation_key`, raises `DerivePrimaryKeyMissing`.
clauses.why: because a re-derived unit otherwise lands its new passages over the originals, or beside them with no key telling them apart

clauses.subject: derivation-key
clauses.statement: Every passage and marker row carries `derivation_key`: lowercase hex SHA-256 over the engine id, the binding less its bounds and `zone`, the output table's declared columns, and the parent row's id, media value and `derivation_key`.

clauses.subject: stale-supersedes
clauses.statement: A unit's latest `ok` or `empty` landing supersedes rows landed earlier under another key. Those rows answer until that landing. The next fold drops the superseded rows and rebuilds the table's sidecars without them.

clauses.subject: task-version
clauses.statement: A host task's `derivation_key` hashes its registered name, its `task_version` and the parent row's id, declared columns and `derivation_key`, so raising the version re-selects every settled unit.

clauses.subject: host-rows
clauses.statement: A host task's content row carries its unit's `unit_ref`, `derivation_key` and `task_version`, `kind` `passage` and `unit_status` `ok`; every unit lands one marker, `ok` over content rows, `empty` over none.

clauses.subject: content-empty
clauses.statement: A host unit landing no row in a content table lands one `kind` `marker`, `unit_status` `empty` row there under its key, so {{run.emit.stale-supersedes}} holds in every content table.
clauses.why: because a read and a fold supersede from one table's rows alone, so a content table never seeing the unit's newest key keeps its stale rows answering

clauses.subject: content-marker-retention-clock
clauses.statement: A generated host marker copies a custom {{store.declare.retain-rows}} timestamp from the parent row when the parent carries a same-named column.
clauses.why: because a generated empty marker must carry the declared clock before the content table accepts its landing

clauses.subject: output-tables
clauses.statement: A host-task pipeline declares exactly its task's marker and content tables, and a unit returns rows for its content tables alone; either breach raises `DeriveOutputTablesMismatch`, the second failing that unit alone.

clauses.subject: marker-last
clauses.statement: A host-task run commits each content table under its own commit, then the marker table, and a content table failing stops the fire before its marker lands, so the unit re-runs and its rows collapse by key.

clauses.subject: version-retained
clauses.statement: On an output table declaring `retain_versions`, {{run.emit.stale-supersedes}} holds per unit and `task_version`, so rows under an earlier task version stay current under that version beside the newer version's rows.

clauses.subject: marker-row
clauses.statement: A unit yielding no passage lands one marker row, `cue_seq` -1 and `kind` `marker`, carrying its status, attempts, last error and whether it retries.

clauses.subject: empty-document
clauses.statement: Only a WebVTT document whose blocks are its header, notes and styles establishes nothing to derive; empty output, or blocks none of which parse, lands `unavailable`.

clauses.subject: canceled-unit
clauses.statement: A unit whose chain a run stop interrupts lands no row and charges no attempt; the pull ends `Canceled` once {{run.cancel.child-reaped}}.

clauses.subject: output-modality
clauses.statement: A text passage extracted from a video parent carries `_modality` `text`, and an advertised image passage carries `image`, each under {{store.reserve.modality}}.
scenarios: WHEN a video parent yields a transcript passage and an advertised picture, THEN their output modalities are `text` and `image`.

clauses.subject: local-content-key
clauses.statement: A local media unit's {{run.emit.derivation-key}} includes a SHA-256 digest of canonical file bytes, so changed bytes under an unchanged path reselect the unit.
scenarios: WHEN a local file changes bytes under the same path, THEN the next tick selects its unit under another key.

clauses.subject: parent-tombstone
clauses.statement: A fold drops derived rows whose parent key is absent or tombstoned in the parent table, then rebuilds their sidecars.
scenarios: WHEN a parent row is tombstoned, THEN the next fold drops its passages and rebuilds the affected sidecars.

clauses.subject: derived-id
