clauses.statement: Every passage and marker row keyed as {{run.emit.primary-key}} carries `derived_id`, lowercase hex SHA-256 over its `unit_ref`, `derivation_key` and `cue_seq`, and a sidecar over such a table defaults its `id_column` to `derived_id`.
clauses.why: because a sidecar re-joins on one column, and a producer column outside the reserved underscore namespace needs no store change

clauses.subject: backward-cue
clauses.statement: If a block starts before the last accepted block, the caption parser raises `DeriveCueOutOfOrder` and drops the block.

clauses.subject: passage-chars
clauses.statement: A passage stays open while it holds fewer than 600 chars.

clauses.subject: passage-span
clauses.statement: A passage stays open while it spans less than 60 s.

clauses.subject: passage-bytes
clauses.statement: One passage's text holds at most 8 KiB.

clauses.subject: passages-per-document
clauses.statement: One document yields at most 2000 rows of passages.

clauses.subject: grammar
clauses.statement: SubRip and WebVTT read through one grammar: a block's timing line, then its text lines joined by a space.

clauses.subject: unsupported-driver
clauses.statement: A `fetch` engine named to the verb raises `DeriveTestEngineUnsupported`.
clauses.why: because the verb drives a transcriber over media, and a link engine takes no media

clauses.subject: authoring-path
clauses.statement: Every connector implements the same trait as either a sandboxed component or a native source compiled into the binary. Dispatch does not branch on these implementation forms.

clauses.subject: type-taxonomy
clauses.statement: The shared types interface carries a schema (name, fields, primary key) and a field (name, data type, nullability) over `boolean`, `int32`, `int64`, `float64`, `string`, `bytes`, `timestamp-millis` and `json`.

clauses.subject: batch-encoding
clauses.statement: A batch crosses the boundary as Arrow IPC bytes, and a position as opaque bytes beside a declared cursor kind.

clauses.subject: arrow-types
clauses.statement: The host reads Arrow `Binary` or `FixedSizeBinary` columns as bytes of that width and `FixedSizeList` of `Float32` or `Float16` as vectors. Each lands in its {{store.reconcile.binary-and-vector}} type without text conversion.

clauses.subject: nested-value
clauses.statement: The connector sends a nested value as `json`; normalization determines its type. The interface defines no recursive type.

clauses.subject: guaranteed-type
clauses.statement: A guest declares the type its parser guarantees: `int64` for a count, `float64` for money and a rate. An unreadable spelling lands as null instead of zero.
clauses.why: because a text column pushes a cast into every downstream read

clauses.subject: read-handle
clauses.statement: A source exports its cursor kind, discovery call and open call taking a table and optional position. The handle's `next` yields one batch or exhaustion; `position` reports the current position.

clauses.subject: write-handle
clauses.statement: A destination exports `prepare`, `write`, `commit` and `abort`. Source and destination are separate worlds sharing the types interface.

clauses.subject: optional-world
clauses.statement: Operator configuration and failure attribution each use an additional world interface. The host probes instances by interface name. A base-world guest instantiates unchanged; neither interface changes the world version.

clauses.subject: partition-attribution
clauses.statement: A guest exporting failure attribution answers with the byte-exact values of the outermost partition column a failed read belongs to. The host reads it on failure and success alike; an empty list keeps the unattributed refusal.
clauses.why: because a read holding one partition back and landing the rest returns success

clauses.subject: attribution-budget
clauses.statement: Failure attribution carries at most 512 entries per session, each value at most 512 B.

clauses.subject: shared-failure
clauses.statement: A read failing under `auth-expired`, or during which the host failed to hydrate or lease a credential, fails unattributed; the host discards the guest's failure attribution for that session.
clauses.why: because every attach binding is session-wide, so a credential failure belongs to every partition the read could reach
scenarios: WHEN an attributing guest fails a read with `auth-expired` while naming two partitions, THEN the session answers no failed partition and the read fails whole.
WHEN an attach header fails to hydrate during a read, THEN the session answers no failed partition and the read fails whole.

clauses.subject: native-read
clauses.statement: A native source reads a table from a position, returning batches each paired with the position after it. A source unable to bound a half-open chunk range falls back to the unbounded read.
clauses.why: because an overlapping read is recoverable and a mis-bounded chunk is not

clauses.subject: native-extra
clauses.statement: A native source may provide a content fingerprint from stat or HEAD without downloading, plus its connector identity, audit entries and a declared reason for unmetered vendor traffic.

clauses.subject: store-blindness
clauses.statement: A source receives credentials, limiter bindings, the run id, the request ledger, the component pin and the incremental position, and no store handle. A store-driven run receives its query set as run parameters.

clauses.subject: world-authorship
clauses.statement: The host generates bindings from its template, the input specification and connector name. Connector authors write only method bodies: authentication, paging and the cursor-kind declaration.

clauses.subject: three-imports
clauses.statement: Both worlds import the WASI 0.2 outgoing HTTP and wall-clock interfaces and the logging interface, and nothing else; every export is a synchronous call. There is no filesystem import and no socket import.

clauses.subject: empty-context
clauses.statement: A guest standard library pulling broader interfaces links against an empty context: no preopens, no environment, no arguments.

clauses.subject: wait-primitive
clauses.statement: Neither world carries a monotonic clock or a sleep primitive, so a guest holds no call open across a wait.

clauses.subject: forwarded-config
clauses.statement: The pipeline's guest configuration table is the one part of the source configuration crossing inward, as one JSON object delivered once per session ahead of discovery.

clauses.subject: config-shape
clauses.statement: Ahead of any I/O, a guest configuration value that is not a table, a serialization over 64 KiB, or a credential or environment reference inside it raises `ConnectorConfigRejected`.

clauses.subject: config-unclaimed
clauses.statement: Where the artifact is local and probed, a guest table declared against a guest exporting no configuration interface raises `ConnectorConfigUnclaimed`.

clauses.subject: unusable-key
clauses.statement: A guest raises a permanent failure for an unsupported configuration key or value.

clauses.subject: config-hashing
clauses.statement: The forwarded table folds into the connector's content hash; with no table forwarded, the artifact digest is that hash verbatim.

clauses.subject: declared-grant
clauses.statement: A manifest lists required outbound hosts and wall-clock access. The host decides the access grant at load. The connector requests no additional permission at run time and has no escalation path.

clauses.subject: undeclared-access
clauses.statement: A connector reaching for access its manifest does not list fails to load, raising `ConnectorUndeclaredAccess` naming that access.
scenarios: WHEN a component importing `wasi:clocks/wall-clock` loads under a manifest without `clock = true`, THEN the load raises `ConnectorUndeclaredAccess` naming the interface and writes no run row.

clauses.subject: host-allowlist
clauses.statement: The outbound allowlist holds exact hosts and subdomain wildcards matched as suffixes; a wildcard entry covers subdomains and not the apex.

clauses.subject: allowlist-shape
clauses.statement: An empty allowlist, a bare wildcard, an empty entry, and an entry carrying a scheme, port or path raise `ConnectorAllowlistRejected`.

clauses.subject: environment-name
clauses.statement: A declared environment name is a name, not ambient access: the operator binds it to a reference and the host resolves and injects the value at call time. No connector reads the process environment.

clauses.subject: ambient-authority
clauses.statement: No credential is a property of the process: no shared client carries a default header and no import returns secret bytes. Every grant binds to one declared host and attaches at request time.

clauses.subject: scope-probe
clauses.statement: A manifest may declare an identity endpoint, the response header carrying granted scopes, and the grant it expects. The host calls it with the bound credential ahead of the first read.
scenarios: WHEN the identity endpoint grants a scope outside the manifest's expectation, THEN the session refuses before discovery and the vendor receives no request.

clauses.subject: probe-transport
clauses.statement: The scope probe's host sits on the allowlist and its scheme is TLS or loopback.

clauses.subject: probe-shape
clauses.statement: A scope probe declaring an empty scopes header or a header outside HTTP field-name token syntax raises `ConnectorScopeProbeRejected`.
clauses.why: because a header no response can carry refuses every session as though the vendor withheld the grant

clauses.subject: scope-exceeded
clauses.statement: A granted scope outside the declared expectation, compared byte for byte, raises `ConnectorScopeExceeded`, and the session does not open.

clauses.subject: scope-unverified
clauses.statement: A probe response carrying no granted-scopes header, or one naming no scope or holding a byte outside visible ASCII, raises `ConnectorScopeUnverified`.

clauses.subject: environment-binding
clauses.statement: A source key binds from the environment as `<key>_from = "env:<NAME>"`. The engine enumerates the bindable keys in one place, each with its value shape: a scalar or a comma-separated list.

clauses.subject: binding-unsupported
clauses.statement: A `_from` binding on a key the connector does not read raises `ConnectorBindingUnsupported`.

clauses.subject: binding-unbound
clauses.statement: A bound key the environment did not supply, or supplied off its declared shape, raises `ConnectorBindingUnbound` at preflight.

clauses.subject: comparison
clauses.statement: Reload compares the candidate's complete declared grant with the admitted manifest for the same connector identity before publishing the candidate; validation under {{connector.declare-capability.allowlist-shape}} precedes comparison.

clauses.subject: dimensions
clauses.statement: The comparison covers outbound hosts, environment names, expected credential scopes and wall-clock access; names and scopes compare byte for byte, and enabling the clock widens its Boolean grant.

clauses.subject: host-inclusion
clauses.statement: Host inclusion succeeds when every candidate entry has a covering predecessor entry under {{connector.declare-capability.host-allowlist}}. Success admits no host the predecessor refuses.
scenarios: WHEN `*.eu.example.com` replaces `*.example.com`, THEN host inclusion succeeds.

clauses.subject: host-witness
clauses.statement: Every reported host witness passes the candidate's outbound matcher and fails the predecessor's outbound matcher.
scenarios: WHEN `*.example.com` replaces `x.example.com`, THEN a host witness differs from the already admitted exact host.

clauses.subject: unresolved
clauses.statement: A comparison establishing neither inclusion nor a replayed witness raises `ConnectorWidenUnresolved`, naming the dimension and reason; reload retains the admitted manifest.

clauses.subject: approval-required
clauses.statement: Additional access without a matching operator approval raises `ConnectorWidenApprovalRequired`, carrying a witness for each widened dimension; reload retains the admitted manifest.
scenarios: WHEN a candidate adds environment name `REPORT_TOKEN` without operator approval, THEN reload retains the admitted manifest and names that environment access.

clauses.subject: approval-binding
clauses.statement: An approval records the authenticated operator, connector identity and both complete manifest digests; publication atomically checks the admitted digest and applies only that candidate, preserving {{run.own.admission-pin}}.
scenarios: WHEN the admitted digest changes after review, THEN the approval does not match the new comparison.

clauses.subject: narrowing
clauses.statement: A candidate included in the admitted grant needs no widening approval; comparison grants no exemption from other load checks.

clauses.subject: limiter-declaration
clauses.statement: A connector declares a limiter capability naming the shared vendor quota, the traffic class of its requests, and the vendor quota-state response headers to forward.

clauses.subject: forward-credential
clauses.statement: A limiter declaration forwarding `authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `cookie` or `set-cookie` raises `ConnectorForwardRejected` at load.
clauses.why: because the report carries forwarded headers verbatim to a party outside the vendor credential's scope

clauses.subject: limiter-binding
clauses.statement: The operator binds that quota name to an endpoint, a bearer token held by reference, and a permit batch size.

clauses.subject: quota-unbound
clauses.statement: A declared quota with no binding raises `ConnectorQuotaUnbound` at load.

clauses.subject: binding-transport
clauses.statement: A limiter endpoint that is neither HTTPS nor loopback or carries a query, fragment or userinfo, and a limiter token that is not a `secret://` reference, raise `ConnectorLimiterBindingRejected` at load.

clauses.subject: limiter-address
clauses.statement: A limiter endpoint may resolve to a private or loopback address; the engine's check of vendor-host addresses does not apply to it.
clauses.why: because the operator authors the limiter endpoint and no vendor answer supplies it

clauses.subject: reservation-point
clauses.statement: The host reserves at the mediation point, the guest's outgoing-HTTP import or the engine's shared client. One permit covers one outbound request.
clauses.why: because one call issues any number of requests for paging, retries and token refresh

clauses.subject: permit-batch
clauses.statement: An acquire may grant a batch of permits under a short TTL. Each request spends one, and the next report surrenders the unspent.

clauses.subject: acquire
clauses.statement: Acquire is an authenticated POST of quota, class and permit count, answered granted with permits and a TTL, or denied with a retry-after. A bare `429` with `Retry-After`, and a zero-permit grant, read as denials.

clauses.subject: acquire-call
clauses.statement: Each limiter call takes at most 5 s. A reservation does not sleep: denial returns `RateLimited` without waiting. The run's retry schedule performs the specified wait.

clauses.subject: unreadable-answer
clauses.statement: An unreadable limiter response raises `ConnectorLimiterUnreadable` and grants no permits.

clauses.subject: denial-ceiling
clauses.statement: A limiter wait, whether a retry-after or a zero-permit grant's TTL, reads as at most the ceiling of {{run.retry.retry-after}}.
clauses.why: because an unbounded wait named by the limiter parks the run past any retry its schedule allows

clauses.subject: report
clauses.statement: Report is an authenticated POST of quota, class, granted, spent, one entry per vendor response (status, retry-after, verbatim headers), an observation instant and the run id.

clauses.subject: report-delivery
clauses.statement: The run delivers reports at least once with bounded backoff and makes one delivery attempt before each refill. An undelivered report accompanies the next. The run audits a report that remains undelivered without failing anything.

clauses.subject: unmetered-request
clauses.statement: Under a declared limiter, a vendor request without a granted reservation raises `ConnectorUnmetered`, including for an unreachable, unbound or failing limiter. These failures do not indicate expired vendor credentials.

clauses.subject: allowlist-precedence
clauses.statement: A request the allowlist refuses reaches no limiter and spends no permit.

clauses.subject: pre-send-hook
clauses.statement: Each outbound hop passes one pre-send hook after the allowlist and before name resolution, carrying the hop's intent: method, scrubbed URL, host, port, traffic class, run id and request body bytes.

clauses.subject: hook-composition
clauses.statement: The limiter reservation is the hook's innermost implementation. An operator hook composes in front of it, so a request the operator hook refuses makes no limiter call and spends no permit.

clauses.subject: hook-refusal
clauses.statement: A hook refusing an intent raises `ConnectorEgressRefused`, naming the host and reason. The host resolves no name, and the retry schedule does not retry the request.

clauses.subject: hook-settle
clauses.statement: The hook receives each admitted hop's outcome after the body read or the failure: the status or transport failure, the request body bytes sent, and the response body bytes the host read. A followed redirect is two intents.

clauses.subject: held-back-request
clauses.statement: A guest swallowing a held-back request still fails its call, and a fault inside the reservation machinery fails the request rather than passing it unmetered.

clauses.subject: synthesized-throttle
clauses.statement: A denied reservation returns to the guest as a synthesized `429` carrying the retry-after. An unreachable limiter fails the request as a transport failure.
clauses.why: because a connector mapping vendor throttles needs no second interface

clauses.subject: replay-reservation
clauses.statement: Replay issues no outbound request and makes no limiter call.

clauses.subject: built-in-grant-absent
clauses.statement: A compiled-in source reaching an outside vendor declares its grant in the pipeline's source configuration; the build raises `ConnectorGrantMissing` without it.

clauses.subject: grant-unhonorable
clauses.statement: A declared grant on a compiled-in source that bypasses the mediated client raises `ConnectorGrantUnhonorable` at load.

clauses.subject: metered-disclosure
clauses.statement: Where the project binds any quota, every compiled-in read records whether it ran metered, the run record states an unmetered read once, and validation warns per pipeline naming the connector.

clauses.subject: counting-not-pricing
clauses.statement: The limiter counts requests and prices none.

clauses.subject: model-endpoint
clauses.statement: Every model call resolves to one operator-configured OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint declared as a capability. The host owns the credential, rate limit and span; the component owns the prompt template and response schema.

clauses.subject: mediated-call
clauses.statement: A model call sends through the mediated client under {{connector.attach.mediation-covers-every-egress}}, its allowlist the configured endpoint host alone, and passes {{connector.meter.pre-send-hook}} like a vendor hop.

clauses.subject: vendor-sdk
clauses.statement: The workspace rejects a model-vendor SDK in any Rust crate under {{topology.compose.vendor-sdk}}. Changing providers requires only a URL edit.

clauses.subject: data-fence
clauses.statement: No ingested value reaches a model outside a data boundary: marker pairs whose opening marker carries the value's provenance label, a preamble declaring the blocks data, and a closing line restating the caller's rules.

clauses.subject: fence-is-not-a-boundary
clauses.statement: The fence lowers the success rate of injected instructions and bounds nothing. No clause treats the output of a fenced call as trusted.
clauses.why: because spotlighting reduces injection and guarantees nothing

clauses.subject: output-taint
clauses.statement: Model output carries the least-trusted provenance label among its fenced inputs, and lands under that label.
clauses.why: because output re-landing as fresh data launders injected text

clauses.subject: provenance-order
clauses.statement: Provenance labels order by trust: `operator` above `ingested:first-party` above `ingested:third-party`. A call fencing no value carries `operator`.
clauses.why: because the least-trusted input is defined only over a total order, and a call fencing nothing sends the operator's template alone

clauses.subject: marker-derivation
clauses.statement: Every marker of one call carries one token of 16 B, derived from every label and value the call fences, as fenced.
clauses.why: because closing one's own block then requires content containing the digest of a batch that contains it

clauses.subject: replay
clauses.statement: The same values, labels, cap and rules fence to the same bytes, and a change to any value or label moves the token.
clauses.why: because a replayed call sends an identical prompt, and a token read from one batch closes no other

clauses.subject: fenced-value-hygiene
clauses.statement: Fencing removes control characters other than newline and tab from a value.

clauses.subject: value-cap
clauses.statement: A value past its declared character cap keeps its first cap characters followed by a truncation mark, and the closing line still follows its block.

clauses.subject: label-hygiene
clauses.statement: Fencing truncates a provenance label at 200 chars and flattens the label to one line without brackets. The label opens or closes no block.
clauses.why: because a label is built from connector-supplied table names and row ids

clauses.subject: empty-batch
clauses.statement: A call fencing no value renders an explicit no-data line instead of an empty section.

clauses.subject: operator-template
clauses.statement: The operator's prompt template stays unfenced in the system role. The idempotency hash covers the template alone.
clauses.why: because hardening the fence leaves a dedup key intact

clauses.subject: cutoffs
clauses.statement: A model reference carries a pinned snapshot id and pre-training and post-training cutoffs, each tagged `documented` or `estimated`. An undeclared cutoff compares as the call's own instant.
clauses.why: because tuning adds knowledge after pre-training, and an estimated cutoff often falls before the reported one
scenarios: WHEN a model reference carries a pre-training cutoff and no post-training cutoff, THEN the post-training cutoff compares as the call's own instant.

clauses.subject: logprobs
clauses.statement: A call to an endpoint exposing token log-probabilities lands them with the call record.
clauses.why: because probe-based leakage estimates read first-token probabilities
scenarios: WHEN an endpoint returns token log-probabilities, THEN the call record carries them beside the response.

clauses.subject: usage
clauses.statement: A call record carries the input and output token counts of the endpoint's `usage` beside the content; an answer without them records none.
clauses.why: because server-run evaluation prices every model call from its usage, failed attempts included

clauses.subject: model-span
clauses.statement: A traced call records one client span under the caller's span: `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.response.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `server.address` and, on failure, `error.type`. The span excludes message content. The request's `traceparent` names this span.

clauses.subject: hosted-tools
clauses.statement: A model call under a credential carrying {{authority.grant.horizon}} that declares a provider-hosted tool, such as search, browse or fetch, raises `InferHostedToolUnderHorizon`, naming the tool, before any byte leaves.
clauses.why: because search inside the provider never reaches the mediated client, so no hook sees it

clauses.subject: distribution-form
clauses.statement: A connector resolves in one of four forms: in-tree by name, a project-local artifact path, an HTTPS URL, or an OCI reference.

clauses.subject: remote-transport
clauses.statement: HTTPS artifact, OCI manifest and OCI layer requests pass through the mediated client with only the reference's authority admitted, under {{connector.attach.transport-port}}, before {{connector.package.digest-mismatch}}.
scenarios: WHEN the host fetches a pinned HTTPS or OCI artifact, THEN the mediated client admits only the reference authority before compilation.

clauses.subject: oci-reference
clauses.statement: An OCI artifact reference is `oci://<registry>/<repository>[:<tag>|@sha256:<digest>]`, with `latest` for an absent selector; an empty registry, repository or selector raises `ConnectorOciReferenceInvalid` before network access.
clauses.why: because a malformed reference must not turn a registry name into an unintended request destination
scenarios: WHEN an OCI reference has an empty repository, THEN validation raises `ConnectorOciReferenceInvalid` without a request.

clauses.subject: oci-component-layer
clauses.statement: An OCI reference resolves a schema-2 image manifest with exactly one layer, whose media type is `application/vnd.wasm.content.layer.v1+wasm`; another shape raises `ConnectorOciArtifactUnsupported` before any component compiles.
scenarios: WHEN an OCI manifest has two component layers, THEN the run raises `ConnectorOciArtifactUnsupported` before compilation.

clauses.subject: oci-layer-integrity
clauses.statement: The fetched OCI layer matches its manifest descriptor's SHA-256 digest and the source pin under {{connector.package.digest-mismatch}}; a descriptor mismatch raises `ConnectorOciLayerMismatch` before cache publication.
scenarios: WHEN the layer bytes disagree with the manifest descriptor, THEN the run raises `ConnectorOciLayerMismatch` and caches nothing.

clauses.subject: oci-registry-bearer
clauses.statement: An optional `config.toml` `[connector.registry."<authority>"] authorization = "Bearer ${secret://<name>}"` binds one OCI registry authority; hydration reaches manifest and layer requests alone under {{connector.resolve.hydration-is-just-in-time}}.
scenarios: WHEN the registry requires a bearer, THEN manifest and layer requests carry its resolved binding while guest requests do not.

clauses.subject: remote-cache
clauses.statement: A remote artifact admitted under {{connector.package.digest-mismatch}} enters the project cache at `.contextful/artifacts/sha256/<digest>` atomically; a later fire reads matching cached bytes before any network request.
scenarios: WHEN a second fire names a cached pin, THEN it loads matching bytes without a registry or HTTPS request.

clauses.subject: remote-cache-corrupt
clauses.statement: Cached artifact bytes whose SHA-256 differs from their cache key raise `ConnectorArtifactCacheCorrupt`; the host neither fetches a replacement nor compiles those bytes.
clauses.why: because a replay must refuse when its recorded artifact bytes are damaged
scenarios: WHEN cached bytes disagree with their key, THEN the run raises `ConnectorArtifactCacheCorrupt` without fetching or compiling.

clauses.subject: remote-fetch-failure
clauses.statement: If fetching a remote artifact's manifest or bytes fails, the host raises `ConnectorArtifactFetchFailed`, naming the scrubbed reference. The host writes no run row and compiles no component.
clauses.why: because a failed installation cannot be mistaken for a source returning no rows
scenarios: WHEN a remote endpoint refuses a required fetch, THEN the run raises `ConnectorArtifactFetchFailed` and writes no run row.

clauses.subject: remote-unpinned
clauses.statement: A remote artifact carrying no 64-hex content pin raises `ConnectorRemoteUnpinned` at parse.

clauses.subject: insecure-artifact
clauses.statement: A plain-HTTP artifact reference raises `ConnectorInsecureArtifact`.

clauses.subject: digest-mismatch
clauses.statement: The host re-hashes the resolved bytes and raises `ConnectorDigestMismatch` on a difference, before the bytes reach the engine.

clauses.subject: artifact-cache
clauses.statement: On Unix, after {{connector.package.digest-mismatch}} admission, the host caches precompiled components by artifact digest and engine compatibility hash; an intact host-written entry deserializes, while a missing, stale or altered entry recompiles.

clauses.subject: pin-requirement
clauses.statement: Either of two switches requires a local artifact pin: store-wide `[connector] require_pin` in the store's `config.toml`, or `require_wasm_pin` in the connector manifest.

clauses.subject: local-unpinned
clauses.statement: With either switch set, an unpinned local artifact raises `ConnectorLocalUnpinned` at build, carrying the digest of the bytes found.

clauses.subject: manifest-posture
clauses.statement: An adopted manifest carries a digest from the fixed builder platform. A template manifest carries a pin requirement and placeholder. The parser accepts a template; the loader refuses it.

clauses.subject: posture-undeclared
clauses.statement: A manifest carrying neither a digest nor both template markers raises `ConnectorPostureUndeclared` at merge.

clauses.subject: build-source
clauses.statement: A manifest's `build.source` is its only build input; the fixed builder platform holds image, target, compiler, package manager and command, and a `build.source` leaving the manifest directory refuses under {{connector.package.manifest-keys}}.
scenarios: WHEN a manifest declares `[build] source = "../guest"`, THEN `connector pin` raises `ConnectorManifestRejected` naming `build.source` and builds nothing.

clauses.subject: pin-verb
clauses.statement: `contextful connector pin <manifest>` builds the guest in a digest-pinned container on one fixed platform and writes the artifact and its digest. `--verify` rebuilds and compares without writing.

clauses.subject: host-built-pin
clauses.statement: `--local` builds with the host toolchain and prints a host-local digest; writing a pin from a host build raises `ConnectorHostPinRefused`.

clauses.subject: path-remap
clauses.statement: Every build remaps the source root and the package cache, so checkout location is not a digest input.

clauses.subject: native-verification
clauses.statement: `--verify --native` checks host triple, compiler and package manager against pinned constants and clears byte-moving configuration before building. A mismatch exits with a status distinct from digest drift.

clauses.subject: interpreted-target
clauses.statement: A host built with the `pulley` feature runs components on the interpreted target as portable bytecode, mapping no executable memory, under the same deadlines and mediated client; the compiled native target stays the default.
clauses.why: because a hardened runtime refusing writable-then-executable pages loads no compiled guest, and interpretation trades throughput for loading there

clauses.subject: interpreted-target-absent
clauses.statement: A host built without the `pulley` feature refuses the interpreted target at construction, naming the feature, before any component compiles.

clauses.subject: component-source
clauses.statement: A pipeline source named by an artifact path, HTTPS URL or OCI reference runs as a component, its config reading `sha256`, `allow`, `attach`, `guest`, `memory_bytes` and `manifest`.

clauses.subject: manifest-keys
clauses.statement: A component source's manifest reads only `name`, `version`, `world`, `wasm`, `wasm_sha256`, `require_wasm_pin`, `build`, and `capabilities` holding `allow_hosts`, `clock` and `scope_probe`. An absent manifest, another key at any depth, or a value off its shape raises `ConnectorManifestRejected` naming the key.
scenarios: WHEN a component source names no `manifest`, THEN validation raises `ConnectorManifestRejected` naming `manifest`.
WHEN a manifest declares `[capabilities.limiter]`, THEN the load raises `ConnectorManifestRejected` naming `capabilities.limiter`, and the guest performs no unmetered execution.

clauses.subject: manifest-pin
clauses.statement: A manifest's `wasm_sha256` pins the artifact its component source loads; a source `sha256` differing from it refuses under {{connector.package.manifest-keys}} before the artifact loads.
clauses.why: because one artifact admitted against two pins holds no single reviewed digest
scenarios: WHEN a manifest pins one digest and the component source's `sha256` another, THEN the load raises `ConnectorManifestRejected` naming `wasm_sha256` and writes no run row.

clauses.subject: manifest-host-grant
clauses.statement: A component source's `manifest` names a project-relative TOML file; at load, each `allow` host must fit its `[capabilities] allow_hosts` declaration or refuses under {{connector.declare-capability.undeclared-access}}, naming the excess host.
clauses.why: because an operator grant cannot extend past the connector's declared host access

clauses.subject: component-load
clauses.statement: `pipeline run` resolves a component source, admits it against its pin and loads it once per fire, before any run row, and records its {{connector.import.config-hashing}} content hash as each run's connector hash.

clauses.subject: component-grant
clauses.statement: A component session's grant is its declared `allow` hosts and `attach` headers alone, with credential attachment governed by {{connector.attach.per-request-hydration}}; a source declaring no `allow` reaches no host.

clauses.subject: component-validate
clauses.statement: `pipeline validate` resolves a local component artifact against the same directory as `pipeline run`, then loads it and runs discovery. Missing exports or world mismatches fail before runs. Validation checks remote artifacts without I/O.

clauses.subject: component-position
clauses.statement: `incremental` beside a component source raises `ConnectorPositionOwned` at validation; the guest's opaque cursor is the run's position.
clauses.why: because a watermark over one field replaces the cursor the guest resumes from, so its next read opens at a position it never reported

clauses.subject: component-target
clauses.statement: `pipeline run` and `pipeline validate` compile components for the interpreted target when `--component-target pulley` or `CONTEXTFUL_COMPONENT_TARGET=pulley` selects it; native stays the default.

clauses.subject: linear-memory
clauses.statement: A connector runs under 256 MiB of linear memory by default, raised per connector to at most 2 GiB.

clauses.subject: call-deadline
clauses.statement: A read call carries a 30 s wall-clock deadline and a discovery call a 60 s one, armed by epoch interruption at 100 ms granularity.

clauses.subject: session-budget
clauses.statement: A session carries a 1 MiB logging budget, dropping and counting messages past it, and holds at most 8 requests outbound at once.

clauses.subject: request-body
clauses.statement: A guest's outbound request body carries at most 8 MiB. The host stops reading past it and fails the call as a deterministic refusal before the request reaches the vendor.
clauses.why: because the body buffers in host memory, outside the guest's linear-memory cap

clauses.subject: world-compatibility
clauses.statement: Compatibility is semver over the world: a guest built against one minor loads on any host advertising a compatible minor.

clauses.subject: world-drain
clauses.statement: On a major world bump no new run admits against the old world, in-flight runs complete or suspend on the world they pinned, and the old world then retires.

clauses.subject: live-reresolution
clauses.statement: Re-resolving or reloading a connector while a journaled run holds it raises `ConnectorHotReload`; a new version applies to runs admitted after it.

clauses.subject: built-in-registry
clauses.statement: The names resolving to compiled-in sources form one enumerated list. A listed name carries no manifest or artifact, and a feature-gated entry stays listed and answers with a rebuild hint.

clauses.subject: http-headers
clauses.statement: The generic HTTP source binds credentials through a `headers` table whose values are templates in the {{connector.reference.value-template}} grammar, hydrated per read.

clauses.subject: http-page-pull
clauses.statement: Under page-number, next-cursor or no pagination and without an incremental field, one generic HTTP source pull reads one page and carries the next page's token as its position. The walk's last page carries a position naming the first page.
clauses.why: because a failed walk resumes at the page it stopped on, and the next run walks the whole table again

clauses.subject: http-url-walk
clauses.statement: Under next-URL or Link-header pagination, one generic HTTP source pull walks every page, and no position carries a page URL.
clauses.why: because a next URL's query may carry a credential, and a position lands unscrubbed in the journal

clauses.subject: http-watermark-walk
clauses.statement: Under an incremental field without next-URL or Link-header pagination, one generic HTTP source pull reads one page from the stored watermark; its position carries that watermark and the next page's token, and the walk's last page carries none.

clauses.subject: http-limiter
clauses.statement: The generic HTTP source reads its {{connector.meter.limiter-declaration}} from a `limiter` config table, and the project manifest holds each {{connector.meter.limiter-binding}} under `[limiters.<quota>]`.

clauses.subject: http-scope-probe
clauses.statement: The generic HTTP source reads its {{connector.declare-capability.scope-probe}} from a `scope_probe` config table and carries its first reference-bound header as the bound credential.

clauses.subject: http-compression
clauses.statement: The generic HTTP source decompresses a body only when `compression` declares `gzip` or `zip`, bounded by {{connector.source.object-expansion}}. The URL extension does not select compression.
clauses.why: because a URL path names a route, not how the vendor stored the bytes

clauses.subject: body-format
clauses.statement: `format` selects the `contextful-decode` decoder — `json` by default, `json-object`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `feed` or a workbook — for HTTP, file and object sources. HTTP declares formats; file and object sources infer them from extensions compared without case.

clauses.subject: json-record-shape
clauses.statement: `json` requires an array of objects; `json-object` requires one object. Both select `records` when declared, otherwise the root; a missing selection or wrong shape is unreadable input under {{run.land.unreadable-input}}.

clauses.subject: json-object-record
clauses.statement: `json-object` emits one row even when the selected object or its nested arrays are empty; decoding retains the full parsed body for pagination pointers.

clauses.subject: json-body-paths
clauses.statement: `records`, `next_cursor_path` and `next_url_path` read JSON pointers in either JSON mode.

clauses.subject: json-object-pagination
clauses.statement: `json-object` admits cursor, next-URL and Link-header pagination; page-number pagination refuses under {{connector.source.format-key-mismatch}} before I/O.
clauses.why: because one object never supplies the empty record array that terminates page-number pagination

clauses.subject: format-key-mismatch
clauses.statement: A JSON record path, a pagination shape, or a decode key declared against a format that does not read it raises `ConnectorFormatKeyRejected` at build.

clauses.subject: delimited-cell
clauses.statement: A delimited source lands every cell as a string and an empty unquoted field as null.
clauses.why: because a dimension file's schema then depends on no data

clauses.subject: declared-encoding
clauses.statement: A non-UTF-8 delimited body decodes through a declared encoding label, and bytes invalid under it raise `ConnectorEncodingInvalid`.

clauses.subject: delimiter
clauses.statement: On `format = "csv"`, `delimiter` names one field delimiter character, defaulting to `,`. Validation accepts a tab and refuses a quote, line break or longer value at build.
clauses.why: because a field delimiter that also opens a quote or ends a record leaves every line two readings

clauses.subject: declared-columns
clauses.statement: `columns` on `format = "csv"` names a headerless body's columns in order. A first record whose field count differs refuses under {{connector.source.configuration-fault}}; a later one is unreadable input under {{run.land.unreadable-input}}, naming its line.
clauses.why: because a headerless body under a short list otherwise lands a shifted cell under the wrong name

clauses.subject: clock-column-spelling
clauses.statement: A delimited clock column other than an RFC 3339 instant or a fixed-width digit stamp raises `ConnectorClockColumnRejected`.

clauses.subject: feed-format
clauses.statement: `format = "feed"` decodes an RSS or Atom document into one row per item or entry carrying `entry_id`, `title`, `link`, `published_at`, `summary`, `author` and `categories`, each null where the entry holds none.

clauses.subject: feed-entry-id
clauses.statement: A feed row's `entry_id` is the Atom `id` or the RSS `guid`, else the entry's link; an entry carrying neither is unreadable input under {{run.land.unreadable-input}}.
clauses.why: because a primary key over `entry_id` then collapses every re-fetched entry onto one row

clauses.subject: feed-published-at
clauses.statement: `published_at` is the Atom `published`, else `updated`, or the RSS `pubDate`, folded to an RFC 3339 instant in UTC; a date that is neither RFC 3339 nor RFC 2822 is unreadable input.
clauses.why: because a watermark over `published_at` then orders instants, whatever offset the feed spells

clauses.subject: feed-categories
clauses.statement: `categories` is JSON array text of `domain` and `term` objects in document order: each RSS `category` text and its `domain`, or Atom `term` and `scheme`; an absent domain is null, an empty term skipped.
clauses.why: because a model then selects items by a facet through `json_extract` over one declared column

clauses.subject: conditional-get
clauses.statement: `conditional = true` sends the position's `etag` as `If-None-Match` and `last_modified` as `If-Modified-Since`. A `304` lands no rows and holds the position; a `2xx` commits the validators it serves.

clauses.subject: conditional-position
clauses.statement: A conditional pull issues one request, and the validators are its whole position: no page token or watermark rides beside them, and the pull reports no further page.

clauses.subject: conditional-rejected
clauses.statement: `conditional` beside a pagination shape or a declared `incremental` raises `ConnectorConditionalRejected` at build.
clauses.why: because a validator names one document, and a watermark position leaves the validators nowhere to commit

clauses.subject: pagination
clauses.statement: A walk declares exactly one pagination shape: a page parameter with a start page, a next-cursor path with a cursor parameter, a next-URL path, or link-header following.

clauses.subject: pagination-ambiguity
clauses.statement: Declaring two pagination shapes raises `ConnectorPaginationAmbiguous`.

clauses.subject: page-cap
clauses.statement: One walk issues at most 1000 requests; a watermark walk counts them from its last page whose every clock passes every clock the walk served before.

clauses.subject: page-loop
clauses.statement: A vendor returning a token or link it already served raises `ConnectorPageLoop`.

clauses.subject: next-link-origin
clauses.statement: The host checks a vendor-supplied next link as a hop under {{connector.attach.weakened-hop}}.

clauses.subject: table-pattern
clauses.statement: A table pattern binds table-name segments into the request URL, percent-encoded, and each table holds its own position.

clauses.subject: table-unmatched
clauses.statement: A table not matching the declared pattern, or binding `.` or `..` into a placeholder, raises `ConnectorTableUnmatched` ahead of any request.

clauses.subject: placeholder-unbound
clauses.statement: A URL or bound-column placeholder naming neither `{table}` nor a table-pattern field raises `ConnectorPlaceholderUnbound` at build.

clauses.subject: bound-columns
clauses.statement: `bound_columns` maps a column name to a template over `{table}` and the table pattern's fields; every row a read fetches carries each column at its filled value, unencoded.

clauses.subject: bound-column-occupied
clauses.statement: A fetched row already carrying a bound column raises `ConnectorBoundColumnOccupied`, failing the read.
clauses.why: because the vendor's value and the table's value otherwise disagree with nothing recording which one landed

clauses.subject: github-recipe
clauses.statement: `recipes/github.toml` lands issues without pull requests and commits per `<owner>/<repo>` table, following the `Link` header, stamping `repo_full_name`, and clocking commits at `/commit/committer/date`.

clauses.subject: github-recipe-keys
clauses.statement: `recipes/github.toml` keys issues on `id` and commits on `sha`, so the boundary row each poll re-serves lands as one row.

clauses.subject: expansion
clauses.statement: An expansion block names its pointer as a URL template over the landed row's scalar columns, percent-encoded, or as a column holding a URL, and names the column the fetched document lands under.

clauses.subject: pointer-ambiguity
clauses.statement: Declaring both pointer forms raises `ConnectorPointerAmbiguous`.

clauses.subject: expansion-order
clauses.statement: After filtering by watermark, the source expands rows with one follow-up request at a time.
clauses.why: because a rejected row then costs no vendor request and no batch bursts one host

clauses.subject: follow-up-failure
clauses.statement: A failed follow-up raises `ConnectorExpansionFailed` for the whole read.
clauses.why: because a position committed past a row missing its detail strands that row

clauses.subject: expansion-budget
clauses.statement: One expanding read issues at most 200 requests of follow-up, judged before the first, buffers at most 256 MiB, and runs at most 600 s. Each budget refuses rather than truncating.

clauses.subject: template-shape
clauses.statement: A pointer template carrying no placeholder, or binding one into the URL authority, raises `ConnectorTemplateRejected` at build.
clauses.why: because a response body then names a credential's destination

clauses.subject: pointer-column-missing
clauses.statement: A placeholder naming a column the rows lack, or carry as an array, raises `ConnectorPointerColumnMissing` on the first row, ahead of its request.

clauses.subject: target-column-occupied
clauses.statement: A target column any landed index row already carries raises `ConnectorTargetColumnOccupied` ahead of the walk.

clauses.subject: walk-boundary
clauses.statement: A directory walk reaches the configured root and nothing outside it, skips dot-entries, and traverses in sorted order. A decode-selecting key narrows nothing.
clauses.why: because a sorted walk over an unchanged tree reproduces across hosts

clauses.subject: declined-tally
clauses.statement: A directory walk records on the run record what it declined, tallied by extension, and reports the total as its {{run.record.skipped-count}}.

clauses.subject: object-address
clauses.statement: The `s3` source reads one `bucket` by exactly one of `key` or `prefix`; declaring both or neither raises `ConnectorObjectAddressRejected` at build.
clauses.why: because a key beside a prefix leaves which objects land to a guess, and neither names no object

clauses.subject: prefix-listing
clauses.statement: A prefix read lists every key under the prefix in key order, narrowed by an optional `suffix`, and lands each object through one decoder. `pick = "latest"` lands the greatest listed key alone.

clauses.subject: object-gzip
clauses.statement: `compression = "gzip"`, or a key ending `.gz` with `compression` undeclared, decompresses an object before decode; `compression = "none"` reads it as stored.

clauses.subject: object-zip
clauses.statement: `compression = "zip"`, or an object key ending `.zip` with `compression` undeclared, decodes one archive member.

clauses.subject: zip-member
clauses.statement: The decoder reads an archive's single member or the member selected by `member`. Multiple members without a selection, or a missing selected member, refuse the read under {{connector.source.configuration-fault}}.
clauses.why: because landing one member of several by archive order picks rows the declaration never named

clauses.subject: object-expansion
clauses.statement: One object or HTTP body decompresses to at most 256 MiB, counted as the bytes arrive. Past it the body lands nothing, named as the object or the scrubbed URL, and an HTTP read refuses whole.

clauses.subject: object-unreadable
clauses.statement: An unreadable object, or one exceeding {{connector.source.object-expansion}}, lands no data rows and one {{run.land.dead-letter}} row naming `s3://<bucket>/<key>`. The rest of the read lands.

clauses.subject: unreadable-all
clauses.statement: An object or file read in which every input it reaches is unreadable, none landing or held unchanged, refuses whole under {{run.land.unreadable-input}}, naming each input.
clauses.why: because every input failing names a declaration fault, such as a wrong `format`, rather than damaged inputs

clauses.subject: configuration-fault
clauses.statement: A compiled-out decoder, unknown `encoding`, missing selected archive member, unselected multi-member archive, or first record mismatching `columns` fails the whole object or file read as a configuration fault. The source names the error and dead-letters nothing.
clauses.why: because dead-lettering each changed input under a declaration none satisfies records one fault as many damaged inputs

clauses.subject: unreadable-position
clauses.statement: With `skip_unchanged = true` a position holds a dead-lettered object at its ETag, and the `file` position holds a dead-lettered file at its digest, so a later read skips it until it changes.
clauses.why: because a dead letter re-landing on every fire fills the dead-letter table with one fault

clauses.subject: dead-letter-replay
clauses.statement: `replay_dead_letters = true` on the `s3` or `file` source re-reads every input its position holds dead-lettered, whatever its ETag or digest, landing it or dead-lettering it again.
clauses.why: because a fixed decoder reads unchanged bytes, which no ETag or digest change announces

clauses.subject: unreadable-incomplete
clauses.statement: A read that dead-letters an input reports no complete snapshot, so a replacing table retires none of that input's earlier rows.
clauses.why: because a complete snapshot claim tombstones every row the read omits

clauses.subject: etag-skip
clauses.statement: With `skip_unchanged = true`, the object source's position maps each object key to its ETag in place of {{run.advance.skip-unchanged}}'s digest; an object whose ETag matches lands nothing, and a read matching every object closes a zero-row success.

clauses.subject: object-credentials
clauses.statement: The `s3` source declares `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key` together, each as one `secret://<name>` reference hydrated per read. Without them, requests go unsigned. The host refuses a literal in either under {{connector.reference.material-in-a-declaration}}.

clauses.subject: object-session-token
clauses.statement: Beside the key pair, the `s3` source accepts an optional `session_token`, one `secret://<name>` reference hydrated per read, and signs each request as a temporary credential.

clauses.subject: object-role
clauses.statement: `credentials = "role"` on the `s3` source signs under {{store.endpoint.role-credentials}} in place of the key pair, refusing alongside a key under {{store.endpoint.role-conflict}}.

clauses.subject: object-transport
clauses.statement: The `s3` source presigns each request through the S3 bucket adapter of {{store.endpoint.addressing}} and sends it through the mediated client, allowlisting the endpoint host alone; a skip compares listed or head-request ETags and downloads no object.
clauses.why: because one S3 client then signs every bucket request while the mediated client stays the one attachment point for source egress

clauses.subject: object-cleartext
clauses.statement: At build, the host refuses an `s3` source binding a key pair to a cleartext endpoint outside loopback under {{connector.attach.cleartext-endpoint}}.
clauses.why: because a presigned URL is a bearer capability for its lifetime

clauses.subject: object-position-owned
clauses.statement: `incremental` beside `skip_unchanged = true` on the `s3` source refuses as {{connector.package.component-position}} at validation.

clauses.subject: document-grain
clauses.statement: A document source lands one row per page, or one row per heading past a length threshold. With a base URL, each row links to its own page anchor.

clauses.subject: document-identity
clauses.statement: A document row's identity is a slug plus an ordinal, chunked or not.
clauses.why: because an identity then survives a document crossing the threshold

clauses.subject: document-unreadable
clauses.statement: An encrypted document or a document with no extractable text on any page counts as unreadable input under {{run.land.unreadable-input}}. The source stores no empty pages for these documents.

clauses.subject: frontmatter-shape
clauses.statement: A nested map, a block scalar, a key carrying the reserved producer prefix, or, compared without case, a repeated key or a key other than `title` naming a column the source lands, in a note's frontmatter raises `ConnectorFrontmatterRejected`.

clauses.subject: conversion-required
clauses.statement: A compound-binary office container, detected by an office extension or by magic bytes under an extension the source reads, raises `ConnectorConversionRequired` naming the conversion command.

clauses.subject: file-source
clauses.statement: The `file` source resolves `root` against the project directory and walks into one `documents` table: `.md` and `.markdown` notes, `.txt` plain text, `.pdf` pages. The source declines other extensions without opening them.

clauses.subject: file-globs
clauses.statement: The source reads a root-relative path if no `exclude` glob matches and either an `include` glob matches or none is declared. `*` and `?` match within one segment; a `**` segment matches any number.

clauses.subject: file-no-follow
clauses.statement: The `file` walk follows no symbolic link, to a file or a directory.
clauses.why: because a link is the one path out of the root that a sorted walk of names cannot see

clauses.subject: file-table-unmatched
clauses.statement: A `file` table other than `documents` refuses as {{connector.source.table-unmatched}}, ahead of the walk.

clauses.subject: document-slug
clauses.statement: A document's slug is its root-relative path without extension, lowercased, each run of characters other than ASCII letters and digits in a segment folded to `-`. Two files folding to one slug fail the read naming both.
clauses.why: because a slug is the identity a link and a citation carry, and two files under one identity overwrite each other's rows

clauses.subject: heading-threshold
clauses.statement: A note whose body past its frontmatter exceeds 8192 B lands one row per heading section, the text before its first heading as its own row; a shorter note and a text file land one row.

clauses.subject: document-columns
clauses.statement: A document row carries slug, ordinal, root-relative path, kind, title, heading, text, url, the file's SHA-256 and a `removed` flag. The title is the frontmatter `title`, else the first level-one heading, else the file stem.

clauses.subject: frontmatter-columns
clauses.statement: Each other frontmatter key lands lowercased as a string column on every row of its note: a scalar as its text, a list as a JSON array.

clauses.subject: document-url
clauses.statement: With `base_url`, a row's url is the base joined with its slug, then `#page=<n>` on a PDF page or the heading's anchor on a heading section; without `base_url` the url is null.

clauses.subject: file-position
clauses.statement: The `file` position maps each landed path to its digest and row count. A matching digest lands nothing, a changed file re-lands whole and tombstones ordinals past its new count, and a vanished file tombstones every row.

clauses.subject: file-unreadable
clauses.statement: An unreadable file lands no data rows and one {{run.land.dead-letter}} row. The source retains earlier rows and continues the read.

clauses.subject: file-rename
clauses.statement: A file renamed onto its old slug re-lands under its new path, and the old path tombstones only ordinals past the renamed file's row count.
clauses.why: because a tombstone on an identity the read lands live removes the renamed document

clauses.subject: file-cap
clauses.statement: The source declines a file over 64 MiB without reading past the leading bytes identifying its format.
clauses.why: because a row-per-page document past that size is an export, not a note, and one file must not exhaust the read's memory

clauses.subject: file-pdf-absent
clauses.statement: A PDF the walk reaches in a build without the PDF decoder fails the read as a configuration fault naming the feature to rebuild with.

clauses.subject: file-position-owned
clauses.statement: `incremental` beside the `file` source refuses as {{connector.package.component-position}} at validation.

clauses.subject: parse-containment
clauses.statement: A compiled-in source decodes behind {{run.land.parse-boundary}}.

clauses.subject: office-part-selection
clauses.statement: The decoder reads an office container by exact part name. The decoder opens no other part and resolves no external entity.

clauses.subject: decompression-budget
clauses.statement: A multi-part office read decompresses at most 64 MiB in total, judged against the archive directory's claim and against the bytes that arrive.

clauses.subject: worksheet-landing
clauses.statement: One worksheet read holds at most 64 MiB — resolved cell text and keys, plus 32 B for each shared string and each stored cell, counted as they land — and lands at most 1048576 rows.
clauses.why: because shared-string fan-out turns a small input into an unbounded output

clauses.subject: cell-out-of-range
clauses.statement: A cell holding a value past the header's width raises `ConnectorCellOutOfRange`; a cell holding none widens nothing.

clauses.subject: external-reference
clauses.statement: An external-reference declaration, an external-links part, or a relationship marked external raises `ConnectorExternalReference`.

clauses.subject: workbook-cell-typing
clauses.statement: The decoder stores a workbook cell as a string and a date cell as its serial number. The decoder stores cached formula values without evaluating formulas.

clauses.subject: workbook-incremental
clauses.statement: An incremental position against a workbook raises `ConnectorIncrementalUnsupported`.
clauses.why: because a variable-width serial number advances a lexicographic watermark past unlanded rows

clauses.subject: report-id-commit
clauses.statement: An async-report source commits the vendor run id when creation returns. Exhausting the polling budget ends the read successfully. The source recreates an expired vendor run for the same window.

clauses.subject: page-drain
clauses.statement: Report paging drains a fixed number of pages per read, one batch per page, each carrying the position after it.

clauses.subject: page-cursor-missing
clauses.statement: A response announcing another page while naming its cursor in neither the cursor field nor the next link raises `ConnectorPageCursorMissing`.

clauses.subject: report-watermark
clauses.statement: The source holds report watermarks per partition: account, grain, breakdown and any split dimension. One position contains the versioned watermark map.

clauses.subject: partition-isolation
clauses.statement: A retryable failure on one partition holds it at its committed position and keeps the pages other partitions drained.

clauses.subject: metric-grain
clauses.statement: A metric read at a grain where the vendor estimates rather than computes it raises `ConnectorMetricGrainRejected`.

clauses.subject: restated-window
clauses.statement: A caught-up partition re-opens its lookback window every run, the pull window is at least that wide, and each row carries a deterministic key over partition, entity, date and breakdown.

clauses.subject: report-event-time
clauses.statement: A report row's event time is an RFC 3339 instant at midnight UTC of the window-start day, null where the vendor gave no usable date.

clauses.subject: ordering-column
clauses.statement: Ordering a report stream by the engine-injected ingest stamp raises `ConnectorOrderingColumnRejected`.
clauses.why: because a late seed then outranks a live restatement

clauses.subject: field-drift
clauses.statement: Report rows enter the batch as untyped JSON. The source recognizes throttling from a throttle status or an error body containing a throttle code.

clauses.subject: report-auth
clauses.statement: An authentication failure on a report read raises `ConnectorAuthTerminal`, terminal against the retry schedule.

clauses.subject: image-row
clauses.statement: An image source lands path, content hash, header width and height, embedded capture instant, file modification time, a modality marker and a null body. No pixel decode runs on ingest.

clauses.subject: image-header
clauses.statement: An image header that does not parse raises `ConnectorImageHeaderUnreadable` naming the path.

clauses.subject: quotability-marker
clauses.statement: Whatever fills an image body records in a companion column whether the text is verbatim extraction or a model's reading.

clauses.subject: marker-body-pairing
clauses.statement: An image body and its quotability marker that are not null together raise `ConnectorQuotabilityMismatch`.

clauses.subject: search-config
clauses.statement: The search source takes a driver, a query, a freshness window and a result ceiling, landing one row per result. Its cursor kind is snapshot-id, keyed on the result URL.

clauses.subject: provider-origin
clauses.statement: Each search call site pins its provider's host. A non-TLS transport or another host raises `ConnectorProviderOriginRejected`, except on loopback.

clauses.subject: search-degradation
clauses.statement: An absent provider key and a provider `5xx` are transient failures yielding a zero-row outcome, and a replay returns the journaled result set.

clauses.subject: poll-only-increments
clauses.statement: Incremental loading is a scheduled poll. A replication socket held open is not a source read.
clauses.why: because its output is unbounded and has no recorded exchange to replay

clauses.subject: receive-form
clauses.statement: A `receive` source declares `format = "jsonl"`, a positive `max_batch_bytes`, a positive `max_queue_depth` and a positive `key_retention_secs`, none defaulted; it serves every declared table and requests nothing from outside.
clauses.why: because a ceiling the sender fills must be the operator's choice, not a guess the binary carries
scenarios: WHEN a `receive` source omits `max_queue_depth`, THEN validation refuses naming the key.

clauses.subject: receive-recorded
clauses.statement: The engine bounds and records a delivered batch before storing its rows. {{connector.source.poll-only-increments}} does not apply to `receive` sources.

clauses.subject: receive-unscheduled
clauses.statement: A `receive` pipeline declaring a `schedule` fails validation.
clauses.why: because a sender, not the cadence, starts its runs, so a scheduled fire fails on every beat

clauses.subject: receive-body
clauses.statement: A `receive` body holds one JSON object per line, `table` naming a declared table and `row` its row object; another shape fails the whole batch as {{run.land.unreadable-input}}, naming the line.
scenarios: WHEN line 2 of a body names an undeclared table, THEN the batch fails naming line 2 and no table lands.

clauses.subject: twin-api
clauses.statement: A source reading through an API licensed to see what no individual user sees raises `ConnectorTwinApiSource`. The engine admits a sanctioned, disclosed organization-wide export path.

clauses.subject: drive-walk
clauses.statement: The drive source walks `folder_id` breadth-first through `files.list`, paging each folder within `drive_id` when declared. The source lists each folder once, sorts children by name and id, and follows no shortcut.
clauses.why: because the source keeps a per-file position and mints its token host-side, which a guest holding no credential bytes cannot

clauses.subject: drive-root-set
clauses.statement: Exactly one of `folder_id` or `folder_ids` selects roots; `folder_ids` holds 1 to 16 entries, all distinct, under one required `drive_id`. An empty, oversized, repeated or ambiguous selection raises `ConnectorDriveRootsInvalid` before listing.
scenarios: WHEN `folder_ids` is empty or accompanies `folder_id`, THEN validation raises `ConnectorDriveRootsInvalid` before listing.

clauses.subject: drive-root-validation
clauses.statement: With `folder_ids`, every selected root names a folder in the declared `drive_id`. A missing or outside-drive root raises `ConnectorDriveRootRejected` before the source lists any selected folder.
scenarios: WHEN one selected root belongs to another Shared Drive, THEN `ConnectorDriveRootRejected` names it before the source lists any selected folder.

clauses.subject: drive-root-walk
clauses.statement: With `folder_ids`, the drive source applies {{connector.source.drive-walk}} to each root while confining descendants to the declared drive, listing each folder once across overlaps.

clauses.subject: drive-root
clauses.statement: A `folder_id` naming no folder, or one outside a declared `drive_id`, fails the read as a configuration fault before any listing.

clauses.subject: drive-overlap
clauses.statement: A file reachable through multiple selected roots lands once by `file_id`. Its `resolved_root` is the lexicographically least selected root id reaching the file.
scenarios: WHEN two selected roots reach one file, THEN one `files` row carries the least root id as `resolved_root`.

clauses.subject: drive-tables
clauses.statement: The drive source serves `files`, one row per file keyed by `file_id` with its version, name, path from the root, MIME type, `modifiedTime`, Drive's `md5Checksum` and the SHA-256 of the bytes read, and `pages`.

clauses.subject: drive-table-unmatched
clauses.statement: A drive table other than `files` or `pages` refuses as {{connector.source.table-unmatched}}, ahead of any request.

clauses.subject: drive-mode
clauses.statement: `mode` selects `bytes-and-pages` by default or `metadata-only`; another spelling raises `ConnectorDriveModeUnknown` before any request.

clauses.subject: drive-capture-record
clauses.statement: Every file row carries `resolved_root`, `export_mime_type`, captured `bytes` and `capture_status`: `captured`, `skipped` or `removed`. A removed row or skipped row without captured bytes has null `sha256`.

clauses.subject: drive-metadata-only
clauses.statement: In `metadata-only` mode, the source hashes exact downloaded or exported bytes, then discards the bytes after recording the digest.
scenarios: WHEN a downloaded version has known bytes, THEN its SHA-256 matches those bytes, which the source discards after capture.
WHEN the source downloads the separately retained named version, THEN its byte SHA-256 reproduces the `files` row's digest.

clauses.subject: drive-version-consistency
clauses.statement: After a metadata-only download or export, the source re-reads the file version; a change from the listed version raises `ConnectorDriveVersionMoved` before any row or cursor commits.
clauses.why: because a digest of newer bytes cannot witness the version named by the file row
scenarios: WHEN a file changes between listing and download, THEN `ConnectorDriveVersionMoved` refuses the capture without a file row or cursor.

clauses.subject: drive-named-skip
clauses.statement: A skipped file row names the file and reason; the per-file bound of {{connector.source.drive-file-cap}} applies in both modes.
clauses.why: because a skipped row cannot attest to bytes the source did not read
scenarios: WHEN a selected file exceeds the byte cap, THEN its skipped row names the file and cap.

clauses.subject: drive-export
clauses.statement: A Google Doc, Sheet or Slides deck lands as its `files.export` PDF and any other file as its `alt=media` bytes; another Google-native type lands a `skipped` reason and no bytes.

clauses.subject: drive-page-grain
clauses.statement: In `bytes-and-pages` mode, each PDF page lands one `pages` row under {{connector.source.document-grain}}, decoded behind {{run.land.parse-boundary}}; bytes land in no column. In `metadata-only` mode, no page content row lands.
clauses.why: because a page is what retrieval ranks and a citation names, and a row column holding a whole file inflates every scan of the table
scenarios: WHEN mode is `metadata-only`, THEN no page content row lands.

clauses.subject: drive-bytes
clauses.statement: In `bytes-and-pages` mode, every whole exported or downloaded body lands as {{store.lay-out.landed-blob}}, named by its file row's `sha256`; in `metadata-only` mode, no blob lands.
scenarios: WHEN mode is `metadata-only`, THEN no landed blob holds the downloaded bytes.

clauses.subject: drive-file-cap
clauses.statement: For a file over `max_file_bytes`, 64 MiB by default, the source stores a file row with a `skipped` reason naming the cap, without pages. The source reads no bytes past the cap and continues.
clauses.why: because a row naming the skipped file answers for it, where truncated bytes read as the whole document

clauses.subject: drive-unreadable
clauses.statement: A PDF body failing to decode behind {{run.land.parse-boundary}} lands its file row with a `skipped` reason naming the failure and no pages, and the read continues.
clauses.why: because one unreadable file failing the fire holds back every other file's row and the position behind them

clauses.subject: drive-export-limit
clauses.statement: A Doc, Sheet or Slides deck whose export Drive answers `403 exportSizeLimitExceeded` lands its file row with a `skipped` reason naming Drive's export limit and no pages, and the read continues.
clauses.why: because Drive refuses that export on every fire, so failing the read stalls the whole tree behind one file

clauses.subject: drive-skip-count
clauses.statement: Each drive pull reports the files it lands with a `skipped` reason as its {{run.record.skipped-count}}, so a fire's `files` run and `pages` run each carry the tally.

clauses.subject: drive-selection-position
clauses.statement: The position binds the declared drive, sorted root set and mode; changing any of them revalidates every root and rewalks the selected trees, rereading files without reusing an earlier frontier.
scenarios: WHEN a configured pipeline changes from `bytes-and-pages` to `metadata-only`, THEN the next read rewalks its roots and rereads retained files.

clauses.subject: drive-selection-removals
clauses.statement: A complete selected-root walk lands tombstones for files removed, moved outside the roots or deselected, and for excess prior pages; an incomplete walk commits no removals.
scenarios: WHEN a complete new selection excludes a formerly captured file, THEN its `file_id` lands a tombstone.
WHEN mode changes from `bytes-and-pages` to `metadata-only`, THEN old pages receive tombstones and no page content row remains.

clauses.subject: drive-root-reassignment
clauses.statement: For selected roots, the position also holds each file's `version` and `resolved_root`. A complete walk re-reads the file when either changes, even with matching `modifiedTime` and path.
clauses.why: because a changed version needs a fresh byte witness even when the file id stays stable
scenarios: WHEN a retained file's version changes with identical `modifiedTime` and path, THEN the read captures its new bytes and digest.

clauses.subject: drive-incremental
clauses.statement: The drive position holds each file's `modifiedTime`, path and page count. A read re-lands a file whose time or path changed, and lands a tombstone for a file gone from the tree and for each page past its new count.

clauses.subject: drive-list-bound
clauses.statement: A selected-root walk shares {{connector.source.page-cap}} across roots; reaching it with a pending folder or page token raises `ConnectorDriveListingExceeded`, naming the folder and committing no selection removals.
clauses.why: because an incomplete listing cannot prove a file left the selected trees
scenarios: WHEN listing reaches the request cap with a next-page token but no queued folders, THEN the read refuses and lands no removal tombstone.

clauses.subject: drive-fire
clauses.statement: One fire shares one minted token, one walk and one read of each file's bytes across the `files` and `pages` tables.

clauses.subject: drive-oauth
clauses.statement: The drive source mints its access token from a refresh token and client credentials bound as `secret://` references, once per fire and again on a `401`, holding it in memory and writing it to no store, journal or record.
clauses.why: because Google's refresh token does not turn over, so the minted token is the one rotating material, and it lapses within the hour

clauses.subject: drive-oauth-shape
clauses.statement: Before any request, the source checks that `oauth.refresh_token`, `oauth.client_id` and `oauth.client_secret` each hold exactly one `${secret://<name>}` reference and nothing else.

clauses.subject: drive-origin
clauses.statement: The drive API and token endpoints are `www.googleapis.com` and `oauth2.googleapis.com` over TLS on the default port; another host, port or scheme refuses as {{connector.source.provider-origin}}, loopback excepted.

clauses.subject: drive-position-owned
clauses.statement: `incremental` beside the drive source refuses as {{connector.package.component-position}} at validation.

clauses.subject: credential-plane
clauses.statement: Outbound credentials authenticate vendor requests separately from credentials admitting callers into a store. A key retains its inbound or outbound purpose regardless of storage location.

clauses.subject: declaration-binds-a-reference
clauses.statement: A declaration's capability block lists required credential names. Each name binds to a `secret://<name>` reference that the resolver hydrates at run time.

clauses.subject: reference-scheme
clauses.statement: `secret://<name>` carries a logical name matching `[a-z0-9-]+` of at most 128 chars. A reference names no storage path, file name or key identifier.

clauses.subject: backend-independence
clauses.statement: The adapter maps a logical name to a storage location. Changing credential stores changes the backend mapping without editing declarations.

clauses.subject: value-template
clauses.statement: A value embedding a credential is a template of literal text with `${secret://<name>}` placeholders, such as `Bearer ${secret://vendor-token}`.

clauses.subject: foreign-placeholder
clauses.statement: `${env://NAME}` or a bare `${NAME}` inside a template raises `SecretForeignPlaceholder` at parse, naming the value and the span.

clauses.subject: malformed-placeholder
clauses.statement: When reading a declaration, the parser raises `SecretMalformedTemplate` for an unclosed, empty or nested placeholder, before any text leaves the process.

clauses.subject: environment-is-a-miss
clauses.statement: Template hydration skips the process-environment adapter and continues through the chain. If no adapter answers, the resolver applies {{connector.resolve.unresolved-name}}.

clauses.subject: environment-opt-in
clauses.statement: `CONTEXTFUL_SECRETS_ALLOW_ENV_TEMPLATES=1` enables the environment adapter for template hydration. The resolver logs one warning per process naming the variable.

clauses.subject: whole-value-binding
clauses.statement: `env://NAME` binds a whole credential outside the template grammar.

clauses.subject: whole-value-reference
clauses.statement: A whole-value `secret://<name>` reference outside templates, such as a `[sync]` credential key, resolves through the assembled adapter chain, including process environment, under {{connector.resolve.first-hit-wins}} and {{connector.resolve.shadowed-name}}.
clauses.why: because a whole-value key sits in the node's own configuration, where `env://NAME` already reads the environment directly

clauses.subject: material-in-a-declaration
clauses.statement: A credential-shaped literal standing where a reference belongs raises `SecretMaterialInDeclaration` at validation, naming the key.

clauses.subject: lease-has-no-scheme
clauses.statement: A leased credential binds as `secret://<name>`. No lease spelling exists in the manifest grammar.

clauses.subject: name-is-the-join
clauses.statement: Declarations, provider entries, cache keys, records and run provider attribution identify the same credential by its logical name.

clauses.subject: provider-port
clauses.statement: One provider interface resolves a reference to credential material. Each backend implements this interface as an adapter. `CONTEXTFUL_SECRETS_BACKEND` selects the adapters in the chain.

clauses.subject: provider-chain
clauses.statement: The chain runs: lease provider, process environment, operating-system keychain, operator-managed secret store, then a tunnel into the deployment trust zone.

clauses.subject: first-hit-wins
clauses.statement: Hydration uses the first adapter answering the name. The resolver consults no later adapter for that reference during the run.

clauses.subject: shadowed-name
clauses.statement: At first hydration, a name answered by the serving adapter and by any adapter behind it raises `SecretNameShadowed`, naming the logical name and both adapters.
clauses.why: because a stray environment variable otherwise shadows the manager unnoticed

clauses.subject: hydration-is-just-in-time
clauses.statement: When building each request, the host asks the resolver for credentials. Cached material follows {{connector.resolve.cache-ttl}}. Declarations, journal entries, audit records, run records and log lines contain no hydrated values.

clauses.subject: redacting-wrapper
clauses.statement: Every hydrated value, including a pure-literal template, uses a wrapper whose debug and display forms print a fixed sentinel. The host reveals bytes only when writing the request.

clauses.subject: wiped-on-drop
clauses.statement: A hydrated wrapper has no `Clone`. Shared owners reference one buffer that zeroes when its last owner drops, including an expired cache entry. The wrapper excludes request and transport copies.
clauses.why: because a freed credential otherwise stays readable until the allocator reuses its memory

clauses.subject: resolver-per-source
clauses.statement: Each source has one resolver and its own cache. The resolver combines concurrent first hydrations of one name into one lookup.

clauses.subject: cache-ttl
clauses.statement: A cache entry lives at most 300 s.

clauses.subject: unresolved-name
