clauses.statement: If no assembled adapter answers a reference, the resolver raises `SecretUnresolvedReference`, naming the reference. The error occurs at preflight for static bindings and at the call otherwise.

clauses.subject: posture
clauses.statement: Four credential configurations order by distance from the engine: inline environment values, request-time reference resolution, external manager using workload identity, and secretless broker sidecar. The workload-identity manager is the default.

clauses.subject: inline-outside-development
clauses.statement: A profile other than development binding plaintext material at a call site raises `SecretInlineCredential` naming the binding.

clauses.subject: forwarding-sidecar
clauses.statement: A sidecar that reads and forwards a stored long-lived credential raises `SecretForwardingBroker`. A sidecar minting a short-lived scoped credential is a lease provider.

clauses.subject: adapter-is-optional
clauses.statement: Each managed backend is one adapter holding opaque versioned ciphertext; a deployment links only the adapters it uses.

clauses.subject: know-how-in-an-adapter
clauses.statement: An adapter exposing a provider-specific exchange, refresh or lifetime entry point raises `SecretProviderKnowHowInBackend` at load.

clauses.subject: aws-secrets-manager
clauses.statement: The `aws-secrets-manager` backend answers `secret://<name>` with the `AWSCURRENT` value of secret id `CONTEXTFUL_AWS_SECRET_PREFIX` plus the name, signing under {{store.endpoint.role-credentials}}; an absent secret is a miss.

clauses.subject: scope-declaration
clauses.statement: `CONTEXTFUL_LEASE_SCOPES` lists the logical names hydrating as run-time leases, each optionally as `name=scope`.

clauses.subject: head-of-chain
clauses.statement: For a declared name, the resolver uses the lease provider without falling back to later adapters. A shadowing adapter raises under {{connector.resolve.shadowed-name}}.

clauses.subject: undeclared-name-defers
clauses.statement: An undeclared name sends the lease provider no request and leaves precedence among the other adapters untouched.

clauses.subject: empty-scope-set
clauses.statement: Selecting the lease backend with no scope declared raises `SecretLeaseScopesEmpty` at startup.

clauses.subject: lease
clauses.statement: The resolver holds a leased credential and its expiry together in memory for the run. The resolver evicts both at expiry. Neither enters a file, journal entry or audit record.

clauses.subject: malformed-lease
clauses.statement: A lease carrying no expiry, or one already past on arrival, raises `SecretMalformedLease` as a transient failure.

clauses.subject: cache-window
clauses.statement: A leased name's cache entry expires at the earlier of {{connector.resolve.cache-ttl}} and the lease's own expiry.

clauses.subject: retirement-margin
clauses.statement: An entry retires 10 percent of its window ahead of expiry, the margin capped at 30 s.
clauses.why: because a request sent near the boundary still lands inside the grant

clauses.subject: endpoint
clauses.statement: The provider answers `POST <provider-url>/leases` carrying a bearer mint credential and body `{ "scope": "<lease scope>" }`.
clauses.why: because a batched answer ties one scope's refusal to every name in it and mints material no request has asked for

clauses.subject: response
clauses.statement: A success carries `value` plus one expiry — `expires_in` seconds, `expires_at` epoch seconds, or an RFC 3339 instant — at the top level or under `lease`.

clauses.subject: unknown-scope
clauses.statement: A `404` raises `SecretLeaseScopeUnknown` as a configuration fault. The resolver does not fall back to a stored credential for a declared name.

clauses.subject: mint-rejected
clauses.statement: A `401` or `403` raises `SecretMintRejected`, classed `auth_expired`.

clauses.subject: rate-limited
clauses.statement: A `429` passes its `Retry-After` to the run's retry, classed `rate_limited`.

clauses.subject: request-rejected
clauses.statement: Any other `4xx` raises `SecretLeaseRequestRejected` as a permanent configuration fault.

clauses.subject: transient-class
clauses.statement: A `5xx` and a transport error are transient. The mint client retries nothing itself; the run's retry schedule is the one retry layer.

clauses.subject: vendor-requests-on-failure
clauses.statement: A run holding an expired lease whose provider is unreachable issues 0 requests to the vendor.

clauses.subject: calls-per-resolver
clauses.statement: A resolver issues at most 1 calls to the mint endpoint per declared name per lease window.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-credential
clauses.statement: The engine authenticates to the mint endpoint with one standing `secret://` credential scoped only to minting. Revoking this credential cuts off each leased source at its next expiry.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-non-recursion
clauses.statement: The lease provider holds the chain as assembled before it joined, so the mint reference hydrates only through adapters behind it.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-unserved
clauses.statement: A bootstrap name no adapter behind the lease provider answers raises `SecretBootstrapUnresolved`, naming the reference.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-declared-leased
clauses.statement: Listing the bootstrap name among the leased scopes raises `SecretBootstrapLeased` at startup.

clauses.subject: bootstrap-backend
clauses.statement: `CONTEXTFUL_LEASE_BOOTSTRAP_BACKEND` composes an operator-managed secret store behind the lease provider to hold the mint reference.

clauses.subject: mint-transport
clauses.statement: The mint client reaches its endpoint over TLS or loopback and ignores system proxy configuration.

clauses.subject: redirect
clauses.statement: A `3xx` from the mint endpoint raises `SecretLeaseRedirect`; the mint credential is not replayed at the target.

clauses.subject: host-mediation
clauses.statement: The host implements outbound HTTP. Before socket I/O, the host checks each request against the declaration, assigns a request id and writes the bound credential onto a permitted request.

clauses.subject: no-material-to-a-guest
clauses.statement: No host import hands credential bytes to guest code; a guest names a request and receives a response.

clauses.subject: unpermitted-request
clauses.statement: A request whose host the declaration does not cover raises `SecretUnpermittedRequest` and fails the guest call even where guest code discards the error.

clauses.subject: transport-port
clauses.statement: The mediated client reaches the network only through a transport interface. The send method connects to a vetted address, follows no redirect, and applies the client's proxy choice, timeout and body ceiling.

clauses.subject: resolve-half
clauses.statement: After {{connector.meter.pre-send-hook}} admits the hop, the transport interface resolves the name. The client checks each returned address under {{connector.attach.private-address}}.

clauses.subject: resolve-once
clauses.statement: The host resolves a permitted host name once per request and connects to the address it vetted, with no second lookup between check and connect.

clauses.subject: private-address
clauses.statement: A host name resolving to a private, link-local, unique-local, loopback or cloud-metadata address raises `ConnectorPrivateAddress`, unless the configured host is itself a loopback name or literal.
clauses.why: because an allowlisted name pointed at an internal range is SSRF

clauses.subject: private-range-admitted
clauses.statement: An address inside a CIDR range listed in `CONTEXTFUL_EGRESS_PRIVATE_RANGES` passes {{connector.attach.private-address}}; the host name allowlist still applies.
clauses.why: because a VPC-bound deployment reaches its sources, interface endpoints and PrivateLink services at private addresses

clauses.subject: private-range-rejected
clauses.statement: A listed range overlapping loopback, link-local `169.254.0.0/16` or `fe80::/10`, or the metadata address `fd00:ec2::254`, raises `ConnectorPrivateRangeRejected` at startup, naming the range.
clauses.why: because admitting the metadata or loopback range reopens the SSRF path the private-address check closes

clauses.subject: bound-host
clauses.statement: A credential-bound source declares one non-wildcard host, checked at validation and session open. A wildcard entry or table-bound endpoint host beside a bound credential raises `SecretWildcardHost`.

clauses.subject: default-attachment
clauses.statement: Without an attachment declaration, the host writes `Authorization: Bearer <value>` from the single bound credential.

clauses.subject: attach-block
clauses.statement: An `[attach]` block maps a header name to a value template. The host hydrates it onto the permitted request, overriding the guest's header of that name.

clauses.subject: per-request-hydration
clauses.statement: A guest session stores hydration handles and plain static headers. The host calls each handle for every permitted request and releases the hydrated header when the request completes.
clauses.why: because session-held credential material outlives the request and delays rotation

clauses.subject: literal-attach-value
clauses.statement: An attach value embedding no reference raises `SecretLiteralAttachValue`.
clauses.why: because a constant header belongs in the guest's request construction

clauses.subject: redirect-pinning
clauses.statement: With or without credentials, a source follows a hop only with the configured host and port on the same or stronger transport. Sources follow cleartext-to-TLS hops at that host and port.

clauses.subject: weakened-hop
clauses.statement: A redirect or vendor-supplied next link moving from TLS to cleartext, or to another host or port, raises `SecretRedirectOffOrigin`, and the read fails.

clauses.subject: landed-origin
clauses.statement: The source stores response bodies only from the configured host and port.

clauses.subject: referer-off
clauses.statement: `Referer` is off on every outbound client.

clauses.subject: header-selects-client
clauses.statement: A source declaring any header, literal or hydrated, uses the hardened client and bypasses the system proxy. A source declaring no header keeps the proxy.

clauses.subject: cleartext-endpoint
clauses.statement: The host marks a reference-hydrated header sensitive. Sending the header to a cleartext endpoint raises `SecretCleartextEndpoint`, except on IPv4 or IPv6 loopback.

clauses.subject: sensitive-header-record
clauses.statement: A run records which header names carried a credential, by name only.

clauses.subject: url-scrubbing
clauses.statement: Before a URL enters an error message, log line or stored column, the host removes query, fragment and userinfo. Scheme, host, port and path remain.

clauses.subject: typed-url-edit
clauses.statement: Metered vendor traffic and control-plane traffic each use one client that clears URLs through typed error mapping. The host scrubs other URLs as text.

clauses.subject: credential-in-a-url
clauses.statement: A configured endpoint carrying userinfo raises `SecretCredentialInUrl` at validation, naming the source.

clauses.subject: mediation-covers-every-egress
clauses.statement: A built-in source, a guest connector, a model call and a limiter call each attach through the one mediated client; {{connector.attach.exec-environment}} names the one attachment outside it.

clauses.subject: exec-environment
clauses.statement: At spawn, an exec step hydrates its env template through the source resolver into the environment cleared by {{run.exec.no-shell}}. This attachment bypasses host mediation and enters {{connector.record.provider-attribution}}.
clauses.why: because the derive driver hands a vendor child its own credential, and a loopback attaching proxy remains an open design

clauses.subject: division-of-labor
clauses.statement: A credential store contributes versioned storage and a trigger. The host drives the OAuth loop from the connector's auth policy and writes the token back as a blind versioned put.

clauses.subject: expiry-hint
clauses.statement: The host may store an opaque `expires_at` hint beside the ciphertext for cache invalidation.

clauses.subject: static-key
clauses.statement: A static key in an operator-managed secret store turns over with no engine step: a run hydrates the current version at its next cache miss.
clauses.why: because the 300 s cache bound already caps staleness, and a per-manager change feed adds a listener and failure domain to every adapter

clauses.subject: oauth-credential
clauses.statement: The host refreshes an OAuth credential at {{connector.lease.retirement-margin}} from its declared expiry. The host puts the refreshed version to the answering adapter, conditioned on the hydrated version, then clears the name's cache entry.

clauses.subject: operator-entered
clauses.statement: An operator re-enters a development or keychain secret by updating the reference.

clauses.subject: leased-credential
clauses.statement: The resolver re-mints a leased credential before its window ends without writing it back. If minting fails, the source uses no credential, including an older value.

clauses.subject: write-back-denied
clauses.statement: A refused put or answering adapter without a write method raises `SecretRotationWriteDenied`. The host discards the refreshed token without serving it, and the run fails closed.
scenarios: WHEN the answering adapter refuses the put of a refreshed token, THEN the run fails and no request carries the refreshed token.

clauses.subject: conditional-put
clauses.statement: If another writer stores a version first, the losing put rehydrates that version without raising an error.
scenarios: WHEN another writer stored a newer version first, THEN the next hydration returns that version and the rotation raises nothing.

clauses.subject: connector-owns-meaning
clauses.statement: The connector's `[auth]`, `[rate_limit]` and `[retry]` blocks define token lifetime, exchange rules, refresh endpoint and scopes, expired-token codes and rate-limit headers. Connector id and version pin these blocks.

clauses.subject: no-master-key
clauses.statement: The engine holds references, and no single encryption key exists whose theft with a database copy yields every credential.

clauses.subject: turnover-preserves-the-name
clauses.statement: Every rotation mechanism keeps the logical name, touching no declaration and no pinned connector artifact.

clauses.subject: operator-record
clauses.statement: An optional operator record describes one logical name's intended grants, account or tenancy, consuming surfaces and rotation location; supplied creation and expiry assertions remain operator metadata.

clauses.subject: metadata-storage
clauses.statement: A committed operator record contains descriptive metadata only. Recording a binding requires neither a credential value nor a decryption key.

clauses.subject: provider-custody
clauses.statement: The selected provider owns credential values, versions and rotation state; an external-manager binding requires no ciphertext copy in the repository.
scenarios: WHEN a binding selects an external manager with no encrypted repository entry, THEN the manager remains the sole owner of its value and versions.

clauses.subject: surface-of-consumption
clauses.statement: An operator record identifies each documented consuming surface and its credential binding name.

clauses.subject: optional-record
clauses.statement: A binding without an operator record remains resolvable and appears in inventory with unknown descriptive fields.
scenarios: WHEN a configured binding has no operator record, THEN inventory includes the binding with unknown descriptive fields.

clauses.subject: unverified-scope-is-marked
clauses.statement: An operator record marks grants as unknown when the operator has not established them.

clauses.subject: rotation-record
clauses.statement: A rotation follows {{connector.rotate.turnover-preserves-the-name}} without requiring a repository commit; operator metadata changes only when its assertions change.
scenarios: WHEN a manager rotates a credential, THEN the repository needs no commit.

clauses.subject: inventory
clauses.statement: `contextful secrets list` displays configured logical bindings with their configured adapters, operator metadata and available provider observations. The command reads no credential values and claims no complete provider inventory.

clauses.subject: observation-provenance
clauses.statement: Each provider-observed field names its adapter and observation time; operator assertions remain separately labelled, including when they disagree with provider observations.
scenarios: WHEN an operator expiry differs from an observed expiry, THEN inventory shows both with their distinct provenance.

clauses.subject: observation-unavailable
clauses.statement: Inventory reports unsupported, denied or failed metadata reads as unavailable with a reason. Inventory neither substitutes operator assertions for provider observations nor hydrates values to obtain metadata.
scenarios: WHEN a provider denies metadata access, THEN inventory reports the reason without reading a credential value.

clauses.subject: expiry-unknown
clauses.statement: Inventory reports an absent expiry as unknown. `no expiry` requires an explicit assertion or observation. Inventory computes days remaining only for a dated expiry and retains its provenance.
scenarios: WHEN neither operator nor provider supplies an expiry, THEN inventory reports unknown expiry and no days remaining.

clauses.subject: expiry-warning
clauses.statement: The inventory marks each dated expiry falling within 30 d and each elapsed expiry, retaining the expiry's provenance.

clauses.subject: configured-is-not-observed
clauses.statement: A configured adapter identifies a binding's configuration; only {{connector.record.provider-attribution}} identifies the adapter that answered a run's reference.
scenarios: WHEN a binding configures multiple adapters and has no run attribution, THEN inventory reports configuration without asserting an answering adapter.

clauses.subject: provider-attribution
clauses.statement: A run's commit-phase and failure rows carry `credential_providers`. The field maps each hydrated logical name to the answering adapter, using names only.

clauses.subject: record-table
clauses.statement: An operator record is a `[secret.<name>]` table in the discovered `contextful.toml`, keyed `description`, `account`, `grants`, `surfaces`, `rotate`, `created` and `expires`, each optional; `expires = "never"` is the one explicit no-expiry assertion.

clauses.subject: record-rejected
clauses.statement: A `[secret.<name>]` table outside discovered `contextful.toml`, without a manifest-bound `secret://` name, or containing an unknown key, mistyped value or credential-shaped string raises `SecretRecordRejected` during declaration read. The error names file, name and key path, excluding values.
clauses.why: because a misspelled name otherwise describes nothing while the real binding reads undescribed, and an echoed value carries a pasted token into CI logs
scenarios: WHEN `contextful.toml` holds `[secret.vendor-tokne]` beside a binding named `vendor-token`, THEN the declaration read refuses and the message carries no record value.

clauses.subject: record-is-inert
clauses.statement: Resolution, attachment, rotation and pipeline content hashing read no operator record. Editing a record changes no plan, run or hydrated value.
scenarios: WHEN an operator record's description changes, THEN the pipeline retains its content hash.

clauses.subject: observe-port
clauses.statement: An adapter's observation interface returns presence, version, creation and expiry for a name, or unavailable with a reason. The interface holds no hydrated value. Inventory holds only observation interfaces.
scenarios: WHEN inventory lists a lease-served binding, THEN its lease observation reads unsupported and the mint endpoint receives 0 requests.

clauses.subject: inventory-output
clauses.statement: `secrets list` exits 0 whatever its marks; `--json` prints one object per binding per line: name, configured adapters, latest answered adapter with run id and instant, operator fields, and observations with adapter and time.

clauses.subject: name-binding
clauses.statement: A connection binds one opaque secret name to its admitted tenant and principal; a run hydrates only the name bound to its connection.
scenarios: WHEN two principals connect one OAuth client, THEN each run resolves only its own refresh-token name.

clauses.subject: adapter-port
clauses.statement: A principal secret adapter resolves a name to credential material and a version. The adapter's write method conditionally stores a replacement version under the same name.

clauses.subject: write-serialization
clauses.statement: Concurrent refreshes of one name serialize across resolvers through the adapter's conditional version; the losing refresh rehydrates the winner under {{connector.rotate.conditional-put}}.
scenarios: WHEN two refreshes race on one name, THEN one version wins and the other resolver rehydrates it.

clauses.subject: lease-custody
clauses.statement: A lease endpoint holding refresh tokens answers the connection's name under {{connector.lease.lease}}; Contextful retains neither the refresh token nor its replacement.

clauses.subject: disconnect
clauses.statement: Deleting a connection revokes its principal secret name before another run hydrates it. If revocation fails, the connection stays paused.
clauses.why: because a deleted connection must not regain vendor access from a cached lease

clauses.subject: picker-source
clauses.statement: The `gdrive-picks` source serves `files` and `pages` with {{connector.source.drive-oauth}} and {{connector.source.drive-page-grain}} for files selected through Picker.

clauses.subject: file-selection
clauses.statement: On `gdrive-picks` and `gdrive-sheet`, `file_ids` selects distinct individual files without a folder root; `folder_id` and `folder_ids` are absent.

clauses.subject: file-selection-limit
clauses.statement: `file_ids` holds at most 128 entries.

clauses.subject: file-selection-invalid
clauses.statement: An empty, repeated or mixed `file_ids` selection, or one exceeding {{connector.drive-picks.file-selection-limit}}, raises `ConnectorDriveFilesInvalid` before a Drive request.
clauses.why: because an ambiguous selection cannot establish which files a later tombstone withdraws
scenarios: WHEN `file_ids` repeats one id or appears beside `folder_id`, THEN validation raises `ConnectorDriveFilesInvalid` before any request.

clauses.subject: file-access
clauses.statement: The source validates each selected file with the bound credential. An uncaptured inaccessible or trashed id, non-file id, or file outside configured `drive_id` raises `ConnectorDriveFileRejected` without landing rows or advancing position.
clauses.why: because an inaccessible picker id cannot count as a complete selection
scenarios: WHEN a picked id is inaccessible to the bound credential, THEN `ConnectorDriveFileRejected` commits neither rows nor position.
WHEN a picked file lies in another Shared Drive than the configured `drive_id`, THEN `ConnectorDriveFileRejected` commits neither rows nor position.

clauses.subject: file-revoked
clauses.statement: When a captured file becomes inaccessible or trashed under a valid credential, the source tombstones its file and pages once. The position adds its id to the withdrawn set. Authentication and transient failures advance no position.
scenarios: WHEN a captured file loses access under a valid credential, THEN its file and pages receive tombstones before the selection position advances.
WHEN two fires follow a captured file's revocation, THEN the first lands its tombstone, the second lands none, and both keep the other picked files in the position.

clauses.subject: file-withdrawn
clauses.statement: A withdrawn id stays selected without refusing later fires. A fire finding the file inaccessible stores nothing for that file. When access returns, the source captures the file as new and removes its id from the withdrawn set.
scenarios: WHEN a withdrawn file becomes readable again, THEN the next fire lands its captured row and the position holds it outside the withdrawn set.

clauses.subject: export-limit
clauses.statement: If Drive answers a picked file's export with `403 exportSizeLimitExceeded`, the source applies {{connector.source.drive-export-limit}}. The file id stays outside the withdrawn set, and its `files` row receives no tombstone.
clauses.why: because Drive refuses that export on every fire while the principal still reads the file, and a tombstone withdraws a file nobody revoked
scenarios: WHEN a captured Sheet's new version exceeds Drive's export limit, THEN its `files` row lands `skipped` rather than `removed`, and the position keeps it.

clauses.subject: file-position
clauses.statement: The position binds sorted `file_ids` and mode; changing either rereads retained files, and a complete read tombstones deselected files and their pages.
scenarios: WHEN a file id leaves a complete selection, THEN its file row and prior pages land tombstones.

clauses.subject: row-scope
clauses.statement: A connection-bound run stamps its Drive `files` and `pages` rows and tombstones with the admitted `tenant` and `principal`. The source supplies neither value.
scenarios: WHEN two tenants select the same file id, THEN each landed row carries only its admitted tenant and principal.

clauses.subject: row-identity
clauses.statement: A connection-bound Drive row and position key include connection identity beside `file_id`. Connections selecting the same file keep separate rows and positions.

clauses.subject: source-name
clauses.statement: The `gdrive-sheet` source serves `rows` and shares {{connector.source.drive-oauth}} and {{connector.drive-picks.file-selection}} without changing the `gdrive` source's `files` and `pages` tables.

clauses.subject: export-format
clauses.statement: A Google Sheet selected for structured capture exports as XLSX; CSV contains only the first sheet.

clauses.subject: sheet-identity
clauses.statement: Each landed spreadsheet row carries `file_id`, sheet id, sheet name, source row number, connection identity, `tenant` and `principal`.
scenarios: WHEN a workbook has two sheets with row 3 on each, THEN their landed keys differ by sheet id.

clauses.subject: row-key
clauses.statement: A spreadsheet row key combines connection identity, file id, sheet id and source row number. A complete recapture tombstones keys absent from the captured workbook.
scenarios: WHEN a complete recapture removes a row, THEN the old row key receives a tombstone.

clauses.subject: cell-values
clauses.statement: The row preserves each cell's typed value and its column position; an empty cell is distinct from a missing row.

clauses.subject: formula-value
clauses.statement: The source stores a formula cell's exported result and records that the cell contains a formula. Contextful does not evaluate the formula.

clauses.subject: export-refusal
clauses.statement: A workbook whose export exceeds {{connector.source.drive-file-cap}} lands a named skipped file row and no partial spreadsheet rows.
clauses.why: because a truncated workbook cannot establish row identity or removal

clauses.subject: export-limit
clauses.statement: When {{connector.drive-picks.export-limit}} rejects a workbook export, the source stores a named skipped file row and retains prior spreadsheet rows and keys. Only {{connector.drive-picks.file-revoked}} tombstones a selected workbook.
clauses.why: because an export over Drive's size limit leaves the workbook readable, so its rows still describe the principal's file
scenarios: WHEN a captured workbook's next export answers `403 exportSizeLimitExceeded`, THEN no spreadsheet row of it receives a tombstone.

clauses.subject: initial-token
clauses.statement: Before the initial full listing, the source obtains a start page token. The source commits the token with the complete listing, preserving replay of changes during listing.

clauses.subject: cursor-scope
clauses.statement: The cursor binds the connection, credential principal, declared drive, selected roots or file ids, and capture mode. A changed binding starts a complete listing.

clauses.subject: page-commit
clauses.statement: A change read follows every `nextPageToken` and advances to `newStartPageToken` only after the resulting rows and removals commit.
scenarios: WHEN a change response has another page, THEN the committed cursor does not skip that page.

clauses.subject: selection-filter
clauses.statement: The source admits a changed file only when its current ancestry or id satisfies the bound selection. Moving outside the selection produces tombstones.

clauses.subject: removed-file
clauses.statement: For a removal change, the source withdraws the file and pages only after establishing that the selected file is absent or inaccessible.

clauses.subject: invalid-token
clauses.statement: If Drive rejects or expires a change token, the source starts a complete selected listing. The incomplete change response advances no removals.
clauses.why: because a missing change interval cannot prove the retained files still satisfy the selection
scenarios: WHEN Drive rejects the cursor, THEN a complete walk reconciles removals before a new token commits.

clauses.subject: delegation-grant
clauses.statement: Domain-wide delegation requires an operator-declared Workspace domain, authorized service account and approved scope set bound to the connection.

clauses.subject: impersonated-principal
clauses.statement: Every delegated Drive request names one admitted Workspace user as its subject; the row and permission sweep retain that subject's identity.

clauses.subject: domain-boundary
clauses.statement: A delegated request for a subject outside its declared domain raises `ConnectorDriveDomainRejected` before token minting.
clauses.why: because administrator approval for one domain conveys no authority over another
scenarios: WHEN a connection names a user outside its approved domain, THEN `ConnectorDriveDomainRejected` precedes any Google request.

clauses.subject: organization-export
clauses.statement: A sanctioned organization-wide export declares its scope and disclosure posture explicitly under {{connector.source.twin-api}}; delegated user reads do not imply that export.

clauses.subject: subject-tuple
clauses.statement: A subject is a tuple of agent, host, `on_behalf_of` principal, task scope, inference zone and incognito flag. A credential binds the subset it names and admits under that combination alone.

clauses.subject: attestation
clauses.statement: Each member carries an attestation, `verified` or `asserted`. Agent, host, task and zone are asserted and render labeled as such; no surface presents an asserted member as identity.

clauses.subject: on-behalf-of
clauses.statement: `on_behalf_of` is verified at the mint against the issuing identity provider, and admission carries it forward as the reader's identity.

clauses.subject: value-hygiene
clauses.statement: The mint checks every subject value: non-empty, at most 256 B, no control character, no leading or trailing whitespace.

clauses.subject: malformed-value
clauses.statement: A value failing {{authority.identify.value-hygiene}} raises `AuthoritySubjectMalformed`, except that the command-line mint trims a padded value where the automated exchange refuses it.

clauses.subject: normalization
clauses.statement: The verified tuple is normalized once, each value trimmed and each blank member dropped, before any consumer reads it. No point of use re-normalizes a value or interprets a scheme prefix.

clauses.subject: subject-missing
clauses.statement: A credential carrying no subject member raises `AuthoritySubjectMissing` at admission, naming the refusing surface and echoing no credential value.
clauses.why: because an unauthenticated face mints a credential naming a public subject; admitting none reads as the owner's ambient authority

clauses.subject: identity-link
clauses.statement: An identity link maps a source principal onto a subject over fields the identity provider verified, recording `method` and `confidence`. Confidence relaxes no check.

clauses.subject: unverified-link
clauses.statement: Only `scim_email` and `oidc_sub` links authorize. An authorization join consuming an `operator_asserted` link raises `AuthorityLinkUnverified`.

clauses.subject: directory-link
clauses.statement: Directory provisioning from the identity provider writes source-account links. A value a source's profile interface returns at request time is data, not a link.

clauses.subject: unlinked-principal
clauses.statement: A subject whose source principal resolves to no link reads from that source only the resources {{disclosure.reach.public-grant}} opens.
clauses.why: because a source principal is the source's spelling; the `user` principal {{disclosure.reach.subject-principals}} spells is the subject's own and needs no link

clauses.subject: agent-ceiling
clauses.statement: A sub-agent's reachable set equals or narrows its parent's; no agent reads beyond the principal it acts for.

clauses.subject: incognito
clauses.statement: Admission carries the caller's incognito flag unchanged, and a derivation turns it on and never off.

clauses.subject: subject-rebound
clauses.statement: A derivation naming an `on_behalf_of` different from its parent's raises `AuthoritySubjectRebound`.

clauses.subject: delegation-profile
clauses.statement: Delegated authority travels in one attenuable, chain-signed library format. The library owns serialization, signatures, block chaining and evaluation; a versioned profile names every fact, check and restriction the engine admits.

clauses.subject: owner-claim
clauses.statement: Profile 2 permits a signed owner store identity only in the root authority block; profile 1 and attenuation blocks reject it, and activation requires an unrestricted read grant over the selected store.

clauses.subject: unrecognized-element
clauses.statement: A credential carrying a block version, predicate, rule or restriction the profile does not name raises `ProfileElementUnrecognized`.

clauses.subject: reserved-fact
clauses.statement: Current time, audience, resolved resources and authenticated request identity are reserved facts the engine supplies. A token block introducing one raises `ProfileReservedFact`.

clauses.subject: evaluator-bound
clauses.statement: The evaluator runs with no third-party block, external function, recursion or regular-expression predicate. Input past {{authority.profile.fact-ceiling}} or {{authority.profile.iteration-ceiling}} raises `ProfileEvaluationBudget`.

clauses.subject: fact-ceiling
clauses.statement: One authorization holds at most 1000 entries in its fact set.

clauses.subject: iteration-ceiling
clauses.statement: One authorization runs at most 100 iterations of the evaluator.

clauses.subject: appended-block
clauses.statement: A block after the first contributes no authority fact to an allow decision; appending narrows a credential or adds nothing.

clauses.subject: unevaluated-restriction
clauses.statement: A grant carrying a row restriction or aggregate bound with no read evaluator raises `ProfileRestrictionUnevaluated` at the mint, at derivation on parent and child, and at admission.

clauses.subject: declared-field
clauses.statement: A restriction field the engine refuses stays declared in the profile and is parsed at every admission.

clauses.subject: declared-scope
clauses.statement: Introspection reports the scope a credential declares without evaluating it. Table policy, source access lists, time bounds and revocation settle effective authority afterwards.

clauses.subject: scoped-session
clauses.statement: Authorization yields a scoped session carrying every restriction the credential expressed. A statement over two tables needs both accesses in one coherent grant; actions and tables never flatten into independent allowlists.

clauses.subject: version-unsupported
clauses.statement: A checkpoint reading a profile version outside its supported set raises `ProfileVersionUnsupported`. Widening the profile mints a new version.

clauses.subject: introspection-surface
clauses.statement: Introspection runs on the command line alone, as `contextful token introspect`; no serving face answers an introspection request.
clauses.why: because an introspection route on a serving face tells any presenter which credentials verify and what each declares

clauses.subject: fields
clauses.statement: A grant names actions, table patterns, and optionally a tenant scope, aggregate constraints, a template allowlist and a row ceiling. An absent constraint leaves its dimension unconstrained; an absent allowlist confers no template.

clauses.subject: actions
clauses.statement: The action vocabulary is `read` for every row-returning surface, `write` to land rows, `execute` to fire a run, `admin` to mint, and `forget` to erase subject data.

clauses.subject: unknown-action
clauses.statement: An action outside the vocabulary raises `GrantActionUnknown` at the mint and at admission.

clauses.subject: pattern-forms
clauses.statement: A table pattern is `*`, covering every table; a prefix ending in `*`, covering every name beginning with that prefix; or any other string, matched exactly. A concrete pattern never covers `*`.

clauses.subject: malformed-pattern
clauses.statement: A pattern with `*` anywhere but its final position raises `GrantPatternMalformed`.

clauses.subject: one-matcher
clauses.statement: One pattern matcher serves derivation legality, view registration, tool visibility and replica object selection.

clauses.subject: star
clauses.statement: `*` is an ordinary grant, bounded by the credential's actions, audience and expiry and visible in the audit record.

clauses.subject: tenant-scope
clauses.statement: A tenant scope pairs a table with an opaque byte string bound to that table's outermost partition column.

clauses.subject: tenant-bytes
clauses.statement: The grant's tenant value, the partition key on disk and the consumer's tenant identifier are identical bytes, compared by bound-parameter equality with no trimming, case folding, collation or Unicode normalization.

clauses.subject: tenant-unbindable
clauses.statement: A tenant-scoped grant on a table declaring no bare outermost partition column raises `GrantTenantUnbindable` at admission.

clauses.subject: unpartitioned
clauses.statement: A consumer needing a per-tenant scope over a table declaring no partition key declares a bare outermost partition column; no other grant dimension scopes rows by tenant.
clauses.why: because a tenant value matched against an arbitrary column is a row restriction, and a scoped-looking grant over an unbound table reads every tenant

clauses.subject: tenant-child-lifetime
clauses.statement: A tenant-scoped child credential is derived per query with a lifetime of 15 min.

clauses.subject: held-parent
clauses.statement: A consumer's service holds one broader parent and derives each per-query child locally. A durable run step derives its child afresh from a parent the run owner holds, never from a persisted child.

clauses.subject: template-allowlist
clauses.statement: A template allowlist denies by default: absent authorizes none, `*` authorizes every template the manifest declares, and a child names only identifiers its parent named or covered.

clauses.subject: template-tables
clauses.statement: A covered template reads the tables its statement names inside that template's session, under every other layer; its coverage adds no table to a raw read.

clauses.subject: template-not-allowed
clauses.statement: Invoking a template outside the allowlist raises `GrantTemplateNotAllowed`, and an uncovered template is absent from the projected tool listing.

clauses.subject: pipeline-resource
clauses.statement: A pipeline identifier is a read resource: listing it, describing it and tracing its runs each need a read grant covering it. A grant over its landed tables confers none.

clauses.subject: pipeline-not-covered
clauses.statement: Describing an uncovered pipeline raises `GrantPipelineNotCovered`, naming it. Listing filters to covered identifiers and raises it when none is covered; a project declaring no pipelines lists empty.

clauses.subject: run-trace-denied
clauses.statement: Tracing a run gates on the pipeline resolved from the run record and raises `GrantRunTraceDenied` without naming that pipeline.

clauses.subject: write-not-covered
clauses.statement: A credentialed table write whose grants carry no `write` over a destination table raises `GrantWriteNotCovered`, naming the table, before its first effect.
clauses.why: because a write grant names the tables a principal authors, and a row landed outside them carries a principal who never authorized it

clauses.subject: row-ceiling
clauses.statement: A read's row ceiling is the least of the grant's, the request's, the template's, each touched table's published ceiling and {{read.respond.face-ceiling}}; an undeclared component imposes none, and the face ceiling is always declared.

clauses.subject: duration-ceiling
clauses.statement: A statement's `max_duration_ms` is the least of its grant, touched-table and request limits; an undeclared component imposes none, and no component declares a default.

clauses.subject: byte-ceiling
clauses.statement: A response's `max_response_bytes` is the least of its grant, touched-table and request limits; an undeclared component imposes none, and no component declares a default.

clauses.subject: horizon
clauses.statement: A grant may carry `horizon`, an instant bounding the availability time and `since` of every read its holder makes, under {{read.horizon.inherited-bound}} and {{read.horizon.exceeds-horizon}}; an absent horizon leaves availability unbounded.

clauses.subject: aggregate
clauses.statement: An aggregate grant carries a minimum group size, a maximum single-contributor share, permitted functions, a groups-per-query ceiling and a row ceiling. A write-only or aggregate-only grant contributes no table to a raw read.

clauses.subject: group-ceiling
clauses.statement: An aggregate grant's groups-per-query ceiling is at least 1 entries; a query producing more groups than the ceiling is cut at it.

clauses.subject: offline
clauses.statement: A holder derives a narrower child with no issuer round trip by appending a signed block. The parent's bytes stay unchanged, independently verifiable and independently withdrawable.

clauses.subject: narrowing
clauses.statement: Every dimension of a child obeys the narrowing table in Shapes, checked by the deriving holder and again across the whole chain at admission.

clauses.subject: widens
clauses.statement: A child broader than its parent on actions, tables, templates or aggregate constraints raises `AttenuationWidens`, naming the dimension.

clauses.subject: horizon-widens
clauses.statement: A child whose horizon falls later than its parent's is broader on `horizon` and refuses as {{authority.attenuate.widens}}, naming that dimension; a child naming no horizon inherits its parent's.

clauses.subject: expiry-extended
clauses.statement: A child whose expiry falls past its parent's raises `AttenuationExpiryExtended`.

clauses.subject: tenant-dropped
clauses.statement: A child dropping its parent's tenant scope or naming another tenant raises `AttenuationTenantDropped`. Adding a scope to an unscoped parent narrows.

clauses.subject: truncation
clauses.statement: The chain-final proof advances an ephemeral key per block; a chain truncated to a broader prefix verifies as nothing.

clauses.subject: bearer
clauses.statement: Derivation proves the chain and not the new holder's identity. A hop authenticating its new actor runs through the exchange.

clauses.subject: per-sub-agent
clauses.statement: An agent derives one child per sub-agent, each bound by its confirmation claim to that sub-agent's own key pair.

clauses.subject: ceiling
clauses.statement: A project persists in version control an issuance policy naming the default audience and the longest lifetime any mint produces, at most 24 h.

clauses.subject: above-ceiling
clauses.statement: An explicitly requested lifetime above the persisted ceiling raises `IssuanceLifetimeAboveCeiling`; an exchange policy's lifetime clamps down to the ceiling instead.

clauses.subject: ceiling-lowering
clauses.statement: Lowering the ceiling records the previous value and its instant; rotation-grace validation uses the recorded value until the last credential minted under it lapses.

clauses.subject: policy-init
clauses.statement: `contextful token policy init` writes the issuance policy naming its audience with a ceiling of the {{authority.verify.bearer-lifetime}} bound; over an existing policy it raises `IssuancePolicyExists` and writes nothing.
clauses.why: because a fresh project mints under a policy it commits, and the served faces admit nothing longer-lived by default

clauses.subject: lower-only
clauses.statement: `contextful token policy lower-ceiling` naming a value at or above the current ceiling raises `IssuanceCeilingNotLowered` and leaves the policy unchanged.
clauses.why: because a raised ceiling mints credentials outliving the grace windows validated against the lower one

clauses.subject: out-of-tree-mint
clauses.statement: Ceiling enforcement binds a mint run inside the project tree; a mint run outside it is bounded at the checkpoint by rotation-grace validation.

clauses.subject: principal-required
clauses.statement: A mint granting `write`, `execute` or `forget` whose subject names no `on_behalf_of` raises `IssuancePrincipalRequired`.

clauses.subject: default-read
clauses.statement: A mint's default action set is `read` alone.

clauses.subject: absent-author
clauses.statement: An absent authorship value on a landed row means no credential authorized the write: the uncredentialed owner or a timer-fired run.

clauses.subject: authoring-posture
clauses.statement: Every table write verb {{authority.verify.write-verbs}} runs under its manifest's authoring posture. `session` authors every write by one verified ambient credential's principal; `per_request` holds no ambient principal, leaving an unaccompanied write unauthored.

clauses.subject: posture-key
clauses.statement: A manifest declares its posture as a top-level `authoring_posture` of `session` or `per_request`. A table write verb reading a manifest whose key is absent or names another value raises `AuthoringPostureUndeclared` before its first effect.

clauses.subject: session-credential
clauses.statement: Under `session`, a table write verb run with no credential raises `AuthoringCredentialMissing` before its first effect.

clauses.subject: one-credential
clauses.statement: A served face admits a verified capability credential, presented as a bearer or bound to a holder key, and nothing else: no static bearer, no gateway shared secret, no unauthenticated owner path.

clauses.subject: missing-key
clauses.statement: A face configured with no issuer key raises `IssuerKeyMissing`, prints the command that fixes it, and binds no port.

clauses.subject: default-key
clauses.statement: A mint naming no issuer key reads `.contextful/issuer.seed`; no file there raises {{authority.issue.missing-key}}.
clauses.why: because the seed `contextful token keygen` writes by default is the one a mint in the same tree reads

clauses.subject: project-root
clauses.statement: The issuance policy, the default issuer seed and the key-set ledger sit under the directory {{store.init.discovery}} bases project paths on; with no `contextful.toml` upward, under the working directory.
clauses.why: because a ledger read from a subdirectory hides every retirement and epoch bump the root records

clauses.subject: unresolvable-key
clauses.statement: A set issuer key reference that resolves to no material raises `IssuerKeyUnresolvable`; no local key is fabricated.

clauses.subject: signing-port
clauses.statement: One signing port signs every credential's authority block and every audit root and tip; no mint path reads a private key. Seed files, secret references resolved at mint time and remote signing oracles are its adapters.

clauses.subject: oracle-custody
clauses.statement: Under the oracle adapter the seed stays inside the custodian, which records each mint as a signing call.

clauses.subject: signature-encoding
clauses.statement: A signing port names its encoding: `ed25519`, a 32-byte key and 64-byte signature; `es256-der` or `es256-raw`, a SEC1 P-256 point signing ECDSA over SHA-256 of the message as ASN.1 DER or 64-byte `r ‖ s`.
clauses.why: because an enclave, a cloud KMS and a browser key each answer ES256 in one encoding, and the tag lets every adapter answer in its own

clauses.subject: der-at-the-edge
clauses.statement: An `es256-raw` signature converts to DER where it leaves the port; a credential and an audit root or tip carry ES256 only as DER.
clauses.why: because the credential format verifies ES256 only in DER, and one stored encoding holds a verifier to one decoder

clauses.subject: encoding-invalid
clauses.statement: A port signature that does not decode under its encoding tag, or does not verify under the port's public key, raises `SignatureEncodingInvalid`; nothing is minted and no root or tip is written.
clauses.why: because a mislabelled signature yields a credential every checkpoint rejects, and refusing at the port names the adapter at fault

clauses.subject: public-key-text
clauses.statement: A port's public key prints as `ed25519:<hex>` or `es256:<hex>` of its SEC1 point; either form, with a compressed or uncompressed point, parses back to the key it names.

clauses.subject: algorithm
clauses.statement: A credential names Ed25519, the default, or ECDSA over P-256; the pinned key's scheme is authoritative.

clauses.subject: algorithm-mismatch
clauses.statement: A credential naming a scheme other than its pinned key's raises `SignatureAlgorithmMismatch`.

clauses.subject: unauthorized-mint
clauses.statement: A mint request presenting no grant carrying `admin` raises `IssuanceUnauthorized`.
clauses.why: because issuance authorizes itself with the same primitive as every other action, and a separate mint secret is a second perimeter to guard

clauses.subject: replica-mint
clauses.statement: A replica holds the issuer's public key and no signing material; a mint there raises `ReplicaCannotIssue`.
clauses.why: because a replica verifies every credential the primary mints and needs no power to produce one

clauses.subject: zone-wildcard
clauses.statement: A mint whose subject declares a wildcard inference zone raises `IssuanceZoneWildcard`.

clauses.subject: key-rotation
clauses.statement: The issuer signing key rotates every 90 d, and at once on suspected compromise.

clauses.subject: rotation-not-due
clauses.statement: A rotation without `--compromise` before {{authority.issue.key-rotation}} falls due raises `IssuerKeyRotationNotDue`, naming the instant it falls due.
clauses.why: because a scheduled rotation ahead of its cadence churns every verifier's pins with nothing withdrawn

clauses.subject: unrecorded-key
clauses.statement: A rotation without `--compromise` of an issuer key the key-set ledger does not date raises `IssuerKeyUnrecorded`; `contextful token record --since` dates it.
clauses.why: because an undated key otherwise rotates at once, skipping the cadence the ledger enforces

clauses.subject: bearer-cap-fixed
clauses.statement: No issuance policy, face or command setting raises the cap {{authority.verify.bearer-lifetime}} sets; a credential living longer admits over a network only bound to a holder key.

clauses.subject: admitted-authority
clauses.statement: Verification yields an admitted-authority value carrying the normalized subject tuple and its grants. Every read surface and row-landing effect takes that value as an argument; nothing downstream re-parses a credential or reads ambient state.

clauses.subject: write-verbs
clauses.statement: `context land`, `run start` and `pipeline run` are the table write verbs. Each admits its accompanying credential before its first effect and stamps that credential's `on_behalf_of` as every landed row's `_authored_by`.

clauses.subject: write-commit
clauses.statement: A credentialed table write reads its denylist afresh and checks expiry immediately before each commit; a credential revoked or lapsed since admission commits nothing, as {{authority.revoke.revoked}} and {{authority.verify.expired}}.

clauses.subject: no-bypass-constructor
clauses.statement: The admitted-authority type has no constructor that produces a value without a verification.

clauses.subject: effect-boundary
clauses.statement: A statement's start and each commit are effect boundaries. Each boundary re-reads expiry, revocation and policy version against the carried value; a lapse between boundaries stops the effect at the next one.

clauses.subject: format-interface
clauses.statement: The credential format sits behind one interface of issue, attenuate, verify and introspect; no enforcement call site names a credential type.

clauses.subject: bad-signature
clauses.statement: A credential with any block signature failing against a pinned key raises `SignatureInvalid` and admits nothing, no verified prefix included.
clauses.why: because a partially verified chain is an unauthenticated credential, and admitting its prefix hands out authority nobody signed as presented

clauses.subject: audience-mismatch
clauses.statement: A checkpoint declaring an expected audience raises `AudienceMismatch` for a credential with a different audience or none; a checkpoint declaring none performs no audience check.
clauses.why: because a credential minted for one store is otherwise replayable against another; the undeclared case is local development

clauses.subject: timestamps
clauses.statement: Every checkpoint decodes timestamps into UTC instants under one grammar and compares instants.

clauses.subject: malformed-timestamp
clauses.statement: A timestamp that does not decode under that grammar raises `TimestampMalformed` at every checkpoint alike.

clauses.subject: expired
clauses.statement: A credential whose expiry precedes the evaluation instant raises `AuthorityExpired` at admission and at each later effect boundary.

clauses.subject: possession-binding
clauses.statement: A confirmation claim holds a client public-key thumbprint. Each request under a credential carrying one bears a proof signed by the matching private key over method, target, body digest, issue instant and nonce; a credential carrying none requires no proof.

clauses.subject: possession-invalid
clauses.statement: A request whose proof does not verify against the confirmation thumbprint raises `PossessionProofInvalid`.

clauses.subject: replay-window
clauses.statement: A proof issued more than 300 s before the checkpoint clock is refused as {{authority.verify.possession-invalid}}; the nonce cache retains each nonce for that window.

clauses.subject: clock-skew
clauses.statement: A proof issued more than 30 s after the checkpoint clock is refused as {{authority.verify.possession-invalid}}.

clauses.subject: replayed-nonce
clauses.statement: A proof whose nonce repeats inside the replay window raises `PossessionProofReplayed`.

clauses.subject: local-transport
clauses.statement: A local transport is a stdio pipe the checkpoint inherited from the process that spawned it, or a Unix socket; every other transport is a network transport.

clauses.subject: local-holder-proof
clauses.statement: On a local transport, a credential whose confirmation claim holds a thumbprint admits only with a proof as {{authority.verify.possession-binding}}; the peer fallback never applies to it, and a missing or failing proof is refused as {{authority.verify.possession-invalid}}.

clauses.subject: local-proof-channel
clauses.statement: A credentialed command-line verb and the stdio tool server sign one holder proof at admission with the Ed25519 seed in `--holder-key`, else take the proof in `CONTEXTFUL_DPOP`, else sign with the seed in `CONTEXTFUL_HOLDER_KEY`; a blank variable is unset.
clauses.why: because a bound credential is otherwise unusable off the network face, and a proof on the argument list is readable through the process table

clauses.subject: local-proof-request
clauses.statement: A local proof covers method `CLI`, the verb's command path as target, such as `context land`, `memory write` or `mcp`, and an empty body.
clauses.why: because binding the verb keeps a proof minted for a read from admitting a write

clauses.subject: local-nonce-store
clauses.statement: A command-line verb checks its holder proof against the nonce store `.contextful/proof-nonces` under the project root, shared by every invocation on that project under an exclusive lock, so a repeated nonce raises {{authority.verify.replayed-nonce}}.
clauses.why: because each invocation is a fresh process, and a per-process cache lets a proof copied from the environment replay for the whole window

clauses.subject: holder-keygen
clauses.statement: `token keygen --holder` writes an Ed25519 holder seed and prints its thumbprint, the value `token mint --holder` binds as the confirmation claim.

clauses.subject: local-peer-fallback
clauses.statement: On a local transport, a credential with no confirmation claim admits only through the operating system's peer authentication: an inherited stdio pipe, or a socket peer whose kernel-reported uid equals the checkpoint process's uid.

clauses.subject: peer-mismatch
clauses.statement: A socket peer presenting a credential with no confirmation claim, whose kernel-reported uid differs from the checkpoint process's uid or which the platform cannot report, raises `TransportPeerMismatch` and admits nothing.

clauses.subject: network-bearer
clauses.statement: A network checkpoint admits a credential with no confirmation claim as a bearer when it names the checkpoint's declared audience and meets {{authority.verify.bearer-lifetime}}; the peer fallback never applies over a network.

clauses.subject: bearer-lifetime
clauses.statement: A bearer whose expiry falls more than 3600 s after its issue instant raises `BearerLifetimeExceeded` at a network checkpoint and admits nothing; its holder refreshes through {{authority.exchange.surface}}.

clauses.subject: connection-scoped
clauses.statement: A local admission binds to the pipe or socket connection that presented the credential; a request on any other connection is refused as {{authority.verify.peer-mismatch}} until that connection presents the credential and admits itself.

clauses.subject: nonce-cache
clauses.statement: A checkpoint's nonce cache holds at most 100000 entries; a proof arriving while it is full answers `503` and admits nothing.
clauses.why: because a proof the cache cannot record is a replay it cannot detect

clauses.subject: public-key-only
clauses.statement: A checkpoint holds public key material and no signing secret, and admits with no call to an issuer, identity provider or policy service.

clauses.subject: key-set
clauses.statement: A checkpoint accepts a set of issuer keys: comma-separated static pins, or a project-published unauthenticated key route returning the current and non-retired versions, opted into per key.

clauses.subject: pin-source
clauses.statement: A command-line checkpoint reads its pins from `--public-key`, else `CONTEXTFUL_ISSUER_PUBKEY`, and its audience from `--audience`, else `CONTEXTFUL_AUDIENCE`. A bare 64-hex pin reads as `ed25519/<hex>`; an unknown scheme prefix is refused as {{authority.verify.key-set-unavailable}}, naming the accepted forms.
clauses.why: because an operator exports the issuer key once per shell, and key tools commonly print a bare Ed25519 key with no scheme prefix

clauses.subject: key-set-refresh
clauses.statement: A published key set refreshes every 300 s, single-flight, plus one refresh on a signature failure, with failure-forced refreshes throttled.

clauses.subject: key-set-unavailable
clauses.statement: A checkpoint opted into a published key set that obtains none, or holding a malformed pin, raises `KeySetUnavailable`: the engine declines to start and a gateway answers `503`.

clauses.subject: key-set-stale
clauses.statement: After a failed fetch the last-known-good set serves while its age since the last successful fetch stays under 1 h; past that the checkpoint raises `KeySetStale`.

clauses.subject: short-lifetime
clauses.statement: A short lifetime is the primary withdrawal: a credential's remaining lifetime bounds its exposure after a provider sign-out or before a denylist entry propagates.

clauses.subject: denylist
clauses.statement: A checkpoint reads a denylist keyed on credential identifier. An entry ages out once its identifier verifies under no live key version.

clauses.subject: revocation-id
clauses.statement: Every derivation carries its own revocation identifier, withdrawing one subtree without ending the root it descends from.

clauses.subject: epoch
clauses.statement: A revocation epoch scoped on project, tenant and principal class invalidates that slice of outstanding authority.

clauses.subject: epoch-store
clauses.statement: A project persists each scope's current epoch and each issuer key version's retirement in `.contextful/keyset.toml` beside the issuer seed; a mint stamps its scope's current epoch, and a checkpoint re-reads the file at each admission.
clauses.why: because a file the checkpoint reads locally keeps a policy service off the admission path, and the seed's directory already holds the issuer's custody

clauses.subject: ledger-unavailable
clauses.statement: A checkpoint pointed at a key-set ledger, or that has read one, raises `KeySetLedgerUnavailable` and admits nothing once the file is absent or malformed.
clauses.why: because a vanished ledger read as empty lifts every key retirement and epoch bump

clauses.subject: unknown-principal-class
clauses.statement: `contextful token revoke --principal-class` naming neither `delegated` nor `unattributed` raises `RevocationPrincipalClassUnknown` and bumps nothing.
clauses.why: because an epoch under a class no credential carries withdraws nothing while reporting success

clauses.subject: revoked
clauses.statement: A credential on the denylist, or carrying an epoch below the current scoped epoch, raises `AuthorityRevoked` at the next effect boundary.

clauses.subject: compromise
clauses.statement: Suspected compromise of signing material runs a project-wide epoch bump together with immediate retirement of the key version. Waiting out a grace window withdraws nothing.

clauses.subject: rotation-grace
clauses.statement: A rotation policy declares a cadence and a grace window, validated against the persisted issuance policy, during which the retiring key version still verifies.

clauses.subject: short-grace
clauses.statement: A declared or overridden grace window shorter than the effective issuance ceiling raises `RotationGraceTooShort`.

clauses.subject: immediate-retire
clauses.statement: Immediate retirement removes a key version from the published set and every static pin; a checkpoint drops it at its next refresh.

clauses.subject: format-withdrawn
clauses.statement: From a declared cutover instant, every admission path raises `CredentialFormatWithdrawn` for a credential in a withdrawn format. Only an explicit declaration restores acceptance.

clauses.subject: surface
clauses.statement: `contextful token exchange` and `POST /auth/exchange` trade a verified external assertion for a capability credential, configured per project by `.contextful/exchange/policy.toml` and `.contextful/exchange/verify.key`. The command reads the assertion from `--jwt` or standard input, and a holder proof from `--dpop`.

clauses.subject: wire
clauses.statement: An exchange request body is the JSON object `{"jwt": "<assertion>"}`, which the command line builds from its assertion; a body of any other shape raises `ExchangeRequestMalformed` and mints nothing. A served face answers a mint `{"token": "<credential>"}`.
clauses.why: because the command line and every served face parse one body through one function, so a refusal reads the same on both

clauses.subject: body-ceiling
clauses.statement: An exchange request body holds at most 64 KiB; a longer body raises `ExchangeBodyTooLarge`, mints nothing and is not parsed.
clauses.why: because an assertion is a few KiB, and parsing an unbounded body is work an unauthenticated caller spends

clauses.subject: unconfigured
clauses.statement: An exchange in a project declaring no exchange policy raises `ExchangeUnconfigured`, naming `.contextful/exchange/policy.toml`, before the body is read.
clauses.why: because an unconfigured project exposes no exchange, whatever a caller sends

clauses.subject: status-map
clauses.statement: Over HTTP, {{authority.exchange.unconfigured}} answers 404, {{authority.exchange.wire}} and {{authority.exchange.holder-proof-invalid}} 400, {{authority.exchange.body-ceiling}} 413, {{authority.exchange.material-missing}} 503, {{authority.exchange.assertion-invalid}} 401, and any other refusal 403; every refusal body is `{"error": {"http", "identifier", "message"}}`.
clauses.why: because a caller repairs a 400 or 413, retries a 503, re-authenticates on a 401, and repairs nothing on a 403

clauses.subject: signing-fault
clauses.statement: Over HTTP, {{authority.issue.missing-key}}, {{authority.issue.unresolvable-key}}, {{authority.issue.algorithm-mismatch}} or {{authority.issue.replica-mint}} during an exchange answers 500, the body naming the identifier and withholding the refusal's detail.
clauses.why: because the face's operator repairs its configuration, and the detail describes the face's keys to an unauthenticated caller

clauses.subject: policy
clauses.statement: An exchange policy declares `expected_iss`, optional `expected_aud`, `subject_map`, `tenant_claim`, `role_claim`, `role_grants`, `default_grants`, `ttl_secs`, `minted_iss` and `minted_aud`.

clauses.subject: injected-material
clauses.statement: Verifying material is operator-injected: a shared secret, an RS256 public key in PEM form, or a key-set document selected by the assertion's `kid`. The exchange makes no network call.

clauses.subject: minted-grants
clauses.statement: Minted grants come from `role_grants` and `default_grants` alone. A verified role matching no entry earns `default_grants`, which is empty unless declared.

clauses.subject: tenant
clauses.statement: The assertion claim `tenant_claim` names becomes the tenant scope of every minted grant; no subject member carries tenancy.

clauses.subject: lifetime-default
clauses.statement: A minted credential lives 900 s where the policy declares no `ttl_secs`.

clauses.subject: lifetime-ceiling
clauses.statement: A configured `ttl_secs` clamps down to 3600 s and never extends.

clauses.subject: audience
clauses.statement: A minted credential carries `minted_aud`, falling back to the project's persisted default audience.

clauses.subject: assertion-invalid
clauses.statement: A bad signature, a lapsed assertion, an untrusted issuer or audience, or a mapped claim absent from the assertion raises `ExchangeAssertionInvalid` and mints nothing.
clauses.why: because no credential exists whose subject the assertion did not verify

clauses.subject: material-missing
clauses.statement: An exchange configured with no verifying material raises `ExchangeMaterialMissing` and mints nothing.

clauses.subject: per-reader
clauses.statement: An embedding application holds no project-wide credential; per request it exchanges its signed-in reader's assertion for that reader's short-lived credential and reads as them.

clauses.subject: no-cross-reader
clauses.statement: An exchanged credential serves only the reader it was minted for.

clauses.subject: holder-binding
clauses.statement: An exchange request carrying a `DPoP` proof over `POST /auth/exchange` and its body mints a credential whose `cnf.jkt` is the proof key's thumbprint, the proof checked as {{authority.verify.possession-binding}}.

clauses.subject: bearer-mint
clauses.statement: An exchange request carrying no proof mints a credential with no confirmation claim, its lifetime clamped by {{authority.exchange.lifetime-ceiling}}, so a network face admits it under {{authority.verify.bearer-lifetime}}.

clauses.subject: holder-proof-invalid
clauses.statement: An exchange request whose proof fails any check of {{authority.exchange.holder-binding}}, a replayed nonce included, raises `ExchangeHolderProofInvalid` and mints nothing.
clauses.why: because a proof the face cannot verify proves no key, and a bearer minted in its place hands replayable bytes to a caller asking for a bound credential

clauses.subject: refresh
clauses.statement: A holder renews a served-face credential by exchanging a fresh assertion for a new credential with its own identifier and a full lifetime from the exchange instant.

clauses.subject: no-extension
clauses.statement: No surface extends a minted credential's expiry: a minted credential presented as the exchange assertion raises {{authority.exchange.assertion-invalid}}, and {{authority.attenuate.expiry-extended}} bounds every derived child.

clauses.subject: write-time
clauses.statement: Redaction runs inside the writer before columnar encoding. Each rule drops its value or transforms it into a policy-defined substitute: keyed digest, token, prefix or generalized band.

clauses.subject: rule
clauses.statement: A rule names a table, a column, one operation and that operation's argument.

clauses.subject: pipeline-wide
clauses.statement: A rule set declared on a pipeline binds every table the pipeline lands, child tables included.

clauses.subject: after-normalization
clauses.statement: Redaction runs after relational normalization; a rule naming a parent column reaches values shredded into child tables.

clauses.subject: before-the-record
clauses.statement: A canonical source writer shapes, normalizes and removes values before recording an opaque admitted payload; neither its inline record nor its blob contains the removed source value.

clauses.subject: refetch
clauses.statement: A fresh pipeline execution over a table under removal rules reads the source again.

clauses.subject: at-rest-scope
clauses.statement: Stored bytes lack only write-time-removed values. A column protected at query time alone is cleartext in storage and readable with the object-store credential.

clauses.subject: summarize-only
clauses.statement: A `summarize_only` column stores its text whole; the flag lands at write time and travels with the column, binding every surface through {{authority.mask.verbatim-quote}}.

clauses.subject: rules-per-pipeline
clauses.statement: A pipeline carries at most 256 entries in its removal rule set.
clauses.why: because a longer rule set is a policy the operator cannot review

clauses.subject: pattern-bytes
clauses.statement: One removal pattern carries at most 4 KiB of source text.
clauses.why: because pattern compilation cost must remain bounded before a writer starts

clauses.subject: compiled-pattern-size
clauses.statement: Each Thompson NFA compiled for one removal pattern occupies at most 1 MiB.
clauses.why: because expanded repetitions must not allocate unbounded matcher state

clauses.subject: pattern-refusal
clauses.statement: Unsupported syntax, Unicode word boundaries, empty matches or a pattern past {{authority.redact.pattern-bytes}} or {{authority.redact.compiled-pattern-size}} raises `EnforceRedactionInvalid` at declaration.
clauses.why: because a failed matcher cannot silently leave a declared sensitive value intact

clauses.subject: in-value
clauses.statement: Pattern removal rewrites the union of all matches in one linear pass, merging overlapping matches into one span; whole-value removal rewrites one cell. JSON paths select object keys, array indices or every array item; unselected values remain unchanged.

clauses.subject: every-land-entry
clauses.statement: A canonical project declaration binds direct and staged writers even when their callers omit its rules.

clauses.subject: combined-authority
clauses.statement: A destination's ordered canonical rule union obeys {{authority.redact.rules-per-pipeline}}; conflicting declared types, classes or policies and duplicate rules refuse before writing parts.
clauses.why: because an additional declaration cannot replace an earlier rule or its type and class authority

clauses.subject: normalized-authority
clauses.statement: Projects declaring protected relational normalization require canonical table bindings for ordinary writes; an undeclared destination enters through a declared root's complete normalization lineage or refuses before durable bytes.
clauses.why: because a child name cannot prove which source column its values descend from

clauses.subject: rewritten-identities
clauses.statement: Relational parent and child identities derive from rewritten source values; removed values contribute no retained identity digest.

clauses.subject: child-selector-lineage
clauses.statement: A normalized child mask selecting a sibling class requires typed sibling-row lineage; a group lacking that lineage refuses before writing any part.
clauses.why: because a source-row index cannot distinguish sibling values from different child rows

clauses.subject: pinned-plan
clauses.statement: A source plan's explicit removal list equals its complete canonical destination rules; an unbound or mismatched list refuses before source execution. Canonical removal still binds an omitted list.
clauses.why: because a content-hashed plan cannot promise rules that its writer ignores

clauses.subject: canonical-journal
clauses.statement: Canonical writer rules require {{authority.redact.before-the-record}} even when a caller's source plan omits its removal list; {{run.journal.redacting-source}} governs absent admission.
clauses.why: because caller omission cannot weaken a durable declaration's recording boundary

clauses.subject: relational-journal
clauses.statement: A protected relational source records its concrete rewritten root and child group, preserving declared root types, child lineage and {{authority.redact.rewritten-identities}} through {{run.journal.prepared-replay}}.

clauses.subject: prepared-payload
clauses.statement: A protected source cannot supply an admitted recording envelope; modified rows, types, destination or normalization fail canonical payload admission before staged parts.
clauses.why: because connector-controlled bytes cannot claim a writer's recording authority

clauses.subject: prepared-continuation
clauses.statement: Protected source continuations refuse before recording unless absent, exact terminal `{ next: null }` without more pages, or text unchanged by every canonical pattern; any canonical whole-value or JSON-path rule refuses text continuations.
clauses.why: because a source-controlled continuation can otherwise retain a removed value beside its rewritten rows

clauses.subject: prepared-clock
clauses.statement: A protected monotonic source proves complete clock-output lineage before execution opens; lineage reaching removed columns, including JSON-path targets, refuses. Protected relational clocks refuse without complete descendant lineage; independent clocks retain {{run.advance.watermark-shape}}.
clauses.why: because progress bytes cannot retain a value that its row removes

clauses.subject: recorded-body
clauses.statement: A store-driven job targeting canonical removal rules refuses before body execution without typed effect-result removal lineage; body calls record results before output landing.
clauses.why: because later row rewriting cannot remove earlier recorded effect results

clauses.subject: prepared-effects
clauses.statement: Canonical effect preparation produces opaque rewritten root and child groups; the paid record and staged group carry the same rewritten values and {{authority.redact.rewritten-identities}}.

clauses.subject: effect-scope
clauses.statement: A prepared effect binds canonical authority to its execution, row and effect entry key and composite projection identity; replay and staging require the independently issued scope, never authority inferred from decoded bytes.

clauses.subject: three-layers
clauses.statement: The reference monitor is three layers: write-time removal, the redistribution bound at push, and row-and-column restriction at query time. A request is authorized at each.

clauses.subject: complete-mediation
clauses.statement: Every read of stored rows traverses the layers. A path reaching stored rows outside a registered relation is a defect, never a documented limitation.

clauses.subject: protection-is-a-rewrite
clauses.statement: Protection is a rewrite in the data plane: predicates compiled into the statement, rewritten projections, a per-credential filter at the sync edge, zone floors. Admission decides entry alone.

clauses.subject: registered-relation
clauses.statement: The compiler emits one relation per granted table, bound to the table's bare name for the session's lifetime. Every retrieval arm reads through it.

clauses.subject: relation-order
clauses.statement: A registered relation applies, in order: mirrored permission semi-join, tenant equality, credential predicate, table policy, project default, table zone, then the column projection carrying masks and zone nulls.

clauses.subject: conjunctive-narrowing
clauses.statement: Steps conjoin: a surviving row survives each step alone, and appending a step removes rows and adds none.

clauses.subject: before-the-cut
clauses.statement: Every step, zone exclusion included, completes before a ranked result is cut to its requested size; visible positions carry no trace of a withheld row.

clauses.subject: vector-arm
clauses.statement: A sidecar vector index returns candidate identifiers, which re-join through the registered relation before contributing to a result.

clauses.subject: replica-again
clauses.statement: A caller holding a filtered replica is constrained again per query, the replica's bytes unchanged.

clauses.subject: session-build
clauses.statement: A session builds its relations at admission and rebuilds them when a revocation or a manifest change invalidates a grant it holds.

clauses.subject: relations-per-session
clauses.statement: A session carries at most 1024 entries in its relation set.
clauses.why: because a larger grant set is a mis-scoped credential

clauses.subject: grammar
clauses.statement: A row predicate is the typed boolean subset of SQL in Shapes: column references, comparisons, conjunction, disjunction, negation, membership lists, pattern matching, null tests and declared-safe scalar functions.

clauses.subject: outside-grammar
clauses.statement: Predicates parse at manifest load; a node outside the grammar raises `EnforcePredicateOutsideGrammar`, naming the node.

clauses.subject: subject-relation
clauses.statement: Subject claims reach a predicate as prepared-statement parameters through a session-scoped subject relation. A claim value carrying SQL syntax occupies a parameter slot and reaches no parser.

clauses.subject: exception
clauses.statement: An exception condition is a boolean expression over subject fields in the same grammar, bound the same way.

clauses.subject: override
