clauses.statement: A worker admits a `POST /submit` only when it carries an HMAC under the worker key over its timestamp and body, within {{surface.dispatch.callback-skew}}, naming a callback under its own `[control] relay`; any other submission raises `DispatchSubmitRejected` and starts nothing.
clauses.why: because an unsigned submission lets any caller start a step and have the worker sign heartbeats and callbacks for a route of its choosing

clauses.subject: submit-exhausted
clauses.statement: A step every listed worker refuses in turn at `POST /submit` fails its unit naming the last refusal, each worker tried once.
clauses.why: because a step bouncing between refusing workers holds its pool slot and exclusion key while never running

clauses.subject: heartbeat-lapse
clauses.statement: A heartbeat lapse past 60 s reschedules that worker's in-flight work onto another matching worker under the next attempt number.

clauses.subject: pool-bound
clauses.statement: A deployment's fire pool runs at most 4 units at once, `[control] pool` replacing the bound; a due unit past the bound stays armed and reports pending.
clauses.why: because one bound per deployment caps the process's concurrent pulls, where a bound per exclusion key caps nothing as pipelines are added

clauses.subject: admission-order
clauses.statement: Due units start by earliest next fire, then highest `[[pipeline]]` `priority`, an integer defaulting to 0, then the least recent of each unit's last run start and last dispatch, a unit with neither first, then id.

clauses.subject: refill
clauses.statement: A wake whose fire ends before its answer admits each unit its evaluation left pending into the freed slot, through the cadence lease; a unit falling due after the evaluation waits for the next wake.

clauses.subject: exclusion-key
clauses.statement: A unit's exclusion key is its pipeline id: a unit due while another under its key is in flight starts no second instance, and its next fire recomputes once the first ends.
clauses.why: because two fires of one pipeline race for one cursor

clauses.subject: export-quiesced
clauses.statement: A due unit whose head or a landing step writes a member of a publication, or a relation its producer reads, starts nothing while `contextful export group` holds that publication, and stays due, reporting pending.
clauses.why: because a producer commit between an export's frontier reads raises {{run.export.group-incompatible}}, and a deferred unit costs one beat where stopping serve costs every dispatch

clauses.subject: export-deferred-slot
clauses.statement: A deferred unit takes no pool slot and writes no dispatch record: its slot passes to the next unit in admission order, and it waits for the next beat or a wake's refill.
clauses.why: because a deferred unit holding its slot stops unrelated units for the whole export, and a recorded dispatch moves its fire past the instant it never ran

clauses.subject: export-claim
clauses.statement: A started unit writing a publication's inputs holds them shared from its start until it ends, so an export of that publication waits for it.
clauses.why: because serve admits a unit before its child commits, so a check at admission alone misses a unit already running

clauses.subject: export-claim-unread
clauses.statement: A unit whose publication inputs serve cannot compute claims every declared publication; a unit whose claim serve cannot take starts nothing and stays due, logging the error.
clauses.why: because an unclaimed unit starting during an export commits between the frontier reads {{run.export.group-incompatible}} rechecks

clauses.subject: lease-gated
clauses.statement: A serve process dispatches only while it holds its deployment's cadence lease; a process finding the lease held arms nothing and, under `--cycle`, exits naming the holder.
clauses.why: because two daemons reading one snapshot otherwise fire every due unit twice

clauses.subject: children-reaped
clauses.statement: A serve process starts each child run in its own process group; on `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, a `--cycle` exit or an unwind it signals each live group `SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL`s the remainder after 10 s, and exits once every child has.
clauses.why: because a child outliving its serve also outlives the cadence lease, and a second scheduler then fires the same pipeline concurrently

clauses.subject: fire-credential
clauses.statement: Under `--issuer-key`, serve mints each store-driven or synthesize child fire one credential for `svc://job/<name>` in the project's default zone, granting {{surface.dispatch.fire-reach}}, in that child's `CONTEXTFUL_TOKEN`; the seed reaches no child argument or variable.
clauses.why: because a serve outlives any credential the ceiling admits, and a credential minted per fire narrows each child to its own job's tables

clauses.subject: fire-reach
clauses.statement: A store-driven fire reaches `read` on its statement's relations and `write` on its `tables`; a synthesize fire reaches `read` on its source, its target and the declared entities table, and `write` on its target.
clauses.why: because a synthesize pass consolidates against live claims and resolves mentions against entities, and writes no table but its claims and their dead letters

clauses.subject: fire-credential-lifetime
clauses.statement: A fire credential lives 600 s, or {{authority.issue.ceiling}} when lower; the child admits it once at start.
clauses.why: because a fire admits its credential before its first read, and a short lifetime bounds a leaked fire credential's exposure

clauses.subject: fire-credential-pins
clauses.statement: Each child holding a minted fire credential also receives `CONTEXTFUL_ISSUER_PUBKEY`, the seed's public key, and `CONTEXTFUL_AUDIENCE`, the issuance policy's default audience the credential carries, replacing values serve inherited.
clauses.why: because the child admits its credential from inherited variables, and a pin or audience other than the minting one refuses every fire

clauses.subject: fire-credential-inherited
clauses.statement: A serve holding no `--issuer-key` passes its own `CONTEXTFUL_TOKEN` to each child it starts.

clauses.subject: fire-credential-missing
clauses.statement: A serve dispatching to child processes, whose applied snapshot schedules a store-driven or synthesize job, holding neither `--issuer-key` nor `CONTEXTFUL_TOKEN`, raises `FireCredentialMissing` at start and fires nothing.
clauses.why: because a missing credential otherwise fails every fire while the serve reports healthy

clauses.subject: fire-credential-zone
clauses.statement: A serve under `--issuer-key`, whose applied snapshot schedules a store-driven or synthesize job, under a root whose `[project.zone]` declares no `default`, raises `FireCredentialZoneUnset` at start and fires nothing.
clauses.why: because a credential signing no zone asserts an undeclared zone, which {{authority.place.undeclared}} admits nowhere but `*`, so every fire reads no row

clauses.subject: binding
clauses.statement: `[control.delegates.<name>]` binds a delegate by `url`, a `mode` of `call` or `submit`, and under `call` a `timeout`; a `store-driven` `body = { delegate = "<name>" }` naming no bound delegate raises `JobDelegateUnbound` at arm or fire.

clauses.subject: host
clauses.statement: A delegate `url` is `http` to a loopback host or the `contextful.delegate` virtual host, carrying no credential; any other spelling raises `DelegateHostRefused` at startup and arms nothing.
clauses.why: because the stock container reaches a delegate only through a loopback relay or the deploy's outbound interception, and a public URL turns daemon configuration into egress
scenarios: WHEN a delegate `url` names a host that is neither loopback nor the virtual host, THEN startup refuses and arms nothing.

clauses.subject: envelope
clauses.statement: A delegate request carries `job`, `execution_id`, `step`, `input_hash`, `idempotency_key` under {{run.journal.idempotency-key}}, `attempt`, `entity` with namespace, key and fence, `as_of`, `version` when fired from an applied snapshot, `pins`, `tables`, the input `row` and `deadline`.
clauses.why: because a delegate holds no state of its own, and a request naming its version and fence lets it refuse before a paid call

clauses.subject: signed
clauses.statement: A request is signed under the worker key over `call`, its timestamp and body, and an answer over `answer`, the request's `idempotency_key`, its timestamp and body, each as {{surface.dispatch.submit-signed}} signs a submission.
clauses.why: because an answer bound to its request cannot be replayed onto another item's call

clauses.subject: rejected
clauses.statement: An answer unsigned or skewed past {{surface.dispatch.callback-skew}} raises `DelegateAnswerRejected` and closes the attempt `Transient`; one outside {{surface.delegate.outcome}} or over {{surface.dispatch.step-result}} raises it and closes the attempt `Permanent`.
clauses.why: because an unsigned answer lets any process on the loopback land rows, and a malformed one cannot change on retry

clauses.subject: call-mode
clauses.statement: Under `call`, one request per attempt holds its connection open and the response body is the attempt's answer; a response arriving after the delegate's `timeout` closes the attempt `Transient`, and its late body records nothing.
scenarios: WHEN a delegate answers `ok` with rows for one item and the daemon restarts before that item's landing commits, THEN the resumed item lands the recorded rows and the delegate receives no second request.

clauses.subject: status
clauses.statement: A `call` response with a status other than `200` closes the attempt `Transient`, whatever its body; a terminal receipt follows a signed `permanent` answer, a `Permanent` rejection or an exhausted budget under {{run.items.retry-budget}}.
clauses.why: because a refusal before work is deployment drift an operator fixes, and a terminal receipt outlives the fix

clauses.subject: call-timeout
clauses.statement: A `call` delegate's `timeout` defaults to 300 s.

clauses.subject: call-timeout-ceiling
clauses.statement: A `call` `timeout` above 3600 s raises `DelegateTimeoutRefused` at validation.
clauses.why: because an item holding a `max_in_flight` slot for over an hour is a stalled delegate, not a slow one

clauses.subject: submit-mode
clauses.statement: Under `submit`, the request is a {{surface.dispatch.worker-target}} submission answered at once; the delegate heartbeats under {{surface.dispatch.heartbeat-beat}}, posts its answer to the callback, and a lapse follows {{surface.dispatch.heartbeat-lapse}}.

clauses.subject: outcome
clauses.statement: An answer is `ok` with rows per declared output table, `defer` with a `retry_at` instant, `transient`, or `permanent` with a reason; `ok` lands as {{run.items.completion}}, `defer` parks, and `transient` and `permanent` follow {{run.items.retry-budget}}.

clauses.subject: defer-parks
clauses.statement: A `defer` parks the item until its `retry_at` under {{run.items.retry-budget}}; the first fire after that instant re-admits it under {{run.items.replay}}, no run sleeps on it, and a row of a job without `isolated_items` closes `Transient` instead.
clauses.why: because a provider budget clears on the provider's clock, and a slot held through the wait starves every other entity
scenarios: WHEN a delegate answers `defer` with a `retry_at` ten minutes ahead, THEN the item's failed-attempt count is unchanged and the first fire after that instant sends the request again.

clauses.subject: currency
clauses.statement: The fence in {{surface.delegate.envelope}} is checked immediately before the request under {{run.items.fence}}; under `submit`, the heartbeat `GET` answers the current attempt and fence, so a delegate learns before a paid call whether it is superseded.
clauses.why: because a delegate that pays after its owner was replaced spends a call whose answer nothing records

clauses.subject: version
clauses.statement: A binding's optional `version` joins the item's owner pins as a body dependency, so a changed version opens a fresh execution identity and a pending item under the old one refuses as {{run.own.pinned-plan-changed}}.
clauses.why: because a prompt or model change inside a delegate otherwise resumes recorded work under new semantics

clauses.subject: clocks
clauses.statement: Signature timestamps on a request and an answer ride each side's system clock; the `deadline` and a `defer` wait ride the engine's instant.
clauses.why: because the engine's instant is injectable while a delegate shares only wall time, and a wait measured on two clocks never fires

clauses.subject: submit-relay
clauses.statement: A `submit` binding on a daemon declaring no `[control] relay` or holding no worker key refuses at startup, as {{surface.dispatch.worker-key}} refuses a worker list.
clauses.why: because a submit delegate posts its answer to the awakeable route the relay binds

clauses.subject: secret-in-document
clauses.statement: A credential value typed into a configuration field raises `SecretMaterialInDocument`; the document holds references and the backend holds material.
clauses.why: because a value in the document reaches every daemon and replica that reads a snapshot

clauses.subject: connector-upload
clauses.statement: An artifact uploaded through the operator surface raises `ConnectorUploadRefused`; the surface references registered connectors by id and version.
clauses.why: because publishing into the registry runs a separate signed path

clauses.subject: store-draft
clauses.statement: An Admin edit validates a complete control document and saves one store-scoped draft bound to its applied version, verified operator and random nonce, leaving the applied pointer unchanged.

clauses.subject: version-race
clauses.statement: An apply whose compare-and-swap loses raises `ManifestVersionConflict`, reloads the winning version and reapplies its pending edits onto it, overwriting no applied version.

clauses.subject: validation
clauses.statement: A document failing engine validation raises `ApplyValidationRefused` and claims no version.
clauses.why: because a snapshot store holding a version daemons refuse to arm stalls every daemon reading it

clauses.subject: owner-unconfigured
clauses.statement: An owner with no storage configured or no credential raises `ConfigOwnerUnconfigured`, answered `503`; no local writer substitutes for the store-scoped API.

clauses.subject: weak-conditional-backend
clauses.statement: A configuration owner or catalog backend whose conditional replacement is not linearizable raises `ConditionalWriteUnsupported` at startup or open.

clauses.subject: uninitialized-store
clauses.statement: An edit or apply against a store that has taken no explicit guarded import, an empty store included, raises `StoreNotInitialized`, answered `409`.

clauses.subject: local-claim
clauses.statement: A local control plane validates and claims `manifest@v<N>.toml` in its snapshot directory, `.contextful/control/<project>/` unless `[control] snapshot_dir` names one, on its own; `contextful pipeline apply` is that apply, and no hosted plane sits on its path.
clauses.why: because {{topology.coordinate.air-gap}} holds a single-node deployment to reach no process outside itself

clauses.subject: synced-attestation
clauses.statement: In a project with `[sync]`, import and apply admit an admin capability, then sign a receipt over the project, version, predecessor receipt digest and snapshot digest through {{authority.issue.signing-port}}.

clauses.subject: receipt-message
clauses.statement:
A JSON control receipt carries `format: 1`, signer public key and signature over UTF-8 `contextful-control-v1
<project>
<version>
<parent-or-minus>
<snapshot-sha256>
<signer>
`; its parent is `-` only for the first version.
scenarios: WHEN a receipt's parent or snapshot digest changes after signing, THEN its signature does not verify.

clauses.subject: receipt-digest
clauses.statement: A predecessor and the bucket head name the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of a receipt's RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes.

clauses.subject: receipt-file
clauses.statement: A synced claim writes immutable `receipt@v<N>.json` beside its snapshot before advancing the applied pointer.
scenarios: WHEN signing fails during a synced import, THEN neither the snapshot nor the pointer names the version.

clauses.subject: attestation-unavailable
clauses.statement: A synced import or apply lacking an admitted admin capability or issuer signing port raises `ControlAttestationUnavailable` and claims no version.
scenarios: WHEN a synced apply presents no admin capability, THEN no version or receipt is claimed.

clauses.subject: guarded-import
clauses.statement: `contextful pipeline import` claims v1 from the declared pipelines while the snapshot directory holds no version; an import over a directory holding a version claims nothing, names that version and exits zero.
clauses.why: because a restart on a warm disk runs import before apply, and a refusal there stops the restart
scenarios: WHEN a warm synced node restarts through pull, import, apply and push, THEN import claims nothing, apply reports the version unchanged, and the restart succeeds.

clauses.subject: adopt-before-claim
clauses.statement: Import or apply over a snapshot directory holding no version first adopts a pulled head verified under {{surface.reconcile.issuer-pin}} against the verb's `--public-key` and meeting {{surface.apply.self-valid}}, though the declarations drop its pipelines or jobs; an import that adopts claims nothing.
clauses.why: because a replacement host claiming a fresh v1 diverges from the bucket's signed head, and the claim that follows removes what a release dropped
scenarios: WHEN a cold node pulls a signed bucket head and runs import, THEN import claims nothing, and apply of one added pipeline claims the head's successor and pushes.
WHEN a release changes only the schedules of pipelines a build job runs `after`, THEN a cold node adopts the old head and apply claims its successor.
WHEN a release removes a pipeline with the build job whose `after` names it, THEN a cold node adopts the old head, apply claims its successor, and the next cold node adopts that.

clauses.subject: external-snapshot
clauses.statement: Import and full apply retain validated `[[external]]` declarations in the snapshot; a pipeline-only apply preserves them, and a pipeline-only editor refuses to discard them under {{surface.apply.validation}}.
clauses.why: because Admin reads external steps from the applied version, beside the jobs {{surface.fire.job-snapshot}} retains

clauses.subject: self-valid
clauses.statement: Import, apply and adoption validate a snapshot's document, build plans and each job's `after` against that snapshot's own pipelines, so apply signs no head its adoption refuses.
clauses.why: because a signed head failing its own adoption refuses every cold start until a reset

clauses.subject: draft-claim
clauses.statement: An Admin apply rechecks the configured store owner, validates its saved draft again, and claims that draft through the owner's version compare-and-swap.

clauses.subject: operator-attestation
clauses.statement: An Admin mutation lacking a fresh console signature over its verified operator, route and body, or reusing a nonce held in store control state across restarts, raises `ControlOperatorAttestationInvalid` before changing the document.
clauses.why: because a shared store capability cannot identify the person who used the console

clauses.subject: draft-table-contracts
clauses.statement: Pipeline editing preserves standalone table metadata from the draft's expected immutable version; apply regenerates that metadata and refuses an altered saved draft under {{surface.apply.validation}} before advancing the pointer.

clauses.subject: draft-absent
clauses.statement: An Admin apply finding no validated store draft raises `ControlDraftAbsent` and changes no applied version.
clauses.why: because an absent draft supplies no document for the version claim

clauses.subject: served-admin-grant
clauses.statement: A served `/control/*` request whose admitted credential holds no Admin grant over `*` without a tenant scope raises `ControlAdminGrantMissing`, answered `403`, before its handler runs.
clauses.why: because the control document arms work over every table and tenant of the store

clauses.subject: served-malformed
clauses.statement: A served Admin edit or apply whose body is not a JSON object holding exactly its route's fields raises `ControlRequestMalformed`, answered `400`, and changes nothing.
clauses.why: because an absent or extra field leaves the operator's intended version or draft ambiguous

clauses.subject: served-unavailable
clauses.statement: A served control request failing with no authority or surface refusal raises `ControlUnavailable`, answered `503`, and returns no internal error text.
clauses.why: because a storage or owner fault message can disclose paths and endpoints to the console

clauses.subject: region-entries
clauses.statement: A residency allow-set holds at most 16 entries.

clauses.subject: region-mismatch
clauses.statement: A configured resource resolving to a region the policy omits raises `EnforceRegionMismatch` at startup, and the runtime serves nothing.

clauses.subject: site-regions
clauses.statement: A push records the pushing site's residency allow-set in the bucket manifest; a push finding a differing set another site recorded, an absent one included, raises `ResidencySitesDiverge` and commits nothing.

clauses.subject: routes
clauses.statement: `POST /connections` creates, `POST /connections/{id}/pause` pauses, and `DELETE /connections/{id}` deletes a connection outside the operator-only `/control/*` routes.

clauses.subject: create
clauses.statement: A served connection create binds an admitted tenant, principal, source selection, secret name and pipeline id in one versioned control claim under {{surface.apply.version-race}}.

clauses.subject: authority
clauses.statement: A connection mutation requires an admitted write credential for its tenant and principal, checked on the request before reading and on the standing record before changing it; a mismatch raises `ConnectionScopeDenied`.
clauses.why: because a caller-controlled tenant or principal could otherwise point a pipeline at another user's credential
scenarios: WHEN a caller names another tenant's connection, THEN `ConnectionScopeDenied` changes no control version.

clauses.subject: idempotent-create
clauses.statement: Repeating create with the same connection id and declaration returns the standing version; a differing declaration raises `ConnectionIdConflict` without replacing it.
clauses.why: because a retried consent callback must not produce a second scheduled pipeline
scenarios: WHEN a consent callback retries the same declaration, THEN one pipeline and schedule remain.

clauses.subject: answer
clauses.statement: Create answers `201` with the claimed connection, version and state; a repeat, pause or delete answers `200`; each claim advances the version by one, deleting an active connection claims twice, and a repeat claims nothing.

clauses.subject: malformed
clauses.statement: A create body outside `id`, `tenant`, `principal`, `file_ids`, `refresh_secret` and `schedule`, an unreadable schedule, or a pause or delete body other than `{}` raises `ConnectionRequestMalformed` and claims nothing.
clauses.why: because a connection record binds exactly the declared selection, so an unrecognised field cannot ride along into the pipeline
scenarios: WHEN a create body carries an OAuth `code` beside its secret name, THEN `ConnectionRequestMalformed` claims no version.

clauses.subject: unknown
clauses.statement: A pause or delete naming no standing connection raises `ConnectionUnknown`; a deleted id stays bound to its retired record, and create refuses its reuse as {{surface.connection.idempotent-create}}.
clauses.why: because a retired id reused by a new declaration restarts a pipeline whose credential is revoked
scenarios: WHEN a deleted connection is paused, THEN `ConnectionUnknown` changes no version.

clauses.subject: pause
clauses.statement: Pause disarms the connection's schedule and prevents new fires; an in-flight fire reaches its run cancellation boundary under {{run.cancel.two-grains}}.
scenarios: WHEN a connection is paused before its due instant, THEN no new Drive fire starts.

clauses.subject: delete
clauses.statement: Delete first pauses the connection, revokes its credential under {{connector.principal-secrets.disconnect}}, then retires its pipeline and schedule through a versioned claim.

clauses.subject: schedule-scale
clauses.statement: Connection schedules share {{surface.dispatch.pool-bound}} and {{surface.arm.next-fire-from-history}}; each connection holds one armed entry rather than one timer or thread.

clauses.subject: consent-boundary
clauses.statement: The calling application owns Google authorization, callback and code exchange; connection create receives only a secret name, never an OAuth code or token.

clauses.subject: page-routes
clauses.statement: The console serves Query at `/query` with `/query/api/*` and Admin at `/admin` with `/admin/api/*`.

clauses.subject: identity-gate
clauses.statement: Cloudflare Access gates hosted pages by default; a deployment without Access uses Cognito managed password login and first-party sessions.

clauses.subject: page-grants
clauses.statement: The server maps each verified Access application audience or Cognito group to Query and Admin grants and verifies the matching grant on every page and API request.
scenarios: WHEN a verified operator holds only a Query grant, THEN Query admits the session and Admin refuses its page and API requests.

clauses.subject: query-surface
clauses.statement: Query presents one composer, one transcript and widgets for returned rows.
scenarios: WHEN an operator asks on Query, THEN the question and grounded answer occupy one transcript beside its widgets.

clauses.subject: saved-transcript
clauses.statement: Query restores a saved transcript only under the verified operator and reading session that wrote it, and only for a store the stores route still lists.
clauses.why: because a shared browser tab otherwise hands one operator's answer rows to the next
scenarios: WHEN a second operator opens Query in the tab where another saved a transcript, THEN Query restores none of its answers or rows.

clauses.subject: narrow-sidebar
clauses.statement: On a viewport too narrow for the sidebar, a header control opens it as a drawer, keeping chat creation, switching and deletion reachable.
clauses.why: because a hidden sidebar with no replacement strands every chat control on a phone
scenarios: WHEN Query renders on a phone-width viewport, THEN a header control opens the chat list with its create, switch and delete controls.

clauses.subject: engine-faces
clauses.statement: Query reaches the governed read face; Admin reaches workflow state and sends edit or apply through a server-held control capability.

clauses.subject: ungated-route
clauses.statement: An anonymous hosted console route serving page or API content instead of the declared identity gate raises `ConsoleRouteUngated` at deploy probe.
scenarios: WHEN an anonymous deploy probe receives `/query` or `/admin/api/workflows` content, THEN it raises `ConsoleRouteUngated`.

clauses.subject: wrong-page
clauses.statement: A page or API request without a verified Access assertion or Cognito session granting that page raises `ConsolePageForbidden` and dispatches nothing.
scenarios: WHEN a Query-only operator requests `/admin/api/workflows`, THEN it raises `ConsolePageForbidden` without dispatching.

clauses.subject: admin-grant
clauses.statement: An Admin edit or apply without a server-held admin capability raises `ConsoleAdminGrantMissing` and reaches no control call.
scenarios: WHEN an Admin operator applies a document without the server-held admin capability, THEN it raises `ConsoleAdminGrantMissing` without a control call.

clauses.subject: source-list
clauses.statement: Admin lists ingest sources from the applied control document, naming each connector, destination, schedule or trigger, applied version and latest run outcome.
clauses.why: because the applied document owns source identity and configuration

clauses.subject: source-draft
clauses.statement: Admin adds a source through the version-bound edit and apply path of {{surface.open-console.engine-faces}}, with a source form and a raw TOML fallback.

clauses.subject: source-preservation
clauses.statement: Adding a source through {{surface.open-console.source-draft}} preserves the applied jobs, models and external steps.

clauses.subject: source-validation
clauses.statement: Saving and applying a source validates connector availability, required configuration, destination compatibility and duplicate identity under {{surface.apply.validation}}; refusals name the affected field and a correction, and leave the applied version unchanged.
scenarios: WHEN an HTTP source draft lacks its endpoint, THEN Admin identifies `source.config.endpoint` and the applied document retains its version.

clauses.subject: source-first-run
clauses.statement: Admin shows the applied version's first and latest source fires, aggregating rows and failures across destinations; absent matching run evidence, the source remains pending after apply.
clauses.why: because claiming configuration establishes no execution outcome
scenarios: WHEN an identical source configuration claims another version, THEN older-version runs leave its first-run state pending.

clauses.subject: source-run-evidence
clauses.statement: A source fire binds its loaded applied version, source identity, configuration digest and destination run identities in the operational record; first and latest summaries travel through {{store.push.run-state}}.
clauses.why: because a pipeline name or start time alone can associate an older configuration's run

clauses.subject: registry-unreadable
clauses.statement: A `CONTEXTFUL_STORES_JSON` value that does not parse raises `StoreRegistryUnreadable` at startup, and no built-in store stands in for the configured set.

clauses.subject: malformed-entry
clauses.statement: One entry that does not decode raises `StoreEntryMalformed` naming it, and is dropped while its siblings are served.

clauses.subject: reserved-id
clauses.statement: A configured entry claiming either built-in id raises `StoreIdReserved`.
clauses.why: because the entry otherwise reads the fixture's rows under its own name

clauses.subject: authored-name
clauses.statement: An entry carrying its own credential or binding name raises `StoreNameAuthored`.

clauses.subject: shared-registry
clauses.statement: Query, Admin and the embeddable client library resolve store identities from the same deployment registry.

clauses.subject: workflow-canvas
clauses.statement: Admin projects the store-published pipelines, jobs, models, publications and external steps as one node–edge graph under {{surface.visualize.dataflow-edges}}, with each pipeline's schedule, steps and latest run outcome.

clauses.subject: dataflow-edges
clauses.statement: The published workflow lists edges `{from, to, via}` between typed node ids: pipeline and build-job `after`, pipeline to produced table, table or model to its reading model or job, build job to model, job to written table and publication.
clauses.why: because a graph the client infers from names draws edges the store never declared

clauses.subject: external-step
clauses.statement: Admin draws each `[[external]]` declaration as a node marked as run outside the engine, joined by its inputs and outputs; the engine runs, schedules and records nothing for it.
clauses.why: because work around the store belongs on the canvas without becoming a job kind {{surface.fire.job-kind-unknown}} refuses

clauses.subject: external-shape
clauses.statement: An `[[external]]` declares `name`, optional `label`, and `inputs` and `outputs` of typed references `table:<name>`, `pipeline:<id>` or `job:<name>`; any other key fails {{surface.apply.validation}}.
clauses.why: because a typed reference keeps a table and a pipeline sharing a name distinct, and no command key makes it runnable

clauses.subject: external-unbound
clauses.statement: An `[[external]]` input or output lacking a `table:`, `pipeline:` or `job:` prefix, or naming no declared table, model, pipeline or job, raises `ExternalStepUnbound` at validation.
clauses.why: because an edge to nothing draws a line the operator cannot trace

clauses.subject: external-collision
clauses.statement: An `[[external]]` whose `name` repeats another external's name, a job's name or a pipeline's id raises `ExternalStepCollision` at validation.
clauses.why: because one name labelling two graph nodes leaves the reader to guess which one ran

clauses.subject: operational-record
clauses.statement: Admin's inspector, pack file surface and learnings view present the store-published operational record.

clauses.subject: listing-page
clauses.statement: One listing call answers at most 1000 entries, flags truncation, and counts the keys the read route declines to serve.

clauses.subject: stdio-credential
clauses.statement: The process transport requires a verified capability token; `--owner` selects its signed owner claim. An absent token raises `StdioCredentialMissing` before protocol framing and never resolves to owner context.

clauses.subject: store-selector
clauses.statement: The child's working directory selects the store by walking up to the project manifest; finding none raises `StoreSelectorAbsent` and exits before writing any protocol framing.

clauses.subject: owner-flag
clauses.statement: A process `--owner` admits the local owner context only with a verified signed claim bound to the selected store and an unrestricted read grant; any other credential raises `OwnerCredentialInvalid` before protocol framing.

clauses.subject: redactor-lookahead
clauses.statement: The streaming redactor buffers 128 chars across each chunk boundary, and no denylist entry is longer than the buffer.
clauses.why: because an identifier split between two chunks otherwise passes unredacted

clauses.subject: unanswerable-suggestion
clauses.statement: A suggested prompt whose answer under these rules is a decline raises `ConsoleSuggestionUnanswerable` when the suggestion set is built.

clauses.subject: stream-redaction
clauses.statement: The server redacts each streamed model chunk before Query emits prose to the operator.

clauses.subject: ungrounded-answer
clauses.statement: A path composing answer prose in a turn holding no tool result raises `ConsoleUngroundedAnswer`.

clauses.subject: unadmitted-tool
clauses.statement: A call naming a tool the turn's packs do not admit raises `ConsoleToolNotAdmitted` and dispatches nothing.

clauses.subject: mutating-tool
clauses.statement: The console's query endpoint admits a read subset: a client-reachable path naming a write raises `ConsoleMutatingToolRequested`. The one write a turn performs is authored on the server.

clauses.subject: org-face-read-only
clauses.statement: A pack registering a write tool on an organization-wide face raises `ConsoleWriteToolOnOrgFace` at startup, naming the pack and the tool, and the face serves nothing.

clauses.subject: direct-file-read
clauses.statement: A table function resolving a path straight against stored bytes raises `ConsoleFileAccessDirect` on this surface.

clauses.subject: mint-refused
clauses.statement: A refused mint raises `ConsoleTokenExchangeRefused`. A store carrying a shared credential falls back to it; one carrying none surfaces the refusal to the reader.

clauses.subject: sources-per-turn
clauses.statement: A source list carries at most 8 entries.

clauses.subject: sources-block
clauses.statement: Every grounded answer includes a sources block citing only the governed results its admitted read tools returned.

clauses.subject: planner-reached-memory
clauses.statement: Scaffolding and every deterministic fallback cover data tables; scaffolding naming a memory relation raises `ConsolePlannerReachedMemory`.

clauses.subject: code-path-bounds
clauses.statement: The code path reads at most 5000 rows per data table and stops after 10 s.

clauses.subject: overlay-cache
clauses.statement: The overlay caches for 5 min, a miss included.

clauses.subject: overlay-length
clauses.statement: An overlay is truncated at 8000 chars.

clauses.subject: turn-flow
clauses.statement: A Query turn plans over admitted read tools, replans once after an unanswered first round, and synthesizes from the resulting governed rows.

clauses.subject: overlay-audience
clauses.statement: A store's prompt overlay reaches the operator-facing synthesis text and stays outside the planner's text.

clauses.subject: unparseable
clauses.statement: A vantage that is neither a calendar day nor an instant raises `ConsoleVantageUnparseable`, answered `400`.

clauses.subject: web-bound-unparseable
clauses.statement: A web leg whose bound fails to parse fails that leg and raises `ConsoleWebBoundUnparseable`.

clauses.subject: sample-labels
clauses.statement: A table's arrivals contribute at most 3 entries of sampled label.

clauses.subject: discovered-chips
clauses.statement: Query builds pre-question chips from described tables admitted to the reader's zone and humanizes their table labels.

clauses.subject: insights-panel
clauses.statement: The insights panel presents row counts returned by the reader's table descriptions.
clauses.why: because a row count from the read face already reflects the reader's relation

clauses.subject: file-gallery
clauses.statement: The file gallery presents only paths returned by the reader's governed file listing and previews them through the read face.

clauses.subject: gallery-path-unlisted
clauses.statement: A gallery preview naming a path absent from the governed file listing under the request's `as_of` raises `ConsoleGalleryPathUnlisted` before preview dispatch.
clauses.why: because the browser must not turn an arbitrary path into a store read
scenarios: WHEN a Query client requests a path absent from the reader's bound file listing, THEN it raises `ConsoleGalleryPathUnlisted` without a preview call.

clauses.subject: distillation
clauses.statement: After the answer streams, a second pass distils the exchange into at most 3 entries shaped `{subject, key, learning}`, zero included.

clauses.subject: unscoped
clauses.statement: A distilled conclusion landing without the reading-session scope raises `ConsoleLearningUnscoped`.

clauses.subject: write-refused
clauses.statement: A served claim write that refuses or returns no scope-bound receipt raises `ConsoleLearningWriteRefused` to Query before answer publication.
clauses.why: because a failed write cannot count as a durable learning

clauses.subject: subject-resolution
clauses.statement: Distillation preserves the subject it observes; recall resolves that subject through entity matching.

clauses.subject: client-authored-view
clauses.statement: A view specification arriving from a client, or composed by the model, raises `ConsoleViewNotServerBuilt`.

clauses.subject: component-choice
clauses.statement: One row with one measure draws a metric; a date column with a measure over 3 rows on distinct days draws a line; anything else draws a table offering a bar view.

clauses.subject: older-transcript
clauses.statement: A client reading a transcript with an unknown component-union member renders its view as a table.

clauses.subject: absence-is-earned
clauses.statement: The card needs a session with no turns, at present time, a live conclusion, an arrived row matching an interest, and a derivation inside its budget. An error or timeout raises `ConsoleBriefUnavailable`, and no card renders.

clauses.subject: topic-tier
clauses.statement: The topic tier needs at least 2 tokens shared between the conclusion's subject and text and the row's label and topics, one of them naming the subject.

clauses.subject: card-subjects
clauses.statement: A card carries at most 3 subjects.

clauses.subject: articles-per-subject
clauses.statement: A subject carries at most 3 entries of matched article.

clauses.subject: catchup-window
clauses.statement: The backend caps the requested window at 7 d.

clauses.subject: greeting
clauses.statement: Query derives a greeting card from arrived rows matching live conclusions in a turnless present-time session.

clauses.subject: share-affordance
clauses.statement: A surface offering a share control on access-explanation output raises `VisibilityShareAffordance`.

clauses.subject: askerless-audience
clauses.statement: A scheduled job posting to an audience under a service identity raises `VisibilityAskerlessAudience`, naming the destination; a scheduled post's corpus is narrowed in the reviewed manifest to what the destination reaches.

clauses.subject: one-operator-principal
clauses.statement: An answer uses one operator's credential; the console offers no room-intersection principal.

clauses.subject: package
clauses.statement: The policy model is a Lean package rooted at `formal/`: `lakefile.toml` declares one `lean_lib` target and no `require` stanza, and `lean-toolchain` names one exact release string.

clauses.subject: declared-dependency
clauses.statement: A `require` stanza in the policy package's `lakefile.toml` reaching any external library raises `FormalPackageDependency`, naming the library.

clauses.subject: toolchain-drift
clauses.statement: A build whose resolved toolchain string differs from the pinned one raises `ProofToolchainDrift`, printing both strings.

clauses.subject: build-cost
clauses.statement: A cold elaboration of the package completes within 60 s and writes at most 2048 KiB of artifacts.
clauses.why: because the check runs on every change

clauses.subject: build-command
clauses.statement: `lake build` at the package root elaborates every declaration and writes the environment the audit reads.

clauses.subject: module-layout
clauses.statement: Five modules carry the package — the layer algebra, placement with the floor, the authority mapping, connector host containment and statement execution — and the library root re-exports all five.

clauses.subject: layer
clauses.statement: A layer is a total function from a row identifier to `Bool`; `composed` folds a list of layers by conjunction, admitting a row when every member admits it.

clauses.subject: floor
clauses.statement: An allow-set is a decidable predicate over a placement value; `floor` intersects a list of allow-sets pointwise, and `floor []` admits every caller as the unit of that fold.

clauses.subject: placement-inductive
clauses.statement: The declared placement is an inductive type carrying its identifier inside the constructor, with one case per category the manifest admits and one case for an absent declaration.

clauses.subject: unmodelled-constructor
clauses.statement: A category the manifest admits with no case in the placement inductive raises `UnmodelledConstructor` at elaboration, naming the category.

clauses.subject: total-definitions
clauses.statement: Every definition is total and computable: none is marked `partial`, `noncomputable` or `opaque`, and decidable equality on each finite enumeration is derived.

clauses.subject: from-the-spec
clauses.statement: Each definition is written from the specification text and derived from no engine source.
clauses.why: because a definition copied from code makes every theorem restate the code instead of checking the specification

clauses.subject: out-of-model
clauses.statement: The policy package defines no credential bytes, signature verification, SQL semantics, journal write, process state or attacker observation, and no theorem reaches one.

clauses.subject: protocol-package
clauses.statement: The protocol model is a second Lean 4 package rooted at `formal/protocol/`, beside the policy package, pinned to the same `lean-toolchain` string, with one `lean_lib` target, one `lean_exe` target and no `require` stanza.

clauses.subject: protocol-model
clauses.statement: The protocol model is a total, computable step function over lease acquisition, renewal, expiry and release, the fenced compare-and-swap on the catalog row and the cursor object, holder pause, message delay and crash.

clauses.subject: protocol-safety
clauses.statement: Four invariants are Lean theorems over every reachable state: one lease holder per fence, fences only increase, no commit lands carrying a fence below the highest granted, and release keeps the lease object and its fence.

clauses.subject: protocol-theorems
clauses.statement: Each protocol invariant theorem is a required constant in the protocol package's inventory, audited by {{assurance.audit-assumptions.check-command}} against the same allowlist.

clauses.subject: protocol-check
clauses.statement: The gate evaluates every invariant on each state reached by every step sequence over three nodes and four lease generations; a breaking state raises `ProtocolInvariantViolated`, printing the shortest sequence reaching it.

clauses.subject: protocol-pins
clauses.statement: {{store.lease.stale-fence}} and {{store.lease.pointer-fence}} pin to the protocol model's invariant theorem `no_commit_below_granted`.
clauses.why: because the model's guarded objects are the catalog row and the cursor object, and a snapshot's sidecars lie outside it

clauses.subject: composition-sound
clauses.statement: `composed_sound`: a row the fold over a list admits is admitted by every member of that list.

clauses.subject: narrowing
clauses.statement: `composed_narrows`: a row admitted by `l :: ls` is admitted by `ls`.
clauses.why: because appending a layer then removes rows and adds none

clauses.subject: order-is-specified
clauses.statement: The composition theorem ranges over the single order {{authority.compose.relation-order}} fixes, and filtering then masking is a different relation from masking then filtering.

clauses.subject: commutation-claim
clauses.statement: A claim that the enforcement stages commute raises `CommutationClaimed`.

clauses.subject: placement-is-a-layer
clauses.statement: `zone_layer_sound`: with the placement check as one more list member, a row the whole list admits was admitted by that check, with no bridging hypothesis.

clauses.subject: floor-no-downgrade
clauses.statement: `floor_no_downgrade`: a floor admitting a caller forces every member of its evidence list to admit that caller.

clauses.subject: fail-closed
clauses.statement: An evidence list holding one fail-closed member yields a floor admitting no public-cloud caller, and the fail-closed allow-set rejects both cloud categories.

clauses.subject: evidence-nonempty
clauses.statement: `floor_no_downgrade`'s negative space names a non-empty evidence list, which {{authority.place.empty-evidence}} holds at the engine.

clauses.subject: symbolic-inclusion
clauses.statement: Zone inclusion is decided by subsumption over patterns, quantified over every constructor and every identifier, the named provider and the undeclared case included.

clauses.subject: subsumption-exact
clauses.statement: Per-entry subsumption decides zone inclusion exactly, a bare category subsuming every identifier under it, so no normal form on allow-sets precedes the decision.

clauses.subject: sampled-inclusion
clauses.statement: Inclusion decided by evaluating a fixed set of example values raises `ZoneInclusionSampled`.

clauses.subject: effective-policy
clauses.statement: An effective policy computed from two allow-sets is included in both.

clauses.subject: proof-targets
clauses.statement: The authority mapping of {{authority.profile.delegation-profile}} carries four proof targets: inclusion; narrowing, where an attenuated child's permission implies its parent's; profile meaning, where permission holds exactly when the audience matches and every block admits; and {{assurance.prove.restriction-preservation}}.
clauses.why: because all four are pure decision functions over a verified credential; the mediation relation covers read-path releases, and the rest of scoped-session execution stays unproved

clauses.subject: restriction-preservation
clauses.statement: `attenuateAll_permits_every_parent_block`: every block of a credential admits each request that any chain of attenuations of that credential permits, under one trusted environment.

clauses.subject: mediation-relation
clauses.statement: `statement_reach_released_rows_pass_session_layers`: the mediation induction ranges over the read path's statement execution, and every row a reachable state has released passed every layer of the session.

clauses.subject: target-binding
clauses.statement: A proof target is bound to one authenticated query path, recorded beside it as a module path and a test, before the claim names it.

clauses.subject: unbound-target
clauses.statement: A target the claim names with no binding raises `ProofTargetUnbound`, naming the target.

clauses.subject: negative-space
clauses.statement: Beside each theorem, its negative space states what it leaves open: that the required members were in the list, that a member removes rather than tests, and that execution reaches the fold before an effect.

clauses.subject: no-negative-space
clauses.statement: A theorem published without its negative space raises `TheoremWithoutNegativeSpace`, naming the constant.

clauses.subject: mediation-from-composition
clauses.statement: A filter-composition theorem offered as a mediation theorem raises `MediationClaimedFromComposition`.
clauses.why: because mediation quantifies over the reachable states of an execution; composition quantifies over a list

clauses.subject: names-carry-reach
clauses.statement: A constant's name states the object it ranges over, not the property a reader hopes for.

clauses.subject: assumption
clauses.statement: An assumption is a declaration the Lean kernel accepts without proof: the set `#print axioms` reports for a constant, which the audit reads through `collectAxioms`.

clauses.subject: allowlist
clauses.statement: The assumption allowlist holds 2 entries, `propext` and `Quot.sound`, and every theorem's footprint is a subset of it.
clauses.why: because no required constant draws on `Classical.choice`

clauses.subject: transitive-audit
clauses.statement: Each required constant's assumption footprint is read transitively off the elaborated environment, naming every assumption reached.

clauses.subject: verdict-input
clauses.statement: A verdict is a function of the elaborated environment and the inventory alone; source text, declaration counts and the build's exit status decide nothing.
clauses.why: because elaboration reports a hole as a warning and exits zero, and a character pattern misses a hole spelled in parentheses

clauses.subject: assumption-outside-allowlist
clauses.statement: An assumption in a footprint and absent from the allowlist raises `AssumptionOutsideAllowlist`, printing the constant and the assumption.

clauses.subject: hole-assumption
clauses.statement: A footprint containing the hole assumption raises `ProofHoleAssumption`, naming the declaration, whatever its syntax spells.

clauses.subject: native-evaluation-assumption
clauses.statement: A footprint containing a per-declaration native-evaluation assumption raises `NativeEvaluationAssumption`, naming the declaration that minted it.

clauses.subject: inventory
clauses.statement: `formal/inventory.toml` holds one row per required constant — name, module, expected statement text, admitted assumptions, binding, negative space — edited apart from the declarations satisfying it.

clauses.subject: missing-constant
clauses.statement: A required constant absent from the elaborated environment raises `TheoremConstantMissing`.

clauses.subject: statement-drift
clauses.statement: A required constant whose elaborated statement differs from its expected text raises `TheoremStatementDrift`, printing both.

clauses.subject: inventory-change
clauses.statement: A change to a required statement lands in the commit carrying the proof it admits.

clauses.subject: allowlist-admission
clauses.statement: An assumption joins the allowlist through an `A-assurance` section naming it, and each inventory row admitting it cites that section in a `record` field.

clauses.subject: report
clauses.statement: The report names the commit, the resolved toolchain, the allowlist and inventory revision applied, and for each required constant its statement match and the assumptions it reaches.

clauses.subject: check-command
clauses.statement: `contextful formal check` elaborates the package, matches every inventory row, audits every footprint, writes the report, and exits non-zero naming the first failing constant.

clauses.subject: two-phase
clauses.statement: A recheck rebuilds the package from the commit's own source and pinned toolchain into an empty artifact directory, fetching nothing, and re-runs the audit against the rebuilt environment.

clauses.subject: credential-free
clauses.statement: A recheck environment exposing a token, a signing key or a registry login raises `RecheckEnvironmentCredentialed`, naming the variable or file carrying it.

clauses.subject: report-mismatch
clauses.statement: A recheck whose per-constant statement text or assumption set differs from the first phase's raises `RecheckReportMismatch`, naming the constant.
clauses.why: because `.olean` output is not byte-reproducible across hosts and paths, while the per-constant report is the fact under check

clauses.subject: wall-time
clauses.statement: A recheck completes within 600 s.

clauses.subject: claim-sentence
clauses.statement: The assurance claim reads: these named decisions satisfy these named Lean specifications under these stated translation and runtime assumptions; each list resolves to code paths, constants and components in the tree.

clauses.subject: beyond-named-decisions
clauses.statement: A claim that the enforcement engine, or any object wider than the named decisions, is verified raises `ClaimBeyondNamedDecisions`.

clauses.subject: trusted-dependencies
clauses.statement: The claim names the delegation library, its cryptography, its parser and the translator as trusted dependencies, and proves none of them.

clauses.subject: unnamed-dependency
clauses.statement: A claim resting on a component absent from its trusted-dependency list raises `TrustedDependencyUnnamed`, naming the component.

clauses.subject: translation-chain
clauses.statement: A statement about translated code inherits four links: the compiler's lowering, the translator (Aeneas, named by one release string), hand-written models of external definitions, and the production build configuration.

clauses.subject: unstated-chain
clauses.statement: A theorem claimed over translated code without its translation chain raises `TranslationChainUnstated`.

clauses.subject: refinement-scope
clauses.statement: Refinement covers the decision functions behind the proof targets, whose inputs are values and whose outputs are decisions.

clauses.subject: refinement-exceeded
clauses.statement: Translation reaching cryptography, a parsing adapter, a database call or concurrency raises `RefinementScopeExceeded`, naming the module.

clauses.subject: reference-model
clauses.statement: The reference model is an executable Lean rendering of the decision functions, built to a binary that reads one case on standard input and prints one decision.

clauses.subject: harness
clauses.statement: The harness drives the reference binary and the decision module's native and WebAssembly builds over each generated case and compares their decisions field by field.

clauses.subject: builds
clauses.statement: The native build decides in process and the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build under the decision-module host; absent `--wasm`, the command compiles the module from the working tree, and the report names the builds compared.

clauses.subject: decision-cases
clauses.statement: A case names one decision: table-pattern coverage, grant narrowing, zone admission against an allow-set, session-zone resolution, or credential admission; a placement decision also carries the zone it resolved.

clauses.subject: credential-cases
clauses.statement: A `verify` case admits one credential against pinned keys as a network checkpoint does; both builds decide it and are compared, the reference model decides none, and the report counts each credential verdict.
clauses.why: because the reference model carries no signature scheme, and a gateway admits the credential before it places the request

clauses.subject: case-classes
clauses.statement: Each run generates malformed inputs, boundary values and well-formed requests, and its report names the classes it drew from.
clauses.why: because a green run is evidence over the generated classes, not an equivalence proof

clauses.subject: malformed-bytes
clauses.statement: The malformed class draws case texts carrying invalid UTF-8 or an integer literal outside the unsigned 64-bit range, handed as bytes to every decider, and each decides such a text malformed.
clauses.why: because a 32-bit WebAssembly build and a 64-bit native build part ways first at byte decoding and integer width

clauses.subject: minimized
clauses.statement: A disagreement is shrunk until no single field removal, string shortening or byte removal keeps any two of the three decisions apart, and the minimized case is recorded.

clauses.subject: corpus-replay
clauses.statement: Every counterexample-corpus case replays before any freshly generated case.

clauses.subject: corpus-entries
clauses.statement: The counterexample corpus retains at most 256 entries, evicting the oldest case a fresh seed reproduces.

clauses.subject: run-budget
clauses.statement: One invocation, corpus replay included, completes within 300 s.

clauses.subject: disagreement
clauses.statement: A case on which any two of the three decisions differ raises `ReferenceModelDrift`, printing the minimized case and every decision.

clauses.subject: discarded-counterexample
clauses.statement: A run reporting a disagreement and writing no corpus entry raises `CounterexampleDiscarded`.

clauses.subject: seed
clauses.statement: Each run records its generator seed, and re-running with that seed reproduces the same case sequence.

clauses.subject: protocol-cases
clauses.statement: Protocol cases are operation sequences and node interleavings a `proptest-state-machine` generator draws over acquire, renew, release, expire, commit, pause, delay and crash steps across three nodes.

clauses.subject: protocol-harness
clauses.statement: The harness drives the protocol package's compiled executable and the Rust store through each protocol case, comparing lease holder, fence, pointer ETag and commit outcome after every step.

clauses.subject: protocol-drift
clauses.statement: A step after which the model's state and the store's projected state differ raises `ProtocolConformanceDrift`, printing the minimized operation sequence and both states.

clauses.subject: command
clauses.statement: `contextful formal differential --seed <n> --cases <n>` replays the corpus, then runs the generated cases, exiting non-zero on the first disagreement.

clauses.subject: one-home
clauses.statement: Enforcement, control-plane state, credential resolution, statement guarding and visibility each resolve to one implementation in the engine; a surface reaches one through the engine route or the registered view compiling it in.

clauses.subject: duplicated-capability
clauses.statement: A surface or crate carrying a second implementation of an engine capability, in any language, or a hand-written copy of an engine constant, raises `CapabilityDuplicated`, naming both sites.

clauses.subject: capability-registry
clauses.statement: `spec/capabilities.toml` names each capability of {{assurance.structure-tree.one-home}} with one home path and one or more defining symbols; an absent registry, a missing or doubled capability, an absent home or an undefined symbol raises `CapabilityHomeUnresolved`.

clauses.subject: cross-language
clauses.statement: The crate-graph stage matches Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript and Python functions, types and constants outside a home by name folded to lowercase without separators, against its symbols and its literal constants' names and values.

clauses.subject: decision-module
clauses.statement: One module owns the enforcement decision; a gateway and the engine reaching the same verdict execute it, compiled native and to WebAssembly from one pinned source.

clauses.subject: adapter
clauses.statement: A surface with no engine process on its request path implements an adapter against the engine's ports.

clauses.subject: derivation-check
clauses.statement: A generated artifact declares the check that fails once its source moves, and the gate's schema stage runs that check.

clauses.subject: mirror-exemption
clauses.statement: A review-time restatement of a build-time rule is admitted where its site carries a `mirrors: <clause id>` comment naming the clause it restates; an unannotated restatement stays {{assurance.structure-tree.duplicated-capability}}.
clauses.why: because a reviewer-facing check sometimes restates a rule, and the annotation keeps the engine its one home and the copy traceable to it

clauses.subject: mirror-unresolved
clauses.statement: A `mirrors:` comment in a tracked file under `crates/`, `tools/` or `apps/` naming no clause of `spec/spec.lock.json` raises `MirrorUnresolved` in the schema stage, naming the file and line.
clauses.why: because an annotation naming nothing exempts a copy while tying it to no rule it could drift from

clauses.subject: typed-subcommand
clauses.statement: An automation step carrying a branch, a loop or a retry, or running past 5 lines, is a typed subcommand shelling out to compiled binaries.

clauses.subject: subcommand-surface
clauses.statement: A subcommand exposes typed options, generated help and an entry point a test calls directly.

clauses.subject: one-path
clauses.statement: The gate invokes the subcommand a contributor invokes.
clauses.why: because a local reproduction and a gate run then execute one code path

clauses.subject: unchecked-shell
clauses.statement: A shell file in the tree that `shellcheck` rejects raises `ShellCheckFailed` in the toolchain stage.

clauses.subject: test-shellcheck
clauses.statement: A gate stage starting a test process over a tree tracking a shell file puts the `shellcheck` {{assurance.automate.unchecked-shell}} runs first on that process's `PATH`.
clauses.why: because a suite asserting a script passes `shellcheck` otherwise depends on whether the sandbox image ships the linter

clauses.subject: build-time-toolchain
clauses.statement: The automation toolchain links into no build profile and enters no release artifact.

clauses.subject: presence-before-absence
clauses.statement: A test whose central claim is an absence first constructs the condition it names and verifies that condition obtains.

clauses.subject: vacuous-exclusion
clauses.statement: An exclusion assertion — `all`, or a negated `any` — in a tracked test file under `crates/` or `tools/`, over a collection no earlier statement of its function shows non-empty, raises `VacuousAssertion` in the test-first stage.

clauses.subject: guard-fires-both-ways
clauses.statement: A guard is validated against the fixture that motivated it and against the state it stands against, passing on the first and failing on the second.

clauses.subject: one-integration-binary
clauses.statement: A crate's integration tests compile in one target, `tests/integration/main.rs`, which declares each suite as a module selected by path.
clauses.why: because each file directly under `tests/` links its own static binary, hundreds of MiB for an engine-linked crate

clauses.subject: feature-gated-suite
clauses.statement: A feature-gated suite carries a module-level `cfg` attribute at the head of its module file and compiles to nothing while its feature is off.

clauses.subject: global-state-lock
clauses.statement: A suite contending process-global state acquires a named lock the integration binary's root module owns; every suite touching that state takes the same lock.
clauses.why: because a lock declared inside one suite leaves another suite free to race the same state

clauses.subject: own-process
clauses.statement: A test needing its own process sits in a top-level file stating why at its site; a thread-scoped log capture is such a test.

clauses.subject: connector-kit
clauses.statement: The connector authoring toolkit ships a conformance suite — discovery returns valid schemas, an opened table yields a finite stream, a position round-trips — plus recorded-HTTP fixture replay and property tests over position monotonicity.

clauses.subject: test-first
clauses.statement: A change altering Rust source under `crates/` or `tools/` adds or alters a test under a package's `tests/` that fails against the base commit's source; a change without one raises `TestNotFirst`.

clauses.subject: test-first-scope
clauses.statement: The test-first stage builds each changed test file's target against the base source with every feature enabled, then runs exactly the tests under that file's top-level module; a target failing to compile there counts as failing.

clauses.subject: comparison-base
clauses.statement: Test-first resolves the supplied comparison revision to one commit and uses that commit for source selection, changed-test selection and base replay; each report records that commit and the tested head.
scenarios: WHEN linear or divergent history supplies a comparison revision, THEN source selection, changed-test selection and replay use the same resolved commit.

clauses.subject: merge-source
clauses.statement: Test-first includes source introduced by merge resolutions; refactor exemptions apply only to source attributable to exempt commits and preserve obligations from behavior changes elsewhere in the comparison.
scenarios: WHEN a merge resolution introduces source behavior without a changed test, THEN the change fails {{assurance.test.test-first}}.
WHEN a comparison combines refactor and behavior commits, THEN the behavior changes retain their failing-test obligation.

clauses.subject: base-evidence
clauses.statement: Test-first reports assertion failures, compilation failures and bounded test executions separately; infrastructure faults follow {{assurance.test.base-unrunnable}} and supply no failing-test evidence.
scenarios: WHEN a base assertion fails, THEN its diagnostic identifies test failure independently of infrastructure output.
WHEN base execution fails through infrastructure, THEN the failure supplies no failing-test evidence.

clauses.subject: base-run-bound
clauses.statement: One test-first execution against the base, its build excluded, runs for at most 300 s; a run past the bound is killed with its process group and counts as failing.

clauses.subject: base-unrunnable
clauses.statement: A base invocation whose output reports a full disk, an unloadable manifest or an unfetchable dependency raises `TestFirstBaseUnrunnable` instead of a verdict.
clauses.why: because such a fault fails at base whatever the tests assert, and reading it as red admits an untested change

clauses.subject: refactor-trailer
clauses.statement: A commit carrying the trailer `Test-First: refactor` exempts the source it alters from {{assurance.test.test-first}}; the rest of the range stays held, and the workspace stage alone holds that commit.
clauses.why: because a behavior-preserving change has no failing test to write, and the existing suite is its specification

clauses.subject: acceptance-surface
clauses.statement: An acceptance test drives a built binary through its command line, MCP or HTTP surface; a workspace package among the acceptance package's dependencies raises `AcceptanceLinksEngine`.

clauses.subject: target-dir-per-stage
clauses.statement: Each cargo stage builds into a target directory of its own, reclaimed once the stage passes.
clauses.why: because stages under different feature unification share no artifacts, and peak disk is then one stage

clauses.subject: checkout-artifacts
clauses.statement: `.cargo/config.toml` names the checkout root, and every workspace package's build script folds its canonical path into the package fingerprint, so a shared target directory recompiles workspace packages per checkout while unchanged dependencies stay fresh.
scenarios: WHEN checkout A and checkout B build different source into one target directory, THEN B's integration tests, doctests and binary execute B's behavior on cold and warm builds, and their shared dependency stays fresh.

clauses.subject: runtime-checkout
clauses.statement: Reusable test helpers resolve the workspace root and tested binary from explicit runtime inputs bound to the invocation; cached helpers carry no compile-time checkout path deciding which source or binary runs.
scenarios: WHEN a helper cached from checkout A receives checkout B's runtime inputs, THEN its workspace operations and binary execution reach B alone.

clauses.subject: one-engine-build
clauses.statement: The workspace stage builds every engine-linked package in one cargo invocation over the union of their features, and the store adapter's suites resolved without `read` link no SQL engine, so the features stage compiles one copy.

clauses.subject: staged-feature-runs
clauses.statement: A defect appearing under one feature combination alone is reached by a staged nightly run, one command per container.

clauses.subject: linked-query-functions
clauses.statement: Columnar file reading and statement serialization link into every build linking the SQL engine, and the read path loads no extension while serving.

clauses.subject: runtime-extension-load
clauses.statement: A read path loading an extension into a binary that statically links the SQL engine raises `ExtensionAutoloadRefused`.

clauses.subject: debug-info
clauses.statement: Development and test profiles carry line-tables-only debug information for workspace code and none for dependencies.
clauses.why: because every engine-linked test binary embeds the bundled engine, and full debug information multiplies each past a sandbox's disk

clauses.subject: release-profile
clauses.statement: Release builds compile with thin link-time optimization, one codegen unit per crate and symbols stripped, and unwind on panic.
clauses.why: because the run keeper survives a panicking job only by unwinding to its guard

clauses.subject: profile-build
clauses.statement: The features stage tests each package under every feature set its manifest lists in `feature-runs`: each other package has its own nightly check; each binary feature run has separate nightly checks for differential tests and all remaining tests.
clauses.why: because one cold build of the binary under one feature set fills most of a stage's wall clock, and a listed set reaches what none and all miss

clauses.subject: container-image
clauses.statement: The repository's `Dockerfile` builds one profile, `contextful-full` by default, as a static binary for the `PLATFORM` and `RUST_TARGET` its arguments name, and ships it in a shell-free runtime image as a non-root user over a declared store volume.

clauses.subject: release-image
clauses.statement: Each profile's release image is an OCI index of a `linux/amd64` and a `linux/arm64` manifest; `contextful-ci image` assembles each from the profile's `x86_64` or `aarch64` musl release binary, with the `Dockerfile`'s runtime user, volume and entrypoint.
clauses.why: because arm64 hosts pull the same tag natively, and each release cell already holds its target's binary, so no image compiles twice

clauses.subject: image-binary-mismatch
clauses.statement: A binary whose ELF machine differs from its target's, or whose program headers name a dynamic interpreter, raises `ImageBinaryMismatch`, naming the target.
clauses.why: because a mislabelled layer runs only under emulation, and a dynamic binary finds no C library in the static runtime

clauses.subject: targets
clauses.statement: All three profiles cross-compile to `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`; edge and full also build for `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-apple-darwin`.

clauses.subject: windows-target
clauses.statement: Windows targets are excluded from the release matrix; no profile publishes Windows artifacts.

clauses.subject: wasi-probe
clauses.statement: No profile ships a `wasm32-wasip2` release; a scheduled-tier ledger entry builds the edge profile for it and holds the compressed artifact to {{assurance.gate.edge-budget}}.

clauses.subject: release-artifact
clauses.statement: Each profile ships a release archive with a SHA-256 checksum and an SBOM, a package-manager formula and an independently tagged container image; the bare formula name and the install script resolve to the full profile.

clauses.subject: release-builder
clauses.statement: The release command uses `cargo build` by default and `cargo zigbuild` under `--builder zigbuild`, forwarding the selected target and profile features.
clauses.why: because Cloudflare Linux builds Darwin targets through Zig while the local release command keeps its native build path
scenarios: WHEN a Darwin cell selects `--builder zigbuild`, THEN the release command invokes `cargo zigbuild` for that profile and target.

clauses.subject: release-metadata
clauses.statement: Each release cell writes a JSON record naming its profile, target, archive, SHA-256 digest and SBOM.
clauses.why: because distributed release cells need a small authenticated input for formula generation
scenarios: WHEN a release cell packages an archive, THEN its JSON metadata names the archive, digest and SBOM.

clauses.subject: formula-manifest
clauses.statement: The formula command accepts a manifest covering every release matrix cell once, with matching asset names and SHA-256 digests, and writes formulas and SHA256SUMS without local archives.
clauses.why: because one aggregation sandbox need not download every archive to produce formulas
scenarios: WHEN every cell's metadata is present without local archives, THEN formula generation writes the profile formulae and SHA256SUMS.

clauses.subject: licence-field
clauses.statement: Every workspace package under `crates/` or `tools/` declares `license = "Apache-2.0"`, inherited from `[workspace.package]`; a package declaring another value or none raises `PackageLicenceMissing`, naming its manifest.
clauses.why: because cargo-deny, cargo-about and SBOM generators read the manifest field, not the `LICENSE` file, so an unlicensed package fails a consumer's licence check

clauses.subject: dependency-allowlist
clauses.statement: The connector authoring dependency allowlist carries `regex` and `serde_json` at its depth limit; a profile graph reaching `fancy-regex`, `pcre2`, `onig` or `serde_json`'s `unbounded_depth` feature raises `DependencyAllowlistViolation`, naming the profile and path.
clauses.why: because a backtracking matcher or a parser without a depth limit lets one hostile record pin a core or exhaust the stack

clauses.subject: stage-sequence
clauses.statement: The gate runs its stages in order — pins, toolchain, schema, test-first, workspace, acceptance, evaluate, features, crate graph, connectors, TypeScript surfaces, formal, budget — all of both tiers when none is named, else the named subset, which `--plan` prints unrun.

clauses.subject: nightly-tier
clauses.statement: `contextful-ci stages --parts --tier nightly` prints the features, formal and budget parts in run order; `stages --parts` prints the remaining parts, those a change runs before merge, and `gate --stage` runs a part of either tier.

clauses.subject: stage-subset
clauses.statement: A selected subset runs in the sequence's order; a stage reading an unselected predecessor's output, with that output absent, raises `StagePredecessorMissing`, naming both stages, before any stage runs.

clauses.subject: affected-parts
clauses.statement: `contextful-ci stages --parts --base <rev> --affected` lists, in run order, the parts of the selected tier the diff from the merge base of `<rev>` and HEAD reaches, the required tier always including `preflight`.

clauses.subject: affected-every
clauses.statement: A change to `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, a toolchain file, anything under `crates/`, `tools/` or `.github/`, or any path no other affected clause maps reaches every part of either tier.

clauses.subject: affected-spec
clauses.statement: A change under `spec/` or `references/` reaches test-first validation, one under `spec/` the foundation workspace part, and each clause whose statement or `spec/pins.toml` entry changed the parts running its pinned test or theorem.

clauses.subject: affected-spec-inputs
clauses.statement: A change to `spec/01-topology.md` or `spec/capabilities.toml` reaches crate-graph, to `spec/adr/A-assurance.md` the formal stage, and to `spec/terms/assurance.toml` every budget part.
clauses.why: because those stages read the file directly, apart from any clause pin

clauses.subject: affected-removed
clauses.statement: A clause the merge base's lock holds and HEAD's lacks reaches the evaluate stage.
clauses.why: because the evaluate stage refuses a ledger entry naming a clause the lock lacks

clauses.subject: affected-unplaced
clauses.statement: An unreadable spec lock or pins file, or a changed clause pinned outside every workspace package, reaches every required part.
clauses.why: because a pin the listing cannot place runs on a part the listing cannot name

clauses.subject: affected-surfaces
clauses.statement: A change under `apps/` or `packages/` reaches the TypeScript surfaces, acceptance and crate-graph parts.

clauses.subject: affected-formal
clauses.statement: A change under `formal/` other than a `lean-toolchain` file reaches the formal and evaluate stages, the foundation, CLI and CLI differential workspace parts, and every feature part.

clauses.subject: windows-checks
clauses.statement: Windows native checks run only as optional diagnostics and contribute no required merge or release verdict.

clauses.subject: test-first-parts
clauses.statement: The test-first parts require a changed test in each changed source package under {{assurance.test.test-first}}; each changed source package's part checks only its own changed tests against the base.
clauses.why: because one base build per package fits the sandbox's wall clock more reliably

clauses.subject: workspace-parts
clauses.statement: The workspace parts compile the feature-unified workspace untested, run differential CLI tests apart and remaining CLI tests in eight shards under {{assurance.gate.cli-shard-map}}, and each other non-acceptance package suite in one of four groups.

clauses.subject: cli-shard-map
clauses.statement: `tools/ci/cli-shards.toml` assigns each remaining CLI test, a nested-build group whole, one shard by recorded duration within 9 min per shard; an unmapped test, reported as drift, joins its group or the least-loaded shard, which adds unit tests and doctests.

clauses.subject: folded-parts
clauses.statement: `stages --parts` folds pins, toolchain, schema and test-first validation into `preflight`; each package group's workspace and evaluate parts into `suite.<group>`, probes into `suite.ci`; crate graph, connectors and surfaces into `perimeter`; members stay runnable alone.
clauses.why: because every part pays its own sandbox setup and compile, and a fold pays it once for every member
