clauses.subject: compile-only
clauses.statement: `gate --stage <part> --compile-only` runs each `cargo test` invocation the part runs, in its own target directory with `--no-run` and without its `--` arguments, and nothing else; a CLI shard compiles every shard's invocations.
clauses.why: because a compile cache serves a part only when the warming build's cargo arguments, environment and target directory match the part's

clauses.subject: compile-groups
clauses.statement: `stages --parts --compile-groups` lists, in run order, the first part of each distinct compile signature — its ordered `--compile-only` invocations and target directory — across both tiers unless `--tier` names one.
clauses.why: because the eight CLI shards share one signature, and warming each compiles it eight times

clauses.subject: fold-verdicts
clauses.statement: A fold runs each member after an earlier member fails, skips a member reading a failed member's output, and fails when any member fails.
clauses.why: because one fold check replaces a check per member, and one run reports every member's verdict

clauses.subject: stage-reports
clauses.statement: Each stage prints the environment it leaves and its memory limit, peak and event counts, and a failing stage prints its diagnostics before propagating its exit code.
clauses.why: because memory exhaustion is silent, and a kill then reads as a number in the log

clauses.subject: stage-timings
clauses.statement: Each part records queue, setup, compilation and test durations separately, alongside its commit, feature set, runner identity and cold or warm cache state.
scenarios: WHEN a part queues and then executes, THEN its report distinguishes queue, setup, compilation and test durations.

clauses.subject: part-budget
clauses.statement: Every part completes within {{assurance.gate.container}} on cold and warm builds; oversized work splits into locally runnable parts retaining every required suite and predecessor obligation.
scenarios: WHEN every part runs with empty caches and then warm caches, THEN each completes within {{assurance.gate.container}} and the union preserves required coverage.

clauses.subject: build-admission
clauses.statement: The runner admits concurrent builds only within available build slots and {{assurance.gate.parallel-jobs}}; excess builds queue before setup and compilation.
scenarios: WHEN occupied build slots reach the admission limit, THEN another build queues without starting setup or compilation.

clauses.subject: timeout-cleanup
clauses.statement: A timed-out part retains phase timings and stdout/stderr diagnostics, terminates its owned process tree, verifies descendant exit and reports a failed verdict before releasing its build slot.
scenarios: WHEN a forced hang leaves a descendant holding output pipes, THEN timeout diagnostics survive, the descendant exits and the part fails before its slot is released.

clauses.subject: pins-stage
clauses.statement: The pins stage resolves every pinned artifact identity a run depends on before any compilation.

clauses.subject: evaluate-stage
clauses.statement: The evaluate stage runs every gate-tier ledger entry and the native case set in the deterministic tier, one part per package group plus a probe part, each reporting the floor and baseline verdicts over its entries.

clauses.subject: schema-stage
clauses.statement: The schema stage regenerates each derived artifact into a scratch location, compares it byte for byte against the committed copy, and runs `contextful-spec lint`.

clauses.subject: secret-ciphertext
clauses.statement: In the schema stage, a key other than `DOTENV_PUBLIC_KEY*` in a git-tracked `.env*` file other than `.env.example` holding a value without the `encrypted:` prefix, or a tracked `.env.keys`, raises `SecretPlaintext`, naming file and key.
clauses.why: because a tracked file reaches every clone, and only dotenvx ciphertext is safe there while its private key stays untracked

clauses.subject: secret-scope
clauses.statement: In the schema stage, a key other than `DOTENV_PUBLIC_KEY*` in a git-tracked `.env*` file whose block — the assignments above it, up to the first blank line — opens with no comment carrying text raises `SecretScopeMissing`, naming file and key.
clauses.why: because a provider token cannot report its own grants, so the comment above it is the one record of what it reaches

clauses.subject: crate-graph
clauses.statement: The crate-graph stage holds run-path crates to reaching read-path crates through the three crossing crates alone; another edge raises `CrateGraphViolation`, naming both crates.

clauses.subject: locked-resolve
clauses.statement: The crate-graph stage resolves every graph `--locked` against the committed `Cargo.lock`, so a lock behind its manifests, or one rewritten before the stage starts, fails the stage before any rule runs; the stage never rewrites it.
clauses.why: because a rule held over a graph the lock file does not record passes a build that resolves another

clauses.subject: row-token
clauses.statement: Every row-returning function of the store crate takes the enforcement token type, whose constructor is private to the enforcement module; a row path outside a registered relation raises `EnforceUnmediatedPath`, naming the function.

clauses.subject: dependency-deny
clauses.statement: The crate-graph stage runs pinned cargo-deny `check bans` over each profile's resolved graph, denying every crate a profile-wide dependency refusal names; a hit raises that refusal's error, naming the profile and the path.

clauses.subject: deny-profile-graph
clauses.statement: A profile's graph is the binary resolved with default features off and the profile's feature on, across every target, excluding development dependencies; the stage prints each profile the binary declares no feature for.

clauses.subject: deny-list
clauses.statement: `deny.toml` holds one `[bans]` entry per crate or feature a profile-wide dependency refusal names, its reason that refusal's clause id; an entry missing or extra raises `DenyListDrift`, naming it.
clauses.why: because a refusal whose crate the list omits passes every profile graph linking it

clauses.subject: unconfigured-egress
clauses.statement: An outbound call reachable under the default configuration — usage ping, license check, update probe — raises `UnconfiguredEgress` in the crate-graph stage, naming the call site.
clauses.why: because some deployments run with no external reach, and a call nobody configured moves data outside every grant, zone and audit record

clauses.subject: interpolated-claim
clauses.statement: A source lint over the runtime crates finding a subject claim formatted into SQL text raises `EnforceInterpolatedSubjectClaim`, naming the file and line.

clauses.subject: formal-stage
clauses.statement: The nightly formal stage runs {{assurance.audit-assumptions.check-command}}, {{assurance.differential-test.command}} and {{assurance.model.protocol-check}}; a non-zero exit from any reds the run.

clauses.subject: container
clauses.statement: The gate container carries four ceilings — processor count, 12 GiB of memory, 18 GiB of usable disk, and a 45 min per-stage wall clock — and a run dies on any one.

clauses.subject: parallel-jobs
clauses.statement: Parallel build jobs number the memory ceiling divided by 3 GiB.

clauses.subject: free-disk
clauses.statement: A stage starting with less than 2 GiB of free disk raises `BuildDiskPrecondition` and exits 28 before doing work.

clauses.subject: build-size
clauses.statement: The nightly budget stage holds total build size to 12 GiB, printing that size, the free space and the largest artifacts; a larger build raises `BuildSizeCeilingExceeded`, naming the head of that list.

clauses.subject: edge-budget
clauses.statement: The edge profile holds to 50 MiB compressed and 60 MiB idle resident set.

clauses.subject: full-budget
clauses.statement: The full profile holds to 150 MiB compressed and 180 MiB idle resident set.

clauses.subject: control-budget
clauses.statement: The control profile holds to 60 MiB compressed and 80 MiB idle resident set.

clauses.subject: footprint
clauses.statement: Per nightly run and per profile, the footprint step builds the static-linked Linux target, compresses it, and holds its size to the profile's budget and its dynamic dependencies to the platform C library.

clauses.subject: budget-stage
clauses.statement: The budget stage runs {{assurance.gate.footprint}} over every profile, in one nightly-tier part per profile, and the evaluate stage builds no profile.
clauses.why: because one link-time-optimized release build of the full profile fills most of one stage's wall clock

clauses.subject: footprint-exceeded
clauses.statement: An artifact over its profile's budget, or carrying a dynamic dependency beyond the platform C library, raises `FootprintBudgetExceeded`, naming the profile.

clauses.subject: typescript-surfaces
clauses.statement: The TypeScript surfaces run each declared typecheck, test and build script in one stage; an absent script skips only that script.

clauses.subject: native-test-files
clauses.statement: The surfaces stage runs every regular native `.test.ts` file under a direct TypeScript surface's `test/` or `tests/` tree through Node's TypeScript strip runner, and refuses absent passing tests or pinned names.
clauses.why: because a package script can omit a pinned test while reporting success

clauses.subject: surface-check-failed
clauses.statement: A surface whose typecheck, unit tests or framework build fails raises `SurfaceCheckFailed`, naming the surface and the script.

clauses.subject: real-read-path
clauses.statement: An evaluation run ingests, indexes, retrieves, reads, judges and scores through the surfaces a caller uses, and the harness adds no storage or runtime primitive.

clauses.subject: through-the-store
clauses.statement: The corpus loads through the real store, and the retriever under test calls {{read.retrieve.ranked-call}} with the options a caller passes.
clauses.why: because an unordered full-scan retriever cannot go red when ranking breaks

clauses.subject: policy-labels
clauses.statement: An evaluation corpus carries zone and row-policy labels in its table declarations, and a run reads it through the access-control path under one admitted credential.
scenarios: WHEN a regression case names a row another agent owns under `owner = subject.agent`, THEN no leg returns it and the hybrid forbidden-row rate reads 0.

clauses.subject: unlabeled-corpus
clauses.statement: A run over a corpus whose tables declare no zone or row policy, with no `local:` zone passed as `--zone`, raises `EvalCorpusUnlabeled` before any row lands.
scenarios: WHEN a corpus's tables declare no policy and the run passes no `--zone`, THEN the run raises `EvalCorpusUnlabeled` and lands no row.

clauses.subject: case-format
clauses.statement: A case carries an id, a corpus path relative to its case file, a question, tags, and an expected block of answer, artifacts, edges, entities, must-cite, must-abstain, must-not-retrieve, time anchor and recency bound.

clauses.subject: row-reference
clauses.statement: A case names a row as `<table>#<key>`, the key joining the row's declared primary-key values with commas, and the runner keys each returned row the same way.

clauses.subject: regression-case
clauses.statement: A case tagged `regression` is a regression case, and its must-not-retrieve set scores {{assurance.evaluate.forbidden-row-rate}}.

clauses.subject: corpus-layout
clauses.statement: A corpus is a directory holding `contextful.toml`, its table declarations and policy labels, and one `rows/<table>.jsonl` per table.

clauses.subject: run-command
clauses.statement: `contextful eval run --goldens <file>` loads the case file, lands and folds each referenced corpus into a scratch store at `--landed-at`, the Unix epoch by default, reads every case, and writes the run report.
clauses.why: because an undated row landed at the epoch predates every question's window, so a replay scores alike on any day

clauses.subject: entity-command
clauses.statement: `contextful eval entity-evidence --manifest <file>` loads versioned synthetic or licensed adjudicated fixtures through {{assurance.evaluate.through-the-store}}, resolving mentions through knowledge cards, following requested predicates through keyed recall, and comparing ordinary ranked evidence retrieval.

clauses.subject: entity-eligibility
clauses.statement: Both entity-evidence arms receive identical evidence admitted by keyed recall under the case anchor and one reader credential; fixed adjudicated tuples grant no answer credit to later, expired, superseded, inaccessible or unresolved evidence.

clauses.subject: entity-metrics
clauses.statement: Entity-evidence reports canonical entity accuracy, eligible-claim recall, ordered relationship-path correctness, citation resolution and appropriate abstention independently under deterministic labels; model judgments occupy separate labels.

clauses.subject: entity-baseline
clauses.statement: Entity-evidence baselines bind fixture version, manifest digest, corpus digest and run configuration, extending {{assurance.baseline.metric-path}} with `entity_evidence.<arm>.<metric>`; versioned ledger entries collect {{assurance.measure.record}} records.

clauses.subject: legs
clauses.statement: Each case calls {{read.retrieve.ranked-call}} three times at limit k: the lexical leg with the question alone, the vector leg with an embedding and an empty query, the hybrid leg with both.

clauses.subject: stub-embedder
clauses.statement: The deterministic tier embeds every row and question with a seeded feature-hashing stub embedder; a corpus row or a case carrying its own embedding keeps it.

clauses.subject: semantic-cache
clauses.statement: `--semantic-manifest` hashes corpus, held-out labels, development queries, configuration, and the model's license, embedding configuration and artifacts at an immutable revision; a changed, unhashed or symbolically linked input or a second table raises `EvalSemanticCacheUnverified` before {{assurance.evaluate.through-the-store}}.
clauses.why: because model quality needs real vectors whose provenance and inputs survive offline replay

clauses.subject: semantic-inputs
clauses.statement: A missing, non-finite, zero-norm or mismatched vector, a relocated held-out file, an overlapping development query or a configuration difference raises `EvalSemanticInputRejected` before retrieval; every leg consumes the same verified cases and corpus.
clauses.why: because a cache fallback or corpus substitution changes the experiment while preserving its name

clauses.subject: semantic-report
clauses.statement: Semantic reports carry {{assurance.evaluate.deterministic-tier}} with sample counts and case-bootstrap uncertainty; a comparable baseline reports overall and per-slice regressions under the pinned tolerance.

clauses.subject: semantic-separate
clauses.statement: Semantic quality reports use their own tier and input identity, exclude answer judging and deterministic mechanics verdicts, and compare baselines only for matching corpus, labels, model and configuration identities.

clauses.subject: run-verdict
clauses.statement: A run holds its report to the floors and, given `--baseline`, to that file; either red verdict exits non-zero, and `--update-baseline` applies {{assurance.baseline.raise-only}} on green alone.

clauses.subject: converter
clauses.statement: Each benchmark and application ground truth converts once into the case format through its own converter, and the runner reads nothing else.

clauses.subject: deterministic-tier
clauses.statement: Recall@k, R-precision, hit-rate@k, reciprocal rank and nDCG@k run with no model call, reported per leg — lexical, vector, hybrid — and per slice.

clauses.subject: distinct-top-k
clauses.statement: Membership in the top k is distinct, and a repeated id counts once.

clauses.subject: absent-truth
clauses.statement: A ranked metric over a case with no relevant set is NaN and drops out of every aggregate; an empty ranking against a non-empty relevant set scores zero.

clauses.subject: precision-floor
clauses.statement: Precision at rank min(k, R), R being the relevant-set size, holds at or above 60 percent.
clauses.why: because precision@k caps at R/k, below the floor whenever R is small

clauses.subject: forbidden-row-rate
clauses.statement: A row named in a must-not-retrieve set holds at 0 percent of a regression case's returned rows.

clauses.subject: duplicate-row-rate
clauses.statement: A repeated table-and-row-key pair holds at 0 percent of the ranking.

clauses.subject: in-window-rate
clauses.statement: A case declaring a recency bound holds its in-window rate at or above 95 percent.

clauses.subject: abstention
clauses.statement: A must-abstain case returns zero rows.

clauses.subject: truth-per-surface
clauses.statement: Expected artifacts score the artifact retriever and expected edges score the edge retriever, reported apart; edge truth with no edge surface configured counts in an unscored tally.

clauses.subject: memory-legs
clauses.statement: Beside {{assurance.evaluate.legs}}, a run naming an admitted reranker adds a hybrid leg passing it as `rerank_with` under {{read.rank.rerank}}, and a memory case adds a keyed leg calling {{read.recall.keyed}} at its time anchor.

clauses.subject: edge-surface
clauses.statement: The edge retriever of {{assurance.evaluate.truth-per-surface}} runs one {{read.traverse.call}} walk per expected entity, over every walkable declared relation at {{read.traverse.hop-bound}}; a case's expected edges score the union of returned edges.

clauses.subject: memory-tags
clauses.statement: A memory case carries one or more tags of `knowledge-update`, `temporal-reasoning`, `abstention` and `selective-forgetting`; a temporal case anchors at `observed_at`, and a forgetting case erases its subject under {{disclosure.erase.privilege}} before reading.

clauses.subject: supersession-correctness
clauses.statement: A run reports, per leg, the rate of memory cases serving a superseded claim at its successor's anchor.

clauses.subject: supersession-floor
clauses.statement: The {{assurance.evaluate.supersession-correctness}} rate holds at 0 percent across native memory cases.
clauses.why: because a retired belief served beside its successor is the distractor memory exists to remove

clauses.subject: recall-under-suppression
clauses.statement: A memory case reports recall@k with the claims {{read.recall.suppression-count}} counts excluded from its judged relevant set.

clauses.subject: evidence-cap-rate
clauses.statement: A memory case reports the share of its served claims whose `evidence_omitted` count under {{read.recall.evidence-references}} is above 0.

clauses.subject: memory-converters
clauses.statement: Beside {{assurance.evaluate.converter}}, LongMemEval and MemoryAgentBench each convert into tagged memory cases, and their scores report beside the native set as {{assurance.baseline.native-gate}} holds.

clauses.subject: filtered-recall
clauses.statement: Each run reports restricted recall@k against an exact scan at three restriction selectivities drawn from the zone and row-policy labels of {{assurance.evaluate.policy-labels}}.
clauses.why: because an approximate index loses recall as a filter narrows, and one unfiltered figure hides that loss

clauses.subject: judged-dimensions
clauses.statement: The reading stage adds four judged dimensions: answer accuracy; abstention, as correct-refusal and hallucination-on-unknown rates; citation faithfulness; and temporal correctness against the bitemporal columns.

clauses.subject: grounded-reader
clauses.statement: The harness reader answers from retrieved rows alone, and the deterministic tier substitutes a stub reader.

clauses.subject: model-endpoint
clauses.statement: The judge and the reader reach a model through {{connector.infer.model-endpoint}}, and the harness holds no credential.

clauses.subject: judge
clauses.statement: The judge is one pinned open-weights instruct model, called once per judged item at temperature zero; a judge swap is a full re-baseline.
clauses.why: because a majority vote at temperature zero samples one mode and adds cost without reducing variance

clauses.subject: judged-run
clauses.statement: `contextful eval run --tier judged` reads and judges every case through the endpoint and model `--endpoint` and `--model` name, stamping that model in the run block; the deterministic tier judges with the stubs.

clauses.subject: cutoff-flags
clauses.statement: `contextful eval run` takes `--snapshot`, `--pretrain-cutoff` and `--posttrain-cutoff` for the reader and `--judge-snapshot`, `--judge-pretrain-cutoff` and `--judge-posttrain-cutoff` for the judge, each cutoff value a month and its tag, as `2024-10:documented`.
scenarios: WHEN a run passes `--pretrain-cutoff 2024-10:documented` and no `--posttrain-cutoff`, THEN the reader's post-training cutoff compares as each call's own instant.

clauses.subject: judged-cutoffs
clauses.statement: A judged run block stamps the reader's and the judge's snapshot ids and their {{connector.infer.cutoffs}}.
clauses.why: because a score from a model trained past a case's resolution measures recall, not reading
scenarios: WHEN a judged run passes `--judge-posttrain-cutoff 2025-03:estimated`, THEN the run block carries that cutoff tagged `estimated` beside the judge's snapshot id.

clauses.subject: systems-metrics
clauses.statement: Tokens per query, latency and cost report beside the quality figures, bucketed by corpus size in tokens relative to the reader's context window.

clauses.subject: checkpoint
clauses.statement: A run appends each case's result as JSONL, and a crash re-runs the in-flight case.

clauses.subject: run-report
clauses.statement: A run report carries one field per gated metric, the sample count behind each mean, the run block, the per-slice breakdown, and the tally of cases sampled, dropped and unscored.

clauses.subject: file
clauses.statement: A baseline file carries a reserved run block `{k, tier, model, samples}` and one entry per gated metric: a bare number at the run's dead band, or an object overriding the band.

clauses.subject: default-dead-band
clauses.statement: A rate-valued entry with no override gates at a 2 percent dead band.

clauses.subject: rank-quality-dead-band
clauses.statement: The ranked-quality entry gates at a 3 percent dead band.

clauses.subject: band-units
clauses.statement: A band carries its metric's own units, and a count entry is pinned at zero with no band.

clauses.subject: metric-path
clauses.statement: An entry names a metric by the report's field path: `retrieval.<modality>.<metric>`, `edge_retrieval.<modality>.<metric>`, `judge.<dimension>`, `latency_ms`, `n_cases`, or `slices.<tag>.` before a bare `<metric>` or any of these but `latency_ms`.

clauses.subject: sample-count
clauses.statement: Every mean-valued path takes a `.n` suffix naming its sample count.
clauses.why: because blanking one case's truth lifts a NaN-filtered mean without moving the case count

clauses.subject: unresolvable-path
clauses.statement: A path resolving to nothing, a mean over fewer than 30 cases, a malformed entry or a non-finite band raises `BaselinePathUnresolved` before the suite runs.

clauses.subject: run-stamp-drift
clauses.statement: A run block differing from the run's own configuration raises `BaselineRunStampMismatch` before the suite runs.

clauses.subject: cutoff-block
clauses.statement: A judged baseline's run block carries the reader's and the judge's snapshot ids and {{connector.infer.cutoffs}}, so {{assurance.baseline.run-stamp-drift}} refuses a run under a changed snapshot or cutoff.
clauses.why: because a score from a model trained later measures more recall, not better reading

clauses.subject: interval
clauses.statement: Each judged figure reports a 95 percent percentile-bootstrap interval over cases from 1000 resamples.

clauses.subject: raise-only
clauses.statement: A baseline update runs after every gate and floor passes, moves each improved entry to its measured value, moves none in the worse direction, and adds no path.

clauses.subject: floors-are-absolute
clauses.statement: An absolute floor gates independently of every committed value.

clauses.subject: floor-coverage
clauses.statement: A report lacking a floor's figure on any leg of its `retrieval` surface breaches that floor; only a forbidden-row or in-window rate over no case holds.

clauses.subject: offline
clauses.statement: The gate is a local command comparing the report against in-tree baselines and floors, reporting both verdicts, with or without a trace store reachable.

clauses.subject: trace-store
clauses.statement: A trace store records run history and curation staging, and decides no verdict.

clauses.subject: golden-custody
clauses.statement: Version-controlled JSONL under `evals/cases/` is the canonical golden set, one loader is its only ingestion door, and a reviewer's edit reaches the gate as a change to the tree.

clauses.subject: answer-key-in-the-store
clauses.statement: An artifact path normalizing under the evaluation directory, reached by a manifest lint or a connector, raises `GoldenSetIngested`.

clauses.subject: generated-redaction
clauses.statement: A golden mined from a live query or promoted from a labeled outcome passes {{authority.redact.write-time}} before commit; a case it cannot redact raises `GoldenRedactionFailed`.

clauses.subject: promotion-source
clauses.statement: Only an adjudicated outcome label promotes into a golden set; a self-rated row does not.

clauses.subject: generators
clauses.statement: Three generators draft candidate cases from the deployment's store — entity-to-fact-to-edge walks, composed edge chains, and questions about absent entities — and a human approves each before commit.

clauses.subject: draft-command
clauses.statement: `contextful eval draft` reads the declared entity, fact and edge tables through one admitted session, runs the three generators, and writes their candidates as case lines; it commits nothing.

clauses.subject: commit-command
clauses.statement: `contextful eval commit` appends each draft an `--approve <id>=<reviewer>` names, redacted under the declaration's removal rules, to the named case file; an id the file already holds refuses the commit.

clauses.subject: held-out
clauses.statement: Retrieval and synthesis are tuned on no gate input.

clauses.subject: rotation
clauses.statement: The native set rotates on a cadence, a sample of its truth is reviewed on each rotation, and a comparison across generations resolves through the pinned run stamp.

clauses.subject: native-gate
clauses.statement: A native benchmark generated from a real corpus is the red or green gate; public benchmark sets run beside it as held-out comparison and decide nothing.

clauses.subject: public-corpora
clauses.statement: A public benchmark corpus enters through a fetch-manifest entry naming its URL, its dataset's terms and a SHA-256 digest, and is never committed; fetched bytes under another digest raise `PublicCorpusDigestMismatch`.
clauses.why: because a corpus whose bytes drift scores another benchmark under the same name

clauses.subject: trace-export
clauses.statement: A run touching a deployed store with a hosted trace endpoint configured raises `TraceExportOutOfPerimeter`; hosted collection serves runs over public or synthetic fixtures alone.

clauses.subject: bounded-case
clauses.statement: A bounded case carries a horizon, an instant each of its reads passes as {{store.available-time.available-as-of}}; its trajectory is the ordered tool calls, queries and retrieved documents its run records.

clauses.subject: checkpoint-route
clauses.statement: A reader, derive engine or embedder naming a checkpoint family resolves each bounded case to the newest family checkpoint whose post-training {{connector.infer.cutoffs}} precedes the case's horizon.
clauses.why: because date-bounded checkpoints remove memorized outcomes at the source

clauses.subject: cutoff-slice
clauses.statement: A backtest report places each case by its resolution instant minus the reader's post-training cutoff and states leakage against a declared reference, a cutoff discontinuity or a clean control model, never a bare pre/post gap.

clauses.subject: cutoff-sensitivity
clauses.statement: The report repeats {{assurance.backtest.cutoff-slice}} with each `estimated` cutoff moved across its declared uncertainty interval, and states the minimum detectable effect.
clauses.why: because finding no leakage bounds it and does not certify its absence

clauses.subject: latest-arm
clauses.statement: A case set run under a checkpoint family also runs the family's latest checkpoint as a paired arm, and the report states the latest-minus-routed difference.
clauses.why: because the latest-minus-dated gap isolates the leakage premium

clauses.subject: answer-key-only
clauses.statement: A judge scores a case resolved before the judge's post-training cutoff against the case's stored expected answer alone.
clauses.why: because a judge reasoning about an outcome may remember it

clauses.subject: run-stamp
clauses.statement: Beyond {{assurance.evaluate.judged-cutoffs}}, taken through {{assurance.evaluate.cutoff-flags}}, a backtest run block stamps the derive engine's and embedder's snapshot ids and cutoffs, the temperature, seed, prompt digest and tool-schema version.
clauses.why: because two runs differing in any of these are two trials, and a report cannot slice on a value it never recorded

clauses.subject: label-interval
clauses.statement: Every bounded case declares its label interval `[t0, t1]`, the span its outcome is observed over; a bounded case without one raises `EvalLabelIntervalMissing` before any of its reads.
clauses.why: because purge and embargo need each label's span, and a label observed past the horizon is the leak itself
scenarios: WHEN a bounded case declares a horizon and no label interval, THEN the run raises `EvalLabelIntervalMissing` and reads nothing for that case.

clauses.subject: split
clauses.statement: A split purges each training case whose label interval overlaps a test case's, and embargoes each training case starting within a declared span after a test fold ends.
clauses.why: because serially correlated labels carry a test fold's outcome into adjacent training cases

clauses.subject: trial-ledger
clauses.statement: A financial return-series profile records each run against its case set as a trial row and computes the deflated Sharpe ratio from trial count, Sharpe variance, series length, skew and kurtosis.
clauses.why: because the deflated Sharpe needs every trial's Sharpe, not a reported count

clauses.subject: seed-repeats
clauses.statement: A configuration runs its declared repeat count; its repeats count as one trial, and the report shows their spread.

clauses.subject: universe-table
clauses.statement: A case evaluating changing membership names a membership table declaring valid time and `available_time`; a case naming literal identifiers reports under a separate `fixed-universe` slice.
clauses.why: because a fixed identifier list names only the members known when the case was written

clauses.subject: fill-instant
clauses.statement: A financial execution profile fills each decision at the first price available strictly after the decision's recorded instant.

clauses.subject: execution-component
clauses.statement: A backtest report stamps its declared execution component's digest and parameters under {{topology.bound-application.domain-neutral}}; a report without one raises `EvalExecutionUndeclared`.

clauses.subject: planted-future
clauses.statement: Each bounded case plants a row available after its horizon in every table it reads; a planted row in the case's trajectory fails the case.
clauses.why: because a planted row proves the bound held on the path the case took, not only in its configuration
scenarios: WHEN a bounded case's trajectory returns the row planted one day after its horizon, THEN the case fails and the report names the call that returned it.

clauses.subject: planted-delisting
clauses.statement: A financial universe profile plants a member delisted inside its window; the case fails unless its trajectory holds that member's delisting return.
clauses.why: because survivorship shows as a missing delisting return, which no aggregate figure reveals

clauses.subject: leak-score
clauses.statement: The case's judge model scores each retrieved document 0 to 4 against a reference answer from rows available before the horizon, landing one row per document and case horizon; the report gives Brier per leak tier.

clauses.subject: trajectory-check
clauses.statement: A bounded case fails when a call in its trajectory lacks the {{disclosure.record.bound-entry}} attributes, or a retrieved document scores at or above the case's declared leak threshold.
clauses.why: because a bound proves the configuration, and leaked page content passes the bound

clauses.subject: query-finding
clauses.statement: A recorded query naming an entity first available after the case's horizon lands a finding naming the call.
clauses.why: because a model that remembers the outcome steers its queries toward it

clauses.subject: trajectory-replay
clauses.statement: `contextful eval replay <run>` re-serves each recorded response without reading the store and reproduces the run report's digest.
clauses.why: because a backtest a third party cannot re-score is a claim, not evidence

clauses.subject: replay-root
clauses.statement: A backtest run report carries the signed audit-chain root covering its run's {{disclosure.record.bound-entry}} entries.
clauses.why: because the root lets a verifier prove each replayed response is the one the run recorded

clauses.subject: forecast-case
clauses.statement: A forecast case carries a freeze instant, a resolution statement naming its vintage, a resolution instant and a probability answer; a backtest forecast case is a {{assurance.backtest.bounded-case}} whose horizon is its freeze instant.

clauses.subject: resolved-before-freeze
clauses.statement: A backtest forecast case whose resolution instant precedes its freeze instant raises `EvalCaseResolvedBeforeFreeze`.
clauses.why: because a question picked after its answer is known leaks through its own existence
scenarios: WHEN a backtest forecast case freezes on `2014-06-01` and resolved on `2014-05-20`, THEN the run raises `EvalCaseResolvedBeforeFreeze` before reading the case.

clauses.subject: settlement
clauses.statement: A forecast case settles through the label join within {{read.settle.grace-window}}, and its scores report as {{read.settle.calibration-report}} groups them.
clauses.why: because one settlement path keeps a forecast's Brier score comparable with an application's calibration

clauses.subject: lead-time
clauses.statement: An answer recorded less than the case's declared minimum lead before resolution scores on a separate track.
clauses.why: because an answer given near resolution reads the outcome rather than forecasting it

clauses.subject: market-context
clauses.statement: A prediction-market profile supplies freeze-instant probability prices as available rows, and the report shows each forecaster's score improvement over that baseline.

clauses.subject: imputed
clauses.statement: A missing answer scores as probability 0.5 for a dataset case; a prediction-market profile instead uses its freeze-instant probability price.
clauses.why: because dropping a missing answer rewards abstaining on hard questions

clauses.subject: coverage-floor
clauses.statement: A forecaster answering below 95 percent of a round's cases is reported unranked.
clauses.why: because imputation alone still lets a forecaster pick its questions

clauses.subject: no-evidence-baseline
clauses.statement: Each round also scores a forecaster given the question text alone, and the report subtracts its Brier score from each forecaster's.
clauses.why: because which questions exist can reveal their answers without any retrieval

clauses.subject: tracks-separate
clauses.statement: Backtest, prospective, tool-free and tool-using scores never pool into one figure.

clauses.subject: ledger
clauses.statement: `evals/ledger.toml` holds one entry per tracked target: an id, an owning clause id, a run-report metric path, a tier, a method naming one integration test, case set or probe, and a threshold.

clauses.subject: unresolved-entry
clauses.statement: An entry whose owning clause, method or metric path resolves to nothing raises `MeasureEntryUnresolved` before any measure runs.
scenarios: WHEN an entry names `run.journal.entry-keys`, THEN the run raises `MeasureEntryUnresolved` and no test runs.

clauses.subject: open-entry
clauses.statement: An entry naming an issue in place of a method reports open and gates nothing, and `evals/ledger.md` carries every entry's computed status.
scenarios: WHEN an entry's method is `{ issue = 43 }`, THEN `evals/ledger.md` lists it open and the evaluate stage ignores it.

clauses.subject: tier
clauses.statement: A gate-tier entry decides the evaluate stage, a trend-tier entry decides nothing, and `contextful-ci measure` runs the gate tier alone unless `--tier` names `trend`, `scheduled` or `all`.

clauses.subject: judged-tier
clauses.statement: An entry whose metric names a judged figure is scheduled-tier; on another tier it resolves to nothing under {{assurance.measure.unresolved-entry}}.
clauses.why: because a judged figure costs a model call per item and moves with the judge, not with the change

clauses.subject: count-first
clauses.statement: A gate-tier entry measures a count, a ratio within one run or a size under a locked resolve; a wall-clock or resident-memory figure is trend-tier.
clauses.why: because a shared container moves wall-clock figures past any band narrow enough to catch a regression

clauses.subject: record
clauses.statement: A measure writes one JSON record carrying its entry id, value, sample count, seed and run stamp; a gate-tier method finishing without one raises `MeasureRecordMissing`.

clauses.subject: seeded
clauses.statement: Every generated fixture and randomized schedule derives from the record's seed, and replaying that seed reproduces a count-valued entry's value.
clauses.why: because a failure that cannot replay cannot be fixed

clauses.subject: seed-mismatch
clauses.statement: A gate or scheduled record whose seed differs from its entry's declared seed raises `MeasureSeedMismatch` and counts as red; a trend mismatch leaves no comparable record.
clauses.why: because a figure measured under another seed replays nothing the ledger names

clauses.subject: timing-iterations
clauses.statement: A timed batch reports p50 and p95 over 200 repeats of its operation, each after warm-up.

clauses.subject: timing-batches
clauses.statement: A timed figure is the median of 5 repeats of its timed batch.

clauses.subject: trend-direction
clauses.statement: Each trend-tier ledger entry declares `higher_is_better` or `lower_is_better` for its metric.

clauses.subject: trend-baseline
clauses.statement: A trend figure compares with the newest earlier successful default-branch report for the same entry and seed under {{assurance.measure.runner-stamp}}; absent matching history yields no annotation.
scenarios: WHEN a newer failed report follows two successful matches, THEN the trend compares with the newer successful match and the stage passes.

clauses.subject: trend-band
clauses.statement: A trend figure more than 25 percent worse than its baseline annotates the run report and fails no stage.
scenarios: WHEN a trend p95 moves from 40 ms to 52 ms on a matching runner stamp, THEN the report carries a +30 percent annotation and the stage passes.

clauses.subject: runner-stamp
clauses.statement: The run block carries the runner's processor model, processor count and memory limit, and a trend figure compares only against a baseline with the same stamp.

clauses.subject: absolute-threshold
clauses.statement: A threshold is an absolute figure of this system's own measure, and it tightens only through {{assurance.baseline.raise-only}}.

clauses.subject: threshold-cost
clauses.statement: A gate-tier target that rises under `<=`, falls under `>=` or moves under `==` carries a `# cost:` comment above its entry that its entry at `<rev>` lacks, or `contextful-ci measure --since <rev>` raises `MeasureThresholdLoosened`.
clauses.why: because a loosened gate otherwise reads as a changed number, and the cost it accepts goes unrecorded

clauses.subject: history
clauses.statement: A run on the default branch attaches its run report to the measured commit under `refs/notes/measures`, and no verdict reads a note.

clauses.subject: run-report
clauses.statement: `contextful-ci measure-report` writes the note line — commit, run id, attempt, exit code, records and trend annotations — with an integer run id, and reads back every earlier note whatever its run id's JSON type.
clauses.why: because earlier notes on `refs/notes/measures` carry text run ids, and an unreadable note hides every older baseline
scenarios: WHEN the baseline note's run id is the text `contextful-measures_2026-10-14` and the run's is `42`, THEN the report writes `42` and its annotation names that text run id as its baseline.

clauses.subject: measured-basis
clauses.statement: A bound with a measured basis names a trend-tier or scheduled-tier ledger entry id as its benchmark.

clauses.subject: version
clauses.statement: A release tag is `v0.<minor>.<patch>`: `<minor>` counts the milestones computing `closed` in the tagged commit's `spec/status.md` plus each store format major past `1`, and `<patch>` counts the existing tags `v0.<minor>.*`.
scenarios: WHEN milestones 0 to 7 and 11 compute `closed` and `v0.9.0` exists, THEN the computed version is `v0.9.1`.

clauses.subject: store-format
clauses.statement: A commit's store format is the `FormatVersion::CURRENT` constant in its `crates/contextful-core/src/store/lay_out.rs`, and `1.0` where that constant is absent; a constant that does not parse raises `TagStoreFormatUnread`.
scenarios: WHEN 16 milestones compute `closed`, `v0.16.1` declares store format `1.0` and `HEAD` declares `2.0`, THEN the computed version is `v0.17.0` and its message carries `Store format 1.0 → 2.0`.

clauses.subject: annotated
clauses.statement: `contextful-ci tag` creates a signed annotated tag on `HEAD` naming the closed milestones once every refusal of this operation clears, and never moves or replaces an existing tag.

clauses.subject: dirty-tree
clauses.statement: A working tree or index differing from `HEAD` raises `TagTreeDirty`.
clauses.why: because the gate then judges files the tagged commit does not hold

clauses.subject: off-branch
clauses.statement: A `HEAD` unreachable from the default branch, `origin/HEAD` unless `--branch` names another, raises `TagOffDefaultBranch`.

clauses.subject: version-regressed
clauses.statement: A computed version below the highest existing `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` tag raises `TagVersionRegressed`, naming both.
scenarios: WHEN milestone 11 reopens after `v0.9.0`, THEN the computed `v0.8.0` raises `TagVersionRegressed`.

clauses.subject: format-break-patch
clauses.statement: A computed `<minor>` equal to the highest existing tag's, while `HEAD`'s store format major differs from that tag's, raises `TagFormatBreakPatch`, naming both formats.
scenarios: WHEN milestone 11 reopens after `v0.9.0` while the store format moves from `1.0` to `2.0`, THEN the computed `v0.9.1` raises `TagFormatBreakPatch`.

clauses.subject: format-notes
clauses.statement: A tag whose store format major exceeds the highest existing tag's carries the message line `Store format <old> → <new>: upgrade every reader, then every writer together.`
clauses.why: because an older reader refuses a manifest of the newer major, and an older writer refuses the table once a newer writer commits

clauses.subject: workspace-version
clauses.statement: A `[workspace.package]` version in `HEAD`'s `Cargo.toml` that is absent or differs from the computed version raises `TagWorkspaceVersionMismatch`, naming both.

clauses.subject: gate-failed
clauses.statement: Once the other refusals clear, every gate stage runs against `HEAD` with `HEAD~1` as base; a failing stage raises `TagGateFailed`, naming the stage's refusal, and no tag is created.

clauses.subject: release-tag-version
clauses.statement: `contextful-ci release` over a `HEAD` carrying a `v*` tag, none of which equals `v` plus the `[workspace.package]` version, raises `ReleaseTagVersionMismatch`, naming both, before any build.
clauses.why: because a tag cut without `contextful-ci tag` otherwise ships binaries reporting another version

clauses.subject: release-run
clauses.statement: The operator pushes the tag, runs `contextful-ci release` per {{assurance.build.targets}} matrix cell, `contextful-ci formula` over their metadata and `contextful-ci image` per profile, then publishes the GitHub release from that tag.
clauses.why: because every packaging command then reads one tag identity, and each runs on the operator's machine

clauses.subject: suite
clauses.statement: `contextful-conformance --binary <path> --output <report>` executes its versioned scenarios through the supplied artifact's public CLI and HTTP surfaces outside a source checkout.

clauses.subject: credential-isolation
clauses.statement: Every artifact invocation receives an empty inherited environment, an isolated home and scratch directory, a fixed executable search path and explicitly supplied synthetic fixture credentials.
clauses.why: because compatibility evidence requires no provider account or inherited credential

clauses.subject: requirements
clauses.statement: Every required scenario executes its declared capabilities; a missing capability or unsupported storage profile records `unsupported`, names its requirement and refuses consumer activation.
scenarios: WHEN a read-only artifact receives a required replay scenario, THEN evidence names the missing run capability and the suite exits unsuccessfully.

clauses.subject: verdict
clauses.statement: A compatibility verdict passes only when every required scenario reports executed success; a parse, an unsupported requirement or a skipped required scenario supplies no execution pass.
scenarios: WHEN a required scenario is skipped, THEN the aggregate compatibility verdict fails.

clauses.subject: verdict-exit
clauses.statement: `contextful-conformance` exits 1 after writing a failing verdict and 2 without a report; release packaging records a failed `suite-exit` scenario for any other exit, or for exit 1 over a passing report.
clauses.why: because the suite's own failing verdict is evidence, not a crashed process
scenarios: WHEN the suite exits 1 over a report whose required scenarios are `unsupported`, THEN the release report holds those scenarios and no `suite-exit` failure.

clauses.subject: scenarios
clauses.statement: The suite exercises pagination and checkpoints, applied scheduling and dependencies, graceful restart, hard-crash replay, empty and replacement captures, public identifiers, credential masking, typed export acknowledgement and receiver visibility.

clauses.subject: mutation-controls
clauses.statement: Planted cursor skips, duplicate public identities, repeated in-window scheduling and acknowledgement before receiver commit each fail their owning scenario.
clauses.why: because a scenario that accepts its motivating defect proves no compatibility
scenarios: WHEN a native source advances past an unserved page, THEN the pagination scenario fails.

clauses.subject: report
clauses.statement: Evidence records the suite revision and version, supplied binary SHA-256 digest, reported version, feature profile, storage profile and every scenario outcome, requirement and diagnostic.

clauses.subject: command-diagnostic
clauses.statement: A failed or timed-out artifact command's diagnostic, a scenario step's included, names its verb and the first error identifier its stderr carries; no other stderr text enters the report.
clauses.why: because a provider failure must name its cause while stderr may carry binding credentials
scenarios: WHEN a command fails with a credential in its stderr, THEN the diagnostic names the verb and error identifier, and the report omits the credential.

clauses.subject: provenance
clauses.statement: Unknown source correspondence remains null; a reported version or successful scenario never supplies a source commit.
clauses.why: because source correspondence requires evidence beyond behavior and a version string
scenarios: WHEN a binary reports a version without source evidence, THEN source correspondence remains null.

clauses.subject: artifact-stability
clauses.statement: The suite verifies the supplied artifact's digest before and after execution; changed bytes refuse a compatibility verdict.

clauses.subject: release-distribution
clauses.statement: Each release archive carries the matching-target suite and compatibility report whatever its verdict; release metadata names the report, binary digest and verdict, preserving failed and skipped outcomes.
clauses.why: because a profile lacking a scenario's capability never passes, and refusing its cell withholds the evidence stating so

clauses.subject: release-notes
clauses.statement: `contextful-ci formula` writes `release-notes.md` stating every cell's local and `cloudflare-d1` verdict, and fails on a cell carrying none; the operator publishes it as the GitHub release body.
clauses.why: because a failing verdict ships, so the release page states it beside the archives

clauses.subject: foreign-target
clauses.statement: A release target unavailable to its packaging host records explicit skipped scenarios with a target diagnostic; its report supplies no execution pass.
clauses.why: because a cross compilation cannot demonstrate the produced artifact's behavior

clauses.subject: storage-profile
clauses.statement: The local profile uses isolated filesystem state; `postgres` uses synthetic PostgreSQL and signed S3 services. An unavailable fixture records its named requirement through {{assurance.consumer.requirements}}.

clauses.subject: d1-profile
clauses.statement: A `cloudflare-d1` verdict runs the supplied `contextful-full` artifact against D1 and R2 bindings, replaces its local disk, and records every required outcome independently of the local and PostgreSQL profiles.

clauses.subject: d1-admission
clauses.statement: A `cloudflare-d1` suite holds a lease row in the bound D1 from before its first reset until it ends, lapsing 120 s after its last renewal; a suite meeting a live lease refuses each required scenario with `ConformanceAlreadyRunning`.
clauses.why: because a process check inside one container misses a suite another container runs against the same database

clauses.subject: d1-release
clauses.statement: Release evidence binds a `cloudflare-d1` report to the artifact digest, source revision, suite revision and storage profile; a required failure, unsupported case, skip or unverified binding supplies no compatibility verdict.

clauses.subject: d1-absent
clauses.statement: A native `contextful-full` release cell without `CONTEXTFUL_CONFORMANCE_D1_ENDPOINT` runs no `cloudflare-d1` pass; its report records binding origin `absent` and every required scenario skipped with `ConformanceBindingAbsent`.
clauses.why: because a release container holds no D1 binding, and the deployment run against D1 and R2 supplies that verdict
scenarios: WHEN a native full cell packages without a D1 endpoint, THEN the suite runs once, for `local`.

clauses.subject: d1-deployment
clauses.statement: Deployment readiness requires a replacement run against Cloudflare D1 and R2, with the same artifact digest and source revision as its release report.

ledes.assurance.audit-assumptions: The assumption allowlist, the transitive footprint audit over the elaborated environment, the inventory and the report.
ledes.assurance.automate: Typed subcommands over compiled binaries, and the boundary shell keeps.
ledes.assurance.backtest: Historical evaluations, called backtests: bounded cases, model-knowledge controls, label intervals and splits, execution metadata, planted leaks and replayable trajectories. Financial return-series and execution profiles are consumer-selected applications of this flow ({{topology.bound-application.domain-neutral}}).
ledes.assurance.baseline: Holding a run against committed baselines and absolute floors, intervals, golden custody and case generation.
ledes.assurance.build: Target directories, the engine-linked invocation, linked query functions, build targets, release artifacts and the dependency allowlist.
ledes.assurance.consumer: Artifact compatibility: source-independent execution, required capabilities, scenario evidence, storage profiles and release distribution.
ledes.assurance.differential-test: The executable reference models, the case generators, the minimized counterexample corpus and the command running them.
ledes.assurance.evaluate: The read-path quality harness: case format, deterministic metrics and floors, judged dimensions, the reader and the judge.
ledes.assurance.forecast: Probability forecasts over consumer-declared outcomes: freeze instant, settlement, lead time, imputation, coverage, reference baselines and separate scoring tracks. Prediction-market baselines belong to an explicitly selected profile ({{topology.bound-application.domain-neutral}}).
ledes.assurance.gate: Stage order, secrets of record, the crate-graph, row-token, egress and dependency rules, the formal stage, the container's ceilings, disk, footprint budgets and surface checks.
ledes.assurance.measure: The target ledger: each tracked target, the clause it serves, how it is measured and its record per commit.
ledes.assurance.model: The Lean policy package and the Lean protocol state machine, their pins, and the definitions theorems and checks range over.
ledes.assurance.prove: The theorem inventory: layer composition, placement, the evidence floor, the proof targets over the authority mapping, and the mediation relation over statement execution.
ledes.assurance.recheck: Rebuilding and re-auditing from pinned source in a credential-free environment.
ledes.assurance.release: The release tag's version, the refusals guarding it, the signed annotated tag `contextful-ci tag` creates, and the local packaging the operator runs from it.
ledes.assurance.scope-claim: The sentence the assurance claim is allowed to be: named decisions, trusted dependencies, translation chain, refinement reach.
ledes.assurance.structure-tree: One home per capability, the one enforcement decision module, adapters, mirror annotations and derived-artifact checks.
ledes.assurance.test: Assertion construction, guard validation, suite placement, test-first and acceptance tests, and the connector test kit.
ledes.authority.attenuate: Deriving a narrower child offline, and the narrowing legality of each grant dimension.
ledes.authority.bound-redistribution: The per-table licence bound applied at push, the root-object allowlist, and the per-credential edge filter.
ledes.authority.compose: The three layers as one reference monitor, and the order a registered relation applies.
ledes.authority.exchange: Exchanging a verified external assertion for a scoped credential under injected verifying material and a declared policy.
ledes.authority.filter-rows: The typed row-predicate grammar, subject binding, the tenant equality and the project default.
ledes.authority.grant: What a credential says a holder does: actions, table patterns, tenant scope, the template allowlist, ceilings, and resources answering by name.
ledes.authority.identify: The subject tuple, its per-member attestation, hygiene at the mint, and the identity links connecting a subject to a source's principals.
ledes.authority.issue: Minting: the persisted lifetime ceiling, the principal a row-landing grant needs, signing custody, and the authoring posture.
ledes.authority.mask: Column classes, strategies and combines, guardrails over an exhaustible value space, the pepper, and masked behavior under caller SQL.
ledes.authority.place: Inference zones: grammar, composition across grains, floors, incognito, and the serve-time outcome.
ledes.authority.profile: The versioned delegation profile over the attenuable-credential library: admitted elements, reserved facts, the bounded evaluator, the scoped session.
ledes.authority.redact: Removal and transformation inside the writer, ahead of columnar bytes and the run path's durable record.
ledes.authority.refuse: The two shapes an unauthorized read takes, the scope guard, and what a refusal discloses.
ledes.authority.resist: The paths that stay closed to an injected instruction.
ledes.authority.revoke: Ending a credential's usefulness ahead of expiry: short lifetimes, the denylist, the scoped epoch, key rotation, format withdrawal.
ledes.authority.verify: Admission at a checkpoint: signatures, audience, timestamps, possession proof, key sets, and the admitted-authority value.
ledes.connector.attach: Host handling of outbound requests: network transport, permitted hosts and addresses, credential headers, redirects and URL scrubbing.
ledes.connector.declare-capability: Manifest-declared host access and the probe that checks a bound credential's granted scopes.
ledes.connector.drive-changes: Change cursors and complete listings of a selected Drive corpus.
ledes.connector.drive-domain-auth: Organization-approved Drive access and the principal whose authority each request carries.
ledes.connector.drive-picks: Files a principal selects through Picker, the selection position, and the rows a tenant connection stores.
ledes.connector.drive-sheet: Google Sheets capture as structured rows, separate from PDF page capture.
ledes.connector.export: Connector interfaces: shared types, source and destination worlds, optional interfaces and compiled-in sources.
ledes.connector.import: Host imports and the configuration table the host forwards to a guest.
ledes.connector.infer: Model requests: endpoint selection, prompt data markers and output provenance labels.
ledes.connector.lease: The first credential adapter: lease declarations, mint requests, expiry, failures and the mint credential.
ledes.connector.meter: Vendor quota declarations, limiter bindings, pre-send checks, permit reservations, denials and usage reports.
ledes.connector.package: Distribution form, digest pinning, per-connector resource bounds and world versioning.
ledes.connector.principal-secrets: Per-principal credential names and the adapter that serves their material.
ledes.connector.record: Optional operator metadata, provider observations, the inventory of configured bindings, and the provider attribution a run emits.
ledes.connector.reference: Outbound credential references, the `secret://` scheme and value templates.
ledes.connector.resolve: The provider interface, adapter order, request-time resolution, credential buffers and deployment security configurations.
ledes.connector.source: The declared behavior of each source compiled into the engine.
ledes.connector.widen: Comparison of a candidate connector manifest with its admitted predecessor, and operator approval of additional host access.
ledes.corpus.address: The three segments of a clause id and what makes each legal.
ledes.corpus.anatomy: The section order of a contract file, the lede and clause list of each operation, and the computed kind of a clause.
ledes.corpus.diagram: The fenced diagram, and the shape every flowchart, sequence and state diagram keeps so a reader sees the parts and what flows between them.
ledes.corpus.guide: A non-normative teaching page per contract, and what keeps it from becoming a second home for a rule.
ledes.corpus.rationale: Where an argument lives: the Why line, the record and its anatomy, and the words a contract file cannot carry.
ledes.corpus.reference: The one legal way a statement reaches a fact another clause owns, and the ban on restatement and literature.
ledes.corpus.registry: Where a spelling is registered, the single owner of an error or a bound, and the collision test.
ledes.corpus.render: The generated files, and the vocabulary no authored file carries.
ledes.corpus.state: Pins, verdicts, the coverage floor, the roadmap's operation claims and each milestone's acceptance test.
ledes.corpus.targets: Per-provider deployment target files, the roles each shape fills, and the page rendered from them.
ledes.disclosure.attest: Chain verification, signed segment roots, lineage attestations, and the reach of each guarantee.
ledes.disclosure.bound-cohort: The line between a per-person table and a cohort table, and the floor a cohort read carries.
ledes.disclosure.bound-staleness: The declared age budget on mirrored authorization, the refusal past it, and the one narrowing posture.
ledes.disclosure.declare-fidelity: The fidelity level a table claims, the source family bounding the claim, and live federation under a reader's delegated credential.
ledes.disclosure.drive-sweep: Mapping Drive file permissions into the governed source's visibility rows.
ledes.disclosure.erase: The one erasure verb: subject tombstones, the bounded provenance cascade, the restaging gate, and the tenant rewrite.
ledes.disclosure.explain: The access decision and its path, replay over a window with its coverage, and the audience report.
ledes.disclosure.mirror: The three-way conjunction, the access tables as store data, and the binding that compiles a table's semi-join.

ledes.surface.fire: Job declaration, the closed kind union, same-tick order, the fire watermark, and one-shot evaluation.
